a.a-buffer.summary: A hidden-surface method that accumulates, for each pixel, a list of the fragments covering it together with subpixel coverage bitmasks and depths, and then composites them. It extends the Z-buffer to handle anti-aliasing and transparent surfaces.
a.a-star.summary: A best-first search that expands vertices in order of the sum of the cost from the start, g, and an admissible heuristic estimate of the cost to the goal, h.
a.a3c.summary: A deep reinforcement-learning algorithm in which multiple actor-learner threads asynchronously compute advantage actor-critic gradients in their own copies of the environment and update shared parameters. It stabilizes training without a replay buffer.
a.aa-tree.summary: A red-black tree variant that simplifies implementation by allowing red nodes only as right children.
a.abp-deque.summary: A non-blocking work-stealing deque in which the owner thread pushes and pops at the bottom without locks while thief threads take from the top with compare-and-swap (CAS). It keeps the performance guarantees of work-stealing scheduling in multiprogrammed environments.
a.abstract-interpretation.summary: A theory of static analysis that approximates program semantics in an abstract domain on a lattice and computes fixed points with abstract operations and widening, yielding properties that are sound for all executions.
a.actor-critic.summary: A reinforcement-learning architecture that jointly learns an actor (the policy), which selects actions, and a critic, which estimates state values, reinforcing the actor with the critic's temporal-difference error.
a.adaboost.summary: A boosting method that combines weak classifiers sequentially, increasing the weights of the samples misclassified by the previous weak classifier.
a.adafactor.summary: An adaptive optimizer that stores the second-moment matrix in factored form through its row and column sums. This makes its memory cost sublinear in the number of parameters.
a.adagrad.summary: An adaptive learning-rate method that divides the learning rate by each coordinate's accumulated sum of squared gradients, giving larger updates to rarely occurring features.
a.adam.summary: An adaptive optimizer that sets per-coordinate step sizes from bias-corrected exponential moving averages of the first and second moments of the gradient.
a.adamw.summary: A fix to Adam that decouples weight decay from the adaptive gradient update so that it behaves differently from L2 regularization.
a.adaptive-huffman.o2.note: Presented an improved implementation of Gallager's method; it is the K in the name FGK.
a.adaptive-huffman.summary: A one-pass form of Huffman coding that updates symbol counts and the Huffman tree after each input symbol. It repairs the tree incrementally by swapping nodes so that the sibling property is preserved.
a.adaptive-metropolis.summary: A random-walk Metropolis method that continually updates its Gaussian proposal using the covariance estimated from the sample path so far. Although the chain is no longer Markovian, it is proven to have the correct ergodic properties.
a.adaptive-radix-tree.summary: A main-memory index based on a byte-wise radix tree whose nodes switch among four sizes (4, 16, 48 and 256 children) according to their fan-out, combined with path compression. It reduces space while keeping keys in sorted order for range scans.
a.adaptive-simpson.summary: An adaptive numerical integration method that estimates the error from the difference between Simpson's rule on an interval and on its two halves, recursively subdividing only where needed.
a.additive-attention.summary: An attention mechanism that, at each decoder step, learns alignment weights over the encoder hidden states to form a context vector.
a.adler-32.o0.note: The algorithm was designed by Mark Adler and defined in RFC 1950 as part of the zlib format.
a.adler-32.summary: A 32-bit checksum that keeps the byte sum A and the running sum B of A, each modulo the prime 65521, and outputs B·65536+A. Defined in the zlib format as an extension of Fletcher's checksum.
a.admm.summary: A method for separable convex optimization that alternately minimizes the augmented Lagrangian over blocks of variables and then updates the dual variable. It is used in distributed optimization and sparse model estimation.
a.adpcm.summary: A waveform coding method that quantizes the difference between each sample and a prediction from previous samples, adapting the quantizer step size to the signal level. It is used in speech and audio codecs such as IMA ADPCM and G.726.
a.aes.summary: A substitution–permutation network block cipher with a 128-bit block and 128/192/256-bit keys. It was adopted as a US federal standard in 2001.
a.affine-invariant-ensemble-sampler.summ: An MCMC method in which each walker of an ensemble is moved by a stretch move along the line toward another walker, making performance invariant under affine transformations of the target distribution. The Python package emcee implements it.
a.affinity-propagation.summary: A clustering method in which data points repeatedly exchange 'responsibility' and 'availability' messages to choose exemplars and clusters jointly. The number of clusters is not fixed in advance.
a.aho-corasick.summary: An algorithm that finds multiple patterns in a single pass over the text using an automaton formed by adding failure links to a trie of the pattern set.
a.aimd.summary: A control rule that adds a fixed amount to the sending rate when there is no congestion and multiplies it by a fixed factor below one on a congestion signal. The analysis showed that multiple users converge to an efficient and fair allocation.
a.akl-toussaint.summary: Method that discards, before the hull computation, every point lying inside the polygon spanned by the extreme points in several directions. It serves as a linear-time preprocessing step for convex hull algorithms.
a.aks-primality.summary: A deterministic primality test that checks the polynomial congruence (X+a)^n ≡ X^n+a (mod X^r−1, n). It was the first to show that primality can be decided deterministically in polynomial time.
a.aks-sorting-network.summary: A sorting network that sorts n inputs with depth O(log n) and O(n log n) comparators. It is asymptotically optimal, but its constants are so large that it is not used in practice.
a.alexnet.summary: A deep convolutional neural network that combined ReLU, dropout, and GPU training to win ImageNet 2012 by a large margin.
a.alias-method.summary: A sampling method that converts a discrete distribution over n outcomes into a probability table and an alias table, picks a cell uniformly and returns either its own value or its alias after one comparison. After the tables are built each sample takes O(1) time.
a.alibi.summary: A method that, instead of position embeddings, adds to attention scores a negative bias proportional to the query–key distance with a fixed slope per head. It allows extrapolation to inputs longer than those seen in training.
a.all-star.summary: Adaptive LL parsing that, at each decision point, runs a subparser per alternative on the actual input to look ahead only as far as needed and caches the results as a DFA. It handles any context-free grammar without left recursion and is used by ANTLR 4.
a.aloha.summary: A multiple-access scheme in which terminals send packets on a shared radio channel at any time and, when no acknowledgment arrives because of a collision, retransmit after a random delay.
a.alpha-beta.o0.note: Correctness and efficiency analyzed by Knuth and Moore (1975)
a.alpha-beta.summary: A technique that obtains the same result as minimax with less search by pruning branches outside the current best-value window (α, β).
a.alpha-shapes.summary: Generalization of the convex hull that describes the shape of a point set by connecting with segments the boundary points of the α-hull, which is defined by disks of radius 1/α. It is computed from the Voronoi diagram (Delaunay triangulation) in O(n log n) time.
a.alphazero.summary: A game-learning algorithm that, through self-play alone and with no domain knowledge beyond the rules, alternates Monte Carlo tree search guided by a neural network's policy and value outputs with training the network on the search results. The same method was applied to chess, shogi and Go.
a.alt-godau-frechet.summary: Algorithm that decides in O(mn) time whether the Fréchet distance between two polylines is at most ε by checking for a monotone path in the free-space diagram, and combines this decision procedure with a search to compute the Fréchet distance.
a.alt.summary: A point-to-point shortest-path technique that precomputes distances to a small set of landmarks and uses the triangle inequality to derive lower bounds on the remaining distance as the heuristic for A* search. The name stands for A*, Landmarks, and Triangle inequality.
a.amanatides-woo.summary: An algorithm that visits, in order, every voxel that a ray passes through in a uniform grid by incrementally updating the parametric distance to the next cell boundary along each axis. Needing only a few comparisons and additions per cell, it is used in grid-based ray tracing and voxel rendering.
a.american-flag-sort.summary: An MSD radix sort that counts digit frequencies to fix the bucket boundaries and then moves elements into their buckets in place by cyclic swaps, without an auxiliary array.
a.ans.summary: An entropy coding method that accumulates symbols into a single integer state according to their probabilities, achieving arithmetic-coding-level compression at Huffman-level speed.
a.antimirov-derivatives.summary: A method that computes the result of a Brzozowski derivative as a set of regular expressions instead of a single expression. Because the number of distinct partial derivatives is at most the number of symbol occurrences plus one, using them as states yields a small NFA.
a.apostolico-giancarlo.summary: A Boyer–Moore variant that records, for each text position, the match length already established by earlier comparisons so that no text character is compared again. The number of character comparisons is bounded by about 2n in the worst case.
a.apriori.summary: An algorithm for frequent itemsets and association rules that grows candidates level by level, generating length-(k+1) candidates from frequent length-k itemsets and pruning with the property that every subset of a frequent itemset is frequent.
a.arc.summary: A cache replacement algorithm that keeps a list of pages seen once recently, a list of pages seen at least twice, and ghost lists of pages evicted from each, and self-tunes the split between the two lists according to ghost-list hits. It is used in ZFS.
a.argon2.summary: A password hash built on a BLAKE2b-based memory-hard function that raises the cost of GPU and ASIC attacks. It is the winner of the Password Hashing Competition.
a.aria.summary: A 128-bit block cipher developed in Korea and adopted as a Korean national standard. It is an SPN like AES but uses an involutory diffusion layer, so encryption and decryption share almost the same circuit.
a.aries.summary: A transaction recovery algorithm based on write-ahead logging (WAL) and log sequence numbers that restores a database after a failure through analysis, redo and undo passes. It repeats history during redo and logs undo actions as compensation log records.
a.arithmetic-coding.summary: A coding method that narrows the entire message down to a single real subinterval of [0,1), approaching the entropy without the constraint of an integer number of bits per symbol.
a.armijo-line-search.summary: A line-search rule that shrinks the step size by a constant factor until a sufficient-decrease condition on the objective along the search direction is met. It is used to choose step lengths in gradient descent and Newton-type methods.
a.arnoldi-iteration.summary: An iterative method that builds an orthonormal basis of a Krylov subspace and a Hessenberg matrix for a general (nonsymmetric) matrix. It underlies nonsymmetric eigenvalue solvers and GMRES.
a.ascon.summary: A family of lightweight authenticated ciphers and hash functions built on a duplex sponge with a 320-bit permutation. It was the first choice for lightweight applications in the CAESAR portfolio and was selected by NIST as its lightweight cryptography standard.
a.auction-algorithm.summary: An algorithm for the assignment problem in which each person bids for the object offering the largest net value by raising its price, and objects go to the highest bidders. It maintains ε-complementary slackness, yields an optimal solution for integer costs when ε is small enough, and was designed with distributed computation in mind.
a.augmented-lagrangian.summary: A method for constrained optimization that repeatedly minimizes the Lagrangian augmented with a quadratic penalty on constraint violation and then updates the multipliers. It converges without driving the penalty parameter to infinity.
a.avl-tree.summary: The first self-balancing binary search tree, which keeps the height difference between the two subtrees of every node at most 1.
a.b-epsilon-tree.summary: An external-memory dictionary that gives B-tree nodes a buffer and reduces their fan-out to B^ε, so that writes accumulate in buffers and are flushed downward in batches. The parameter ε trades insertion cost against query cost, and the design is used in write-optimized storage engines.
a.b-link-tree.summary: A concurrent B-tree variant that adds to every node a link to its right sibling and a high key. A search that meets a node being split can follow the link, so searches need no locks and insertions lock only a small number of nodes.
a.b-tree.o0.note: First released as a 1970 Boeing research laboratory report
a.b-tree.summary: A balanced multiway search tree that keeps its height low by storing multiple keys and children in each node. It is the standard for disk-based indexes.
a.baby-step-giant-step.summary: A time–memory trade-off algorithm for discrete logarithms that stores baby steps g^j in a table with m ≈ √n and matches giant steps h·g^(−im) against it. Both time and space are O(√n).
a.backpropagation.o0.note: First description of reverse-mode automatic differentiation
a.backpropagation.o0.venue: University of Helsinki master's thesis (in Finnish)
a.backpropagation.summary: A method that applies the chain rule from the output layer toward the input layer to compute the gradients of all weights in a neural network in a single backward pass.
a.bacon-rajan-cycle-collection.summary: A cycle-collection algorithm for reference-counted systems that gathers objects whose count was decremented to a nonzero value as candidate roots and finds cyclic garbage by trial deletion, tentatively subtracting internal references from the candidates. A concurrent version is presented as well.
a.bagging.summary: An ensemble method that reduces variance by training a model on each bootstrap sample and combining their predictions by averaging or voting.
a.baillie-psw.summary: A primality test that requires a number to pass both a base-2 strong probable-prime test and a strong Lucas probable-prime test. No composite passing it is known, and several libraries use it as their default test.
a.baker-gc.summary: A real-time garbage collection algorithm that interleaves copying collection with program execution in small increments and bounds pause times by copying an object immediately in a read barrier whenever the program touches one not yet moved.
a.bankers-algorithm.o0.note: The Banker's Algorithm appears in Section 6, 'The Problem of the Deadly Embrace', of this manuscript; Dijkstra also wrote a Dutch manuscript on the topic, EWD108.
a.bankers-algorithm.summary: A deadlock-avoidance algorithm that, on each resource request, checks whether granting it leaves the system in a safe state in which every process can still run to completion, and grants the request only if so.
a.barnes-hut-t-sne.summary: A t-SNE variant that approximates the input similarities with sparse nearest neighbors and the repulsive gradient terms with a Barnes–Hut space-partitioning tree, reducing the cost to O(N log N).
a.barrett-reduction.summary: A technique that precomputes μ = ⌊b^(2k)/N⌋ for a fixed modulus N and approximates the quotient with multiplications and shifts to compute x mod N. It obtains the remainder with a few correcting subtractions and no division instruction.
a.batagelj-zaversnik-cores.summary: An algorithm that computes the core number (k-core membership) of every vertex in O(m) time by placing vertices in degree buckets, removing minimum-degree vertices first and updating the degrees of their neighbours.
a.batch-norm.summary: A technique that stabilizes training by normalizing layer inputs with minibatch statistics and then applying a learnable scale and shift.
a.baum-welch.summary: A maximum-likelihood algorithm that iteratively estimates the parameters of a hidden Markov model using forward and backward probabilities.
a.bbhash.summary: A minimal perfect hashing method that hashes keys into a bit array, fixes the positions of keys that did not collide and passes colliding keys on to the next level, repeating until all keys are placed. It parallelizes easily and was designed for massive key sets.
a.bbr.summary: A congestion control that, instead of reacting to loss, models the path from the measured bottleneck bandwidth and minimum RTT and paces sending rate and inflight data to match their product (the BDP).
a.bch-code.summary: A cyclic code whose generator polynomial is designed to have consecutive powers of a finite-field element as roots, so that it can correct a chosen number of errors.
a.bcjr.summary: A MAP decoding algorithm that computes the a posteriori probability of each bit with forward and backward recursions on a trellis, minimizing the symbol error rate. It serves as the component decoder of turbo codes.
a.bcrypt.summary: A password hash that slows brute-force attacks by repeating the Blowfish key setup a number of times set by a cost factor (Eksblowfish).
a.bdf.summary: An implicit linear multistep method that requires the derivative of the polynomial interpolating past solution values to satisfy the differential equation at the current time. It is the standard approach for stiff ordinary differential equations.
a.belady-min.summary: A replacement algorithm that evicts the page that will not be used for the longest time in the future. It requires knowledge of future references and cannot be implemented online, but it minimizes page faults and serves as the baseline for other policies.
a.belief-propagation.summary: An inference algorithm in which the nodes of a graphical model pass messages to their neighbors to compute marginal probabilities. It is exact on trees and is used as an approximation (loopy BP) on graphs with cycles.
a.bellman-ford.summary: An algorithm that relaxes every edge V−1 times to compute single-source shortest paths with negative weights allowed, and detects negative cycles.
a.bender-farach-colton-lca.summary: An algorithm that reduces LCA to range-minimum queries on an Euler tour whose adjacent values differ by ±1, then uses block decomposition, a sparse table and precomputed tables for small blocks to obtain linear preprocessing and constant-time queries. It is simpler to implement than earlier methods.
a.bentley-mcilroy-partitioning.summary: A three-way partitioning scheme for quicksort that gathers keys equal to the pivot at both ends of the array during partitioning and swaps them into the middle afterwards. The qsort built on it is used in BSD-derived C libraries.
a.bentley-mcilroy.summary: A compression preprocessing method that records a fingerprint (hash) of each fixed-size block of the input and replaces long strings repeated far apart with references to their earlier occurrence. It removes long repetitions that lie outside the window of ordinary compressors.
a.bentley-ottmann.summary: An algorithm that reports all k intersection points among line segments in O((n + k) log n) using a sweep line and an event queue.
a.berlekamp-factorization.summary: A deterministic algorithm that factors a square-free polynomial f over a finite field by computing the null space of the matrix Q−I derived from the Frobenius map and taking gcds of f with its elements. It is efficient over finite fields of small characteristic.
a.berlekamp-massey.summary: An algorithm that iteratively finds the shortest linear feedback shift register (LFSR) generating a given sequence. In BCH and Reed–Solomon decoding it computes the error-locator polynomial from the syndromes in O(n²) time.
a.bert.summary: A bidirectional representation model that pretrains a Transformer encoder with masked language modeling and next sentence prediction.
a.bezier-curve.o0.title: Citroën internal technical report
a.bezier-curve.o1.title: Renault UNISURF surface design system
a.bezier-curve.summary: A method for defining and evaluating smooth curves by repeated linear interpolation of control points. It was devised independently in automobile body design.
a.bfgs.summary: A quasi-Newton optimization method that updates a Hessian approximation with a rank-two correction from gradient differences and steps. Published independently by four authors in 1970, it is a default method in nonlinear optimization libraries.
a.bfs.o0.title: Connected-component search in the Plankalkül dissertation manuscript
a.bfs.summary: A graph traversal that uses a queue to visit vertices in order of their distance from the start vertex. It finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs.
a.bfv.o1.note: It ports Brakerski's LWE-based scheme to Ring-LWE; the two papers together give the scheme its name BFV.
a.bfv.summary: A Ring-LWE-based homomorphic encryption scheme that manages noise without modulus switching by placing the plaintext in the high-order bits of the ciphertext (scale invariance). It supports modular integer arithmetic and is implemented in Microsoft SEAL and OpenFHE.
a.bgp.summary: A path-vector routing protocol that exchanges, between autonomous systems, reachability information together with the list of autonomous systems to be traversed (the AS path). The AS path prevents loops and routes are chosen by policy.
a.bgv.summary: A leveled fully homomorphic encryption scheme based on LWE or Ring-LWE that uses modulus switching to curb noise growth after multiplication. It evaluates circuits of a preset depth without bootstrapping and is implemented for integer arithmetic in HElib and OpenFHE.
a.bic-tcp.summary: A TCP congestion control for fast long-distance networks that grows the window toward the size just before the last loss in a binary-search manner, increasing quickly when far from the target and slowly when close to it.
a.bicgstab.summary: An iterative method for nonsymmetric linear systems that adds a local residual-minimizing step to the biconjugate gradient method (Bi-CG) to smooth its convergence.
a.bidirectional-path-tracing.summary: A Monte Carlo rendering method that generates subpaths from both the camera and the light sources and connects their vertices to form light paths of various lengths. It has lower variance than unidirectional path tracing in scenes dominated by indirect light.
a.bidirectional-rnn.summary: A recurrent network with two hidden layers that process the sequence forward and backward, both connected to the same output layer. Each time step can use both past and future context.
a.bidirectional-search.summary: A point-to-point search technique that alternates a forward search from the source with a backward search from the target and determines the shortest path once the two searches meet. Bidirectional Dijkstra is its standard form and serves as the basic query scheme of many road-network routing techniques.
a.bilateral-filter.summary: A nonlinear filter that averages neighboring pixels using the product of a spatial Gaussian weight and a Gaussian weight on intensity (color) difference. It smooths noise while preserving edges.
a.binary-exponential-backoff.summary: A retransmission rule that doubles the range from which the random retransmission delay is drawn after each successive collision. It was named in the Ethernet paper of Metcalfe and Boggs and became the retransmission rule of CSMA/CD.
a.binary-fuse-filter.summary: A static approximate membership filter that improves on the construction of xor filters, bringing storage within 13% of the lower bound and speeding up construction.
a.binary-gcd.summary: An algorithm that computes the greatest common divisor of two integers using only shifts (division by 2), subtraction and comparison instead of division. It strips common factors of two and then repeatedly subtracts odd values.
a.binary-heap.summary: A priority queue that stores a complete binary tree in an array and keeps every parent greater than or equal to its children.
a.binary-insertion-sort.o0.title: Mention of binary insertion in the Moore School Lectures
a.binary-insertion-sort.o0.venue: Cited as the origin in Knuth, TAOCP Vol. 3
a.binary-insertion-sort.summary: An insertion sort that finds the insertion position by binary search, reducing the number of comparisons to O(n log n).
a.binary-search.o0.note: The form that works for all n is due to D. H. Lehmer (1960)
a.binary-search.o0.title: Mention of binary search in the Moore School Lectures
a.binary-search.o0.venue: Cited as the origin in Knuth, TAOCP Vol. 3 §6.2.1
a.binary-search.summary: A search that halves the search interval of a sorted array at each step, finding an element in O(log n).
a.binomial-heap.summary: A data structure that represents a priority queue as a forest of binomial trees, supporting the merging of two heaps in O(log n).
a.birch.summary: A clustering algorithm for very large data that scans the data once, accumulating clustering-feature (CF) summaries in a height-balanced CF tree, and then clusters those summaries. It works incrementally within a memory budget.
a.bitonic-sort.summary: A sorting network that repeatedly merges bitonic sequences. Its comparison order is independent of the input, making it well suited to parallel hardware.
a.bk-tree.summary: A metric-space tree for discrete-valued distance functions that stores elements with each child edge labeled by its distance from the parent. It prunes branches using the triangle inequality and is used for tasks such as similar-word search under edit distance.
a.bkd-tree.summary: A dynamic external-memory k-d tree that maintains a set of static k-d trees whose sizes grow in powers of two and merges them logarithmically on insertion. It keeps high space utilization and fast bulk insertion, and is used for numeric and geographic point indexing in Lucene.
a.blake.summary: A hash that uses the ChaCha core operation as its compression function. It was a finalist in the SHA-3 competition.
a.blake2.summary: A hash that reduces the number of rounds in BLAKE and adds a parameter block, making it faster than MD5.
a.blake3.summary: A hash and XOF that parallelizes the BLAKE2s compression function in a Merkle tree mode.
a.blast.summary: A heuristic for searching large sequence databases that approximates local alignment by extending short word matches used as seeds.
a.blat.summary: A sequence alignment method that keeps an in-memory index of non-overlapping k-mers of the reference genome and extends clustered query k-mer hits into alignments. It quickly finds alignments spanning introns when mapping mRNA to a genome.
a.blind-signature.summary: A scheme in which the requester blinds a message with a random factor, has it signed, and then removes the blinding to obtain a valid signature. The signer cannot see what it signed, enabling anonymous electronic cash and electronic voting.
a.blinn-phong.summary: An illumination model that approximates specular reflection using the halfway vector instead of the Phong model's reflection vector. It was the default lighting in fixed-function GPU pipelines.
a.block-sort.summary: A merge sort built on stable in-place merging that splits ranges into blocks, rotates and swaps them, and uses part of the array as an internal buffer. It sorts stably in O(n log n) time with O(1) extra memory.
a.blocked-bloom-filter.summary: A Bloom filter variant that places all bits for an element within a single cache-line-sized block. It reduces each query to one cache miss at the cost of a slightly higher false-positive rate for the same space.
a.blockquicksort.summary: A quicksort whose partitioning step first records comparison results in block-sized buffers and then performs the swaps in bulk, reducing branch mispredictions.
a.bloom-filter.summary: A probabilistic data structure that marks a bit array with multiple hashes to test set membership with no false negatives and a tolerated rate of false positives.
a.blossom-v.summary: An implementation of a minimum-cost perfect matching algorithm based on Edmonds' blossom method. It grows multiple alternating trees simultaneously, updates dual variables separately for each tree, and manages edges with priority queues.
a.blowfish.summary: A Feistel cipher with a 64-bit block that uses key-dependent S-boxes. Its key setup is deliberately expensive.
a.bls-signature.summary: A short digital signature using a bilinear pairing on elliptic curves, in which a signature is a single curve point. Signatures can be aggregated into one, so it is used in places such as Ethereum's consensus layer.
a.bluestein-fft.summary: An algorithm that computes a DFT of arbitrary length with power-of-two FFTs by recasting it as a convolution with a chirp signal.
a.blum-blum-shub.summary: A pseudorandom number generator that repeatedly squares x modulo a Blum integer N and outputs low-order bits. Predicting the next bit is provably as hard as the quadratic residuosity problem.
a.bm3d.summary: Denoising that groups similar blocks into 3-D arrays, shrinks them in a 3-D transform domain (collaborative filtering), and aggregates the results. It consists of a hard-thresholding stage followed by a Wiener-filtering stage.
a.bndm.summary: A string search algorithm that reads each text window from right to left while simulating, with bit parallelism, the nondeterministic suffix automaton of the reversed pattern. It uses the positions where prefixes of the pattern are recognized to make long shifts.
a.boehm-gc.summary: A conservative mark-sweep garbage collector that, without type information from the compiler, treats every word in the stack, registers and heap that looks like a pointer as a pointer while marking. It is used for C and C++ programs.
a.bogacki-shampine.summary: An embedded Runge–Kutta 3(2) pair that computes third- and second-order solutions together to control the step size. It reuses the last stage as the first stage of the next step (FSAL) and is used in MATLAB's ode23 and SciPy's RK23.
a.boids.summary: A distributed behavioral model that reproduces flocking behavior with only three rules: separation, alignment, and cohesion.
a.boltzmann-machine.summary: A generative network of symmetrically connected stochastic units, including hidden units. Weights are learned from the difference between pairwise unit correlations under the data and under the model's equilibrium distribution.
a.booth-multiplication.summary: An algorithm for signed binary multiplication that examines adjacent pairs of bits of a two's-complement multiplier to decide whether to add, subtract or skip the multiplicand. A run of consecutive ones is handled with one subtraction and one addition.
a.booth-rotation.summary: An algorithm that finds, in linear time, the starting position of the lexicographically smallest of all cyclic rotations of a string by adapting the KMP failure function. It is used to compute canonical forms of circular strings.
a.boruvka.summary: The first minimum spanning tree algorithm, which merges components by simultaneously adding the cheapest outgoing edge of each component.
a.bose-nelson.summary: A construction for sorting networks that splits the inputs in two, sorts each half recursively and joins them with a recursive merging network. It is used to generate fixed networks for small input sizes.
a.boundary-package-merge.summary: A variant of the package-merge algorithm that keeps only boundary information for each level instead of storing every package, computing optimal length-limited prefix codes in O(nL) time and O(L²) space. It is used, for example in Zopfli, to build length-limited Huffman codes for DEFLATE.
a.bowtie.summary: A method for aligning short DNA reads by quality-aware backtracking search on the Burrows–Wheeler transform and FM index of the reference genome. It uses a forward index and a mirror index together to curb excessive backtracking.
a.bowyer-watson.summary: A Delaunay triangulation algorithm that inserts points one at a time, deleting the triangles whose circumcircle contains the new point and retriangulating the resulting cavity.
a.box-muller.summary: A transform that turns two independent uniform variates U₁, U₂ into two independent standard normal variates √(−2 ln U₁)·cos(2πU₂) and √(−2 ln U₁)·sin(2πU₂).
a.boyer-moore.summary: A string search that compares the pattern from right to left and skips ahead by large amounts using the bad-character and good-suffix rules.
a.boyer-myrvold.summary: A linear-time planarity test that adds edges one at a time to a depth-first search tree while merging biconnected components, and also produces either a planar embedding or a Kuratowski subgraph.
a.boykov-kolmogorov.summary: A maximum-flow algorithm that grows search trees from both the source and the sink, augments when the trees meet, and reuses the trees by re-attaching orphaned nodes. It was designed for graph-cut energy minimization in computer vision.
a.bpe-tokenization.summary: A tokenization method that starts from characters and repeatedly merges the most frequent adjacent symbol pair in the corpus to build a subword vocabulary. It adapts the BPE compression algorithm to neural machine translation.
a.bpr.summary: A personalized ranking criterion that maximizes the posterior probability of pairwise orderings in which items a user interacted with rank above items they did not, together with a bootstrap-sampling SGD procedure to optimize it.
a.branch-and-bound.summary: A method for integer and combinatorial optimization that repeatedly branches the solution space into subproblems and prunes those whose bounds, obtained from relaxations, cannot improve on the best solution. It is the basic framework of mixed-integer programming solvers.
a.brandes-betweenness.summary: An algorithm that computes the betweenness centrality of all vertices in O(nm) time on unweighted graphs by counting shortest paths from each source and then accumulating dependencies in reverse order.
a.braun-ssa.summary: An SSA construction algorithm that, without a dominator tree or dominance frontiers, looks up a variable's current definition locally while processing basic blocks, creates φ-functions only on demand and removes trivial ones immediately. SSA form can be built directly from an abstract syntax tree.
a.brent-cycle-detection.summary: A cycle-detection algorithm that finds the cycle length and start of an iterated-function sequence by moving the comparison point at power-of-two intervals. It was presented in a paper improving Pollard's rho factorization.
a.brent-method.summary: A root-finding algorithm that switches among bisection, the secant method and inverse quadratic interpolation while keeping a bracketing interval. It guarantees convergence and usually converges quickly, so many numerical libraries use it as the default root finder.
a.bresenham-circle.summary: An algorithm that rasterizes a circle using only integer arithmetic, via octant symmetry and incremental error decisions.
a.bresenham-line.summary: An algorithm that draws a line on a raster grid using only integer addition and an error term.
a.bridson-poisson-disk.summary: An algorithm that generates Poisson-disk samples in arbitrary dimensions in O(n) time by picking a point from an active list, generating up to k candidates in the annulus between radius r and 2r, and accepting those that a background grid shows to be at least r from all existing points.
a.brief.summary: A binary descriptor formed as a bit string of intensity comparisons between predefined pixel pairs within a smoothed patch. Descriptors are matched quickly with the Hamming distance.
a.brodal-queue.summary: A priority queue supporting insert, meld, find-min and decrease-key in O(1) worst-case time and delete in O(log n) worst-case time. It achieves the amortized bounds of Fibonacci heaps in the worst case.
a.bron-kerbosch.summary: A backtracking algorithm that lists all maximal cliques of an undirected graph by recursively updating three sets: the current clique, the candidates and the excluded vertices.
a.brooks-forwarding-pointer.summary: A technique for incremental copying collection in which every object carries a forwarding-pointer field pointing to itself or to its copy, and all accesses go through this indirection, implementing the read barrier without a conditional branch.
a.brotli.o0.note: Originally developed by Google in 2013 for WOFF 2.0
a.brotli.summary: A web compression format that combines LZ77, Huffman coding, second-order context modeling, and a built-in static dictionary.
a.broyden-method.summary: A quasi-Newton method for systems of nonlinear equations that approximates the Jacobian with rank-one updates instead of recomputing it at every iteration.
a.brzozowski-derivatives.summary: A method that defines the derivative of a regular expression r with respect to a symbol a as the language of the remainders of strings in r that begin with a, after removing that a, and computes it syntactically. Repeated derivatives convert a regular expression directly into a DFA or decide whether a string matches.
a.bsp-tree.summary: A visible-surface method that recursively partitions a scene's polygons by planes into a binary tree built in advance and then traverses the tree according to the viewpoint to obtain a back-to-front order. For static scenes the tree need not be rebuilt when the viewpoint changes.
a.bst.summary: A binary tree that places smaller keys in the left subtree and larger keys in the right subtree. It was devised independently by several researchers around 1960.
a.btpe.summary: A binomial variate generation algorithm that performs rejection sampling with a majorizing function built from a triangle, a parallelogram and two exponential tails. When np is large it produces samples in constant expected time.
a.bubble-sort.summary: A sort that repeatedly passes over the array, comparing adjacent elements and swapping them when they are out of order. It takes O(n^2) time on average and in the worst case.
a.buddy-allocation.summary: A memory allocation technique that splits memory into power-of-two blocks, halving a block until it fits the request, and on release merges a block with its free buddy. It is used in the Linux page allocator.
a.buffer-tree.summary: An external-memory (a,b)-tree in which each internal node has a buffer that collects operations and pushes them down in batches. Each batched operation costs O((1/B) log_{M/B}(N/B)) amortized I/Os, which yields external-memory sorting, priority queues and similar algorithms.
a.bulk-synchronous-parallel.summary: A parallel computation model that structures a computation as a sequence of supersteps, each consisting of local computation on every processor, message exchange and a global barrier synchronization. It was proposed as a bridging model between hardware and software.
a.bulletproofs.summary: Short non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs that need no trusted setup and rely only on the discrete-logarithm assumption. Range-proof size grows only logarithmically in the number of bits, and they are used for confidential transactions in Monero and elsewhere.
a.bully-algorithm.summary: A leader-election algorithm in which a process that detects the coordinator's failure sends election messages to all higher-numbered processes and, if none responds, declares itself coordinator. The highest-numbered live process is elected.
a.bump-mapping.summary: A technique that perturbs surface normals using the gradient of a height function, without changing the geometry, so that lighting makes the surface appear wrinkled or bumpy. Because only the normals used in shading change, silhouettes remain smooth.
a.burst-trie.summary: A structure for string keys that first collects keys in small containers such as lists or trees and, when a container grows too large, 'bursts' it into a trie node. It combines the fast prefix branching of tries with the space efficiency of the containers.
a.bvh.o0.note: Proposed hierarchical geometric models for visible-surface algorithms and is cited as the starting point of the hierarchical bounding volume idea.
a.bvh.o1.note: Applied a hierarchy of bounding boxes to accelerate ray tracing.
a.bvh.summary: An acceleration structure that nests bounding volumes enclosing objects in a tree, so that when a ray or query misses a volume all objects beneath it can be skipped. It is widely used in ray tracing and collision detection to reduce the number of intersection tests.
a.bw-tree.summary: A latch-free B-tree that references nodes indirectly through logical IDs and a mapping table and, instead of modifying nodes in place, prepends delta records and swings the mapping with CAS. It targets multicore processors and flash storage and keeps sibling links as in B-link trees.
a.bwa.summary: A method for aligning short sequencing reads that performs backward search with backtracking, allowing mismatches and gaps, on an index built from the Burrows–Wheeler transform of the reference genome. It explores the prefix trie implicitly on the BWT without building it.
a.bwt.summary: A reversible transform that sorts all rotations of a string and takes the last column. Grouping identical characters together improves the compression ratio.
a.byzantine-agreement.o0.note: The name 'Byzantine Generals Problem' was introduced in the same authors' 1982 TOPLAS paper 'The Byzantine Generals Problem' (doi:10.1145/357172.357176).
a.byzantine-agreement.summary: A consensus algorithm in which nodes exchange messages over several rounds so that correct nodes agree on the same value even if some nodes behave arbitrarily (Byzantine faults). With unsigned messages, tolerating m faults requires at least 3m+1 nodes.
a.bzip2.summary: A block-sorting compressor that applies BWT, MTF, run-length encoding, and Huffman coding in sequence.
a.c4-5.summary: A successor to ID3 for building decision trees that adds the gain ratio, splits on continuous attributes, handling of missing values, and pruning.
a.cabac.summary: An entropy coding method that binarizes syntax elements and codes each bin with a table-based binary arithmetic coder, using the probability of a context model selected from neighboring information. Introduced in H.264/AVC, it is also the entropy coder of HEVC and VVC.
a.calendar-queue.summary: A priority queue that distributes event times into an array of fixed-width 'day' buckets, much like hashing, keeping each bucket as a sorted list. By resizing the number and width of buckets as the queue size changes, it runs in O(1) average time in discrete-event simulation.
a.calic.summary: A lossless image compression algorithm that predicts pixels with gradient-adjusted prediction (GAP), which judges edge direction from local gradients, refines the prediction with context-based error feedback, and codes the residuals with context-based arithmetic coding.
a.camellia.summary: A 128-bit block cipher jointly developed by NTT and Mitsubishi Electric. It is an 18- or 24-round Feistel network with inserted FL functions and is standardized by ISO/IEC and the IETF.
a.camshift.summary: A tracking algorithm that locates the target center with mean shift on a color probability distribution image and updates the search window's size and orientation from the distribution's moments every frame. It was proposed for face tracking.
a.canny-edge-detector.summary: An edge detector that smooths with a Gaussian, computes gradients, and obtains thin edges through non-maximum suppression along the gradient direction and hysteresis tracking with two thresholds. It was designed around criteria of detection, localization, and single response.
a.canonical-huffman.summary: A representation of a prefix code in which codewords are determined solely by each symbol's code length and assigned in lexicographic order, so that codewords of equal length are consecutive binary numbers. Since only the code lengths need to be transmitted instead of the code table, it is used in many formats such as DEFLATE and JPEG.
a.cantor-zassenhaus.summary: A probabilistic algorithm that factors a polynomial over a finite field by first splitting it into products of equal-degree factors via distinct-degree factorization and then separating them with gcds against (q^d−1)/2 powers of random polynomials. It is a standard method in computer algebra systems.
a.cart.summary: Classification and regression trees that make binary splits by Gini impurity or squared error and apply cost-complexity pruning.
a.cartesian-tree.summary: A binary tree built from a sequence so that it is a binary search tree with respect to positions and heap-ordered with respect to values. It can be built in linear time with a stack and is used to reduce range-minimum queries to lowest-common-ancestor queries.
a.catboost.summary: A decision-tree boosting method that handles categorical features with ordered target statistics and uses ordered boosting to reduce the target leakage and prediction shift of gradient boosting. It uses symmetric (oblivious) trees as base learners.
a.catmull-clark.summary: An algorithm that subdivides polygon meshes of arbitrary topology into smooth surfaces by systematically adding face, edge, and vertex points.
a.catmull-rom-spline.summary: A cubic Hermite interpolating spline whose tangent at each control point is set from the difference of the two neighboring control points; the curve passes through every control point, and changing one point affects it only locally. It is widely used to interpolate animation paths and camera motion.
a.cbc-mode.o0.note: Defined as a DES mode of operation together with the ECB, CFB and OFB modes.
a.cbc-mode.summary: A block-cipher mode of operation that XORs each plaintext block with the previous ciphertext block before encryption. The first block uses an initialization vector, so identical plaintext blocks encrypt differently depending on position.
a.ccd-ik.summary: An inverse kinematics solver that iterates over the joints of a chain from the end toward the root, rotating each joint so that the vector from that joint to the end effector points toward the target, and repeats the sweep. Its simplicity makes it widely used in games and animation.
a.ccm.summary: An AEAD scheme that computes an authentication tag with CBC-MAC and encrypts with counter mode. It needs only one block-cipher key and is used in IEEE 802.11i, Bluetooth LE and TLS.
a.celt.summary: A low-delay audio codec that splits MDCT coefficients into the energy of each critical band and a unit-norm shape vector, transmitting the energy explicitly and coding the shape with pyramid vector quantization. It serves as the MDCT layer of the Opus codec.
a.cfrac.summary: A factorization algorithm that collects small quadratic residues arising from the continued fraction expansion of √n that are smooth over a factor base and combines them into a congruence of squares. Lehmer and Powers first described it, and Morrison and Brillhart turned it into a computer algorithm with a factor base and linear algebra.
a.chacha.summary: A stream cipher that modifies the Salsa20 quarter-round to increase diffusion per round.
a.chacha20-poly1305.summary: An AEAD construction that combines ChaCha20 encryption with Poly1305 authentication. It is one of the mandatory cipher suites of TLS 1.3.
a.chaikin.summary: A subdivision algorithm that produces a smooth curve by repeated corner cutting, replacing each edge of a polyline with two new points at 1/4 and 3/4 along it. The limit curve is a uniform quadratic B-spline.
a.chain-decomposition.summary: A method that decomposes a graph into chains, one per back edge of a depth-first search tree, and uses the result to find bridges and cut vertices and to test 2-vertex- and 2-edge-connectivity.
a.chain-replication.summary: A replication technique that arranges replicas in a chain: writes enter at the head and propagate in order to the tail, while reads and replies are served by the tail, providing strong consistency with high throughput.
a.chaitin-register-allocation.summary: A register-allocation approach that builds an interference graph linking variables live at the same time, colors it by repeatedly removing nodes whose degree is below the number of registers, and inserts spill code when coloring fails.
a.champ.summary: A HAMT variant that splits each node's entries into payload entries and sub-node entries, grouped separately and tracked by two bitmaps. This speeds up iteration and equality checks and lowers memory use; it is used, for example, by Scala 2.13's immutable HashMap.
a.chan-hull.summary: An O(n log h) convex hull algorithm that runs Graham scan on small groups and then performs a Jarvis march over the group hulls.
a.chandy-lamport-snapshot.summary: An algorithm that obtains a consistent global snapshot of a distributed system with FIFO channels by propagating marker messages and recording each process's state and each channel's state without halting execution.
a.chang-roberts.summary: A leader-election algorithm for unidirectional rings in which each process circulates its identifier, forwarding received identifiers larger than its own and discarding smaller ones, so that the process with the largest identifier is elected. It uses O(n log n) messages on average.
a.chase-lev-deque.summary: A lock-free work-stealing deque built on a growable circular array. The owner works at the bottom and thieves take from the top, removing the fixed-size limit and overflow problem of earlier deques.
a.chd.summary: A construction of minimal perfect hash functions that splits the keys into buckets, places the buckets from largest to smallest by searching for collision-free displacement values, and stores the displacement array in compressed form.
a.cheney.summary: An algorithm that performs copying GC without recursion or an auxiliary stack by using the new semispace itself as the breadth-first search queue.
a.chew-second-algorithm.summary: Delaunay refinement algorithm that repeatedly inserts circumcenters of poor-quality triangles into a constrained Delaunay triangulation, splitting boundary edges when needed, to produce meshes with a guaranteed minimum angle. The original paper also covers mesh generation on curved surfaces.
a.chiba-nishizeki.summary: An algorithm that lists subgraphs such as triangles by processing vertices in decreasing order of degree and marking their neighbours. It lists all triangles in O(a(G)m) time, where a(G) is the arboricity of the graph.
a.chien-search.summary: A method that finds the roots of the error-locator polynomial by evaluating it at every element of the finite field in turn, updating each term by a constant multiplication to save work. BCH and Reed–Solomon decoders use it to locate errors.
a.chinese-postman.summary: An algorithm that solves the Chinese postman problem on undirected graphs in polynomial time by computing a minimum-weight perfect matching on the odd-degree vertices with shortest-path distances as weights, duplicating the matched paths, and finding an Eulerian circuit, which gives the shortest closed walk traversing every edge at least once.
a.cholesky.o0.note: Published by his colleague Benoît after Cholesky's death, describing Cholesky's procedure.
a.cholesky.summary: A factorization of a symmetric positive-definite matrix into a lower-triangular matrix times its transpose. It solves linear systems and least-squares problems with about half the work of LU factorization.
a.chord.summary: A distributed hash table protocol that provides O(log n)-hop lookups using finger tables on a consistent hashing ring.
a.christofides.o0.note: The original technical report was republished in Operations Research Forum in 2022.
a.christofides.o1.note: The same algorithm was published independently in the USSR; van Bevern and Slugina (2020) documented its history.
a.christofides.summary: An approximation algorithm for the metric traveling salesman problem that adds a minimum-cost perfect matching on the odd-degree vertices of a minimum spanning tree, forms an Eulerian circuit, and shortcuts repeated vertices, yielding a tour at most 1.5 times optimal.
a.chu-liu-edmonds.summary: An algorithm that finds a minimum-cost spanning arborescence of a directed graph by selecting the cheapest incoming edge for each non-root vertex, contracting any resulting cycle into a single vertex with adjusted edge weights, solving recursively, and then expanding the cycles.
a.cipolla.summary: An algorithm that solves x² ≡ n (mod p) by finding a such that a²−n is a quadratic non-residue and computing (a+√(a²−n))^((p+1)/2) in the extension field F_p(√(a²−n)). It is preferable to Tonelli–Shanks when p−1 contains a large power of two.
a.cityhash.summary: A family of non-cryptographic string hash functions released by Google. It has 32-, 64- and 128-bit variants tuned for fast hashing of short strings on 64-bit CPUs.
a.ckks.summary: A Ring-LWE-based homomorphic encryption scheme that treats ciphertext noise as part of the approximation error, supporting approximate arithmetic on vectors of real or complex numbers. Rescaling after multiplication preserves precision, and it is used for tasks such as machine-learning inference on encrypted data.
a.clahe.summary: Contrast enhancement that equalizes histograms over image tiles while clipping each histogram at a fixed height to limit contrast amplification, interpolating across tile boundaries. It avoids over-amplifying noise.
a.clarke-wright.summary: A construction heuristic for the vehicle routing problem that starts with a separate round trip from the depot to each customer and merges routes in decreasing order of the distance saved by joining them, subject to capacity constraints.
a.classical-mds.summary: A multidimensional scaling method that double-centers a distance matrix into an inner-product matrix and recovers point coordinates from its top eigenvectors. With Euclidean distances it gives the same result as PCA.
a.classifier-free-guidance.summary: A technique that jointly trains conditional and unconditional diffusion models in one network and, at sampling time, combines their predictions with a weight to trade diversity for fidelity to the condition. No separate classifier is needed.
a.clauset-newman-moore.summary: A greedy community-detection algorithm that repeatedly merges the pair of communities with the largest modularity gain, found with heaps. It runs in O(md log n) time, where d is the depth of the dendrogram.
a.clenshaw-algorithm.summary: A method that evaluates linear combinations of functions satisfying a three-term recurrence, such as Chebyshev polynomials, by a backward recurrence. It generalizes Horner's method to such bases.
a.clenshaw-curtis.summary: A numerical integration rule that integrates the Chebyshev series interpolating the integrand at Chebyshev points. It can be computed quickly with a cosine transform.
a.clh-lock.summary: A FIFO queue spin lock in which each thread enqueues its node at the tail with an atomic swap and spins on the flag of its predecessor's node. The nodes form an implicit linked list without explicit next pointers.
a.clinger-algorithm.summary: An algorithm for converting a decimal string to the nearest floating-point number. When the significand and the power of ten are exactly representable it takes a fast path of a single floating-point multiplication or division; otherwise it refines an extended-precision approximation with big-integer arithmetic.
a.clip.summary: A method that contrastively trains an image encoder and a text encoder on large-scale image–text pairs so that matching pairs have similar embeddings. It enables zero-shot classification from class-name prompts.
a.clique-percolation.summary: A method that finds overlapping communities, in which a vertex may belong to several communities, by joining adjacent k-cliques that share k−1 vertices into one community.
a.closest-pair-divide-and-conquer.o0.not: Solved the planar closest-pair problem in O(n log n) time.
a.closest-pair-divide-and-conquer.o1.not: Generalized divide and conquer to multidimensional space, solving the closest-pair problem in fixed dimension in O(n log n) time.
a.closest-pair-divide-and-conquer.summar: Algorithm that splits the points by one coordinate, recursively finds the closest pair on each side, and then examines cross pairs only inside a narrow strip around the dividing line, finding the overall closest pair in O(n log n) time.
a.cmac.summary: A CBC-MAC variant that computes a MAC over messages of any length with a single block-cipher key. XORing a key-derived value into the last block makes it secure for variable-length messages, and NIST standardized it as SP 800-38B.
a.codel.summary: Active queue management that measures each packet's sojourn time in the queue and starts dropping when the minimum sojourn time over an interval exceeds a target, shortening the interval between drops. It needs almost no tuning.
a.coherent-point-drift.summary: Point set registration method that treats one point set as the centroids of a Gaussian mixture model and the other as data, aligning them by maximizing the likelihood with the EM algorithm. Constraining the centroids to move coherently as a group, it handles rigid, affine and non-rigid registration.
a.comb-sort.summary: A variant of bubble sort that starts with a large comparison gap and shrinks it by a constant factor between passes. Small values near the end of the array move forward quickly, so it needs fewer swaps than bubble sort.
a.commentz-walter.summary: A multi-pattern search algorithm that matches a trie of the reversed patterns from the right end of a text window and skips ahead with Boyer–Moore-style shift rules. On average it inspects only part of the text characters, and its shifts are bounded by the length of the shortest pattern.
a.conditional-random-field.summary: A discriminative undirected graphical model that directly models the conditional probability of a label sequence given an observation sequence as an exponential-family model of feature functions. It is used for sequence labeling such as part-of-speech tagging and named-entity recognition.
a.conjugate-gradient.summary: An iterative method for symmetric positive-definite linear systems that proceeds along mutually conjugate search directions. It is a standard solver for large sparse systems.
a.connected-component-labeling.summary: Assigns a unique label to each group of connected foreground pixels in a binary image. The classic two-pass scheme records provisional labels and their equivalences in a first raster scan and resolves them in a second scan.
a.consistent-hashing.summary: A distributed hashing scheme that places nodes and keys on the same hash ring so that only about 1/n of the keys move when nodes are added or removed.
a.constrained-delaunay.summary: Triangulation that must contain a given set of segments (constraints) and otherwise satisfies the empty-circumcircle condition among points that are visible to each other past the constraints. It is the basis for meshing planar straight-line graphs (PSLGs) and for polygon triangulation.
a.contraction-hierarchies.summary: A road-network routing technique whose preprocessing contracts vertices one by one in order of importance while adding shortcut edges that preserve shortest paths; queries run a bidirectional Dijkstra search that only follows edges toward higher-ranked vertices. Routing engines such as OSRM and GraphHopper use it.
a.contrastive-divergence.summary: A learning rule that approximates the log-likelihood gradient with samples from a few steps of Gibbs sampling started at the data rather than from the equilibrium distribution. It became the standard way to train restricted Boltzmann machines.
a.cook-torrance.o0.note: The following year it also appeared as a paper with the same title in ACM Transactions on Graphics 1(1) (doi:10.1145/357290.357293).
a.cook-torrance.summary: A physically based reflectance model that expresses specular reflection as the product of a microfacet distribution function, a geometric attenuation term and a Fresnel term. By modeling wavelength-dependent Fresnel reflection from the material's refractive index, it reproduces the color difference between metals and plastics.
a.coppersmith-winograd.summary: An algorithm that lowered the matrix multiplication exponent to 2.376 using a laser method that exploits arithmetic progression structure.
a.copying-gc.summary: A garbage collector that reclaims memory without fragmentation by copying and compacting live objects into the other semispace.
a.cordic.summary: An algorithm that computes trigonometric and related functions by iterating rotations through predetermined angles using only shifts and additions. Used in hardware without multipliers and in calculators, it was later extended to hyperbolic functions and logarithms.
a.cost-scaling.summary: A successive-approximation algorithm for minimum-cost flow that refines an ε-optimal flow with push–relabel operations while decreasing ε in each phase. Solvers such as OR-Tools use this approach for minimum-cost flow.
a.count-min-sketch.summary: A sketch that approximates the frequencies of stream elements, erring toward overestimation, by taking the minimum of counters across multiple hash rows.
a.count-sketch.summary: A streaming sketch that updates arrays of counters using several hash functions and ±1 sign hashes, and estimates an item's frequency by taking the median. It is used to find frequent items.
a.counting-bloom-filter.summary: An extension of the Bloom filter that uses counters instead of bits to support element deletion.
a.counting-quotient-filter.summary: An extension of the quotient filter that stores variable-length counters per element and speeds up operations with hardware bit-manipulation instructions. It supports concurrent updates.
a.counting-sort.summary: A non-comparison sort that counts the occurrences of each key value and determines positions from prefix sums. It runs in O(n + k) for a key range k.
a.cover-tree.summary: A hierarchical tree that arranges the points of a metric space in levels satisfying covering and separation conditions whose radius halves at each level. For data with a small expansion constant, nearest-neighbor search takes time logarithmic in the number of points.
a.cramer-shoup.summary: The first practical public-key cryptosystem proven secure against adaptive chosen-ciphertext attacks in the standard model under the decisional Diffie–Hellman assumption alone. It extends ElGamal with values that let the receiver check ciphertext validity.
a.crc.summary: An error-detecting code that treats data as a polynomial over GF(2) and appends the remainder of division by a generator polynomial as the check value. It is easy to implement with shift registers and is strong at detecting burst errors.
a.crc32c.summary: A CRC using the 32-bit generator polynomial 0x1EDC6F41, chosen by a search for good error-detection properties. It is used in iSCSI, SCTP, ext4, Btrfs and others, and x86 SSE4.2 has a dedicated instruction for it.
a.crdt.summary: Replicated data types designed so that, even when each replica is updated without coordination, all replicas converge to the same state by merging states (state-based) or delivering commutative operations (operation-based). They guarantee strong eventual consistency.
a.criminisi-inpainting.summary: Exemplar-based inpainting that fills the missing region by copying the most similar patches from the rest of the image, prioritizing locations where linear structures continue into the hole. It restores both texture and structure after large objects are removed.
a.crossing-number-pip.summary: Point-in-polygon test that casts a ray from the query point in one direction and reports the point as inside when the ray crosses the polygon boundary an odd number of times. It implements the even–odd rule.
a.crp.summary: A route-planning technique split into metric-independent preprocessing that partitions the road network hierarchically, a fast customization phase that recomputes distances between cell boundary vertices for a new cost function, and Dijkstra-based queries on the multilevel graph, so that frequently changing cost functions can be handled quickly.
a.ctc.summary: A loss function that sums the probabilities of all alignment paths, including a blank symbol, with a forward–backward algorithm, letting a recurrent network learn label sequences without pre-aligned inputs and labels.
a.ctr-mode.o0.note: Cited as the first description of driving a block cipher with a counter to produce a keystream.
a.ctr-mode.summary: A mode of operation that encrypts successive counter values with a block cipher to produce a keystream XORed with the plaintext. Blocks are independent, allowing parallel processing and random access.
a.ctrie.o0.note: Presented at the LCPC 2011 workshop; the proceedings were published in 2013.
a.ctrie.o1.note: Extends the same structure with a constant-time snapshot operation.
a.ctrie.summary: A concurrent map that updates a HAMT-like hash trie without locks using CAS operations. Indirection nodes make resizing and updates atomic, and a later extension added constant-time atomic snapshots; it is implemented as Scala's TrieMap.
a.ctw.summary: A sequential probability assignment method that recursively mixes, at every node of a context tree, the probabilities given by all context-tree models of depth up to D, efficiently computing a Bayesian mixture over all tree-source models. Combined with arithmetic coding, it has a guaranteed redundancy bound for tree sources.
a.cube-mapping.summary: An environment mapping scheme that stores the environment as images projected onto the six faces of a cube centered at the viewpoint and looks up the face selected by the direction vector's component of largest magnitude. With less distortion than spherical projections and no singularities, it became a standard GPU texture format.
a.cubic.summary: A TCP congestion control that grows the congestion window as a cubic function of the time elapsed since the last loss. Window growth is independent of RTT, and it is the default congestion control in Linux and other systems.
a.cuckoo-filter.summary: An approximate set-membership structure that stores fingerprints in a cuckoo hash table and supports deletion.
a.cuckoo-hashing.summary: A hashing scheme that gives each key two candidate positions and, on a collision, evicts the existing key to its other candidate, guaranteeing worst-case O(1) lookups.
a.cuppen-divide-and-conquer.summary: An eigenvalue algorithm for symmetric tridiagonal matrices that splits the problem into two subproblems, solves them, and merges the results by solving a secular equation for a rank-one modification. It is used in LAPACK's divide-and-conquer eigensolvers.
a.cycle-canceling.summary: A minimum-cost flow algorithm that starts from a feasible flow and repeatedly sends flow around negative-cost cycles in the residual graph; when no negative cycle remains, the flow has minimum cost.
a.cycle-sort.summary: An in-place sort that decomposes the sorting permutation into cycles and writes each element directly to its final position. It minimises the number of writes to the original array.
a.cyk.o0.venue: Air Force Cambridge Research Lab technical report
a.cyk.summary: An O(n³) parsing algorithm for grammars in Chomsky normal form that fills a table with the nonterminals that can generate each substring.
a.cyrus-beck.summary: Two- and three-dimensional line clipping algorithm that writes the segment parametrically and uses dot products with the normal of each boundary of a convex clip region to obtain entering and leaving parameters, yielding the portion that lies inside the region.
a.cytron-ssa.o0.note: An extended version appeared in TOPLAS in 1991 as "Efficiently computing static single assignment form and the control dependence graph".
a.cytron-ssa.summary: An algorithm that computes dominance frontiers from the dominator tree, inserts φ-functions only at iterated dominance frontiers, and renames variables during a walk of the dominator tree to build SSA form. The same framework also yields the control dependence graph.
a.d-ary-heap.summary: An array-based heap in which every node has up to d children. The tree height drops to log_d n, making insert and decrease-key faster at the cost of O(d log_d n) time for delete-min.
a.d-star-lite.summary: A replanning algorithm that performs an LPA*-style incremental search from the goal toward the current position and replans by incorporating only the edge-cost changes the robot observes as it moves. It implements the same navigation strategy as D* with a simpler structure.
a.d-star.summary: A dynamic A* that incrementally replans paths when edge costs change in a partially known environment.
a.damerau-levenshtein-distance.summary: A string distance defined as the minimum number of operations among insertion, deletion, substitution and transposition of two adjacent characters. It stems from the observation that most spelling errors are a single error of one of these four kinds.
a.dancing-links.o0.note: Knuth credits Hitotumatu and Noshita (1979) with earlier use of the linked-list technique.
a.dancing-links.summary: A technique that exploits the fact that a node removed from a doubly linked list still holds its neighbor pointers, so it can be put back in constant time. It is used to remove and restore rows and columns in the backtracking search for exact cover (Algorithm X).
a.data-centric-code-generation.summary: A query execution technique that divides a query plan at pipeline breakers and compiles each pipeline into a tight machine-code loop that keeps tuples in registers. Code is generated with LLVM.
a.dbscan.summary: A clustering method that links core points, those with at least minPts neighbors within radius ε, into dense regions and labels points reachable from no cluster as noise. It finds arbitrarily shaped clusters without fixing their number in advance.
a.dc3.summary: A suffix array construction algorithm that recursively sorts the suffixes at positions not divisible by three using character triples, sorts the remaining suffixes with that result and merges the two sets. It runs in linear time and extends to parallel and external-memory models.
a.dct.summary: An orthogonal transform that represents a signal as a sum of real cosine basis functions. Because energy concentrates in the low-frequency coefficients, it is used in lossy compression such as JPEG and MPEG.
a.dctcp.summary: A TCP congestion control for data centers in which switches set ECN marks when the queue exceeds a threshold and senders reduce the congestion window in proportion to the fraction of marked packets.
a.ddim.summary: A diffusion sampling method that defines non-Markovian forward processes sharing the DDPM training objective, enabling deterministic sampling in far fewer steps.
a.ddpg.summary: An actor-critic algorithm with a deterministic-policy actor and a Q-function critic as neural networks, learning off-policy in continuous action spaces with a replay buffer and slowly tracking target networks.
a.ddpm.summary: A method that parameterizes the reverse process of a diffusion model with a network predicting the noise added at each step, trained with a simplified noise-prediction loss. It showed a connection to denoising score matching.
a.de-boor-algorithm.summary: A method that evaluates splines stably via a recurrence that builds B-spline basis functions from lower to higher degree. It generalizes de Casteljau's algorithm to B-splines.
a.deep-belief-network.summary: A probabilistic generative model built by greedily training and stacking restricted Boltzmann machines one layer at a time. It was widely used for unsupervised pretraining of deep networks.
a.deepwalk.summary: A method that learns low-dimensional vertex representations by treating short random walks generated on the graph as sentences and training a SkipGram language model on them.
a.deferred-reference-counting.summary: A reference-counting technique that counts only references from within the heap, not from the stack and local variables, collecting objects whose count drops to zero in a table and reclaiming them after a stack scan confirms they are unreferenced.
a.deferred-shading.summary: A rendering approach that first resolves visibility and stores per-pixel attributes such as normals and material parameters in buffers, and then performs lighting only for the visible pixels. It avoids the cost of shading occluded fragments and later became widespread as G-buffer-based real-time rendering.
a.deficit-round-robin.summary: An approximation of fair queuing that adds a fixed quantum to each queue's deficit counter every round and sends packets only as far as the counter allows. It achieves fairness with variable-length packets using O(1) work per packet.
a.deflate.o0.title: The Deflate method of PKZIP 2.0
a.deflate.summary: A format that further compresses the output of LZ77 match finding with Huffman codes. It underlies zip, gzip, and PNG.
a.dekker-algorithm.o0.note: The algorithm is due to the Dutch mathematician Th. J. Dekker; Dijkstra presented it as Dekker's solution in this manuscript (and in the earlier Dutch manuscript EWD35).
a.dekker-algorithm.summary: A mutual exclusion algorithm that lets two processes take turns entering a critical section using only shared variables (intent flags and a turn variable). It is the first known correct two-process mutual exclusion solution.
a.delta-stepping.summary: A parallel single-source shortest-path algorithm that groups vertices into distance buckets of width Δ, repeatedly relaxing light edges within the current bucket and relaxing heavy edges once after the bucket is settled. Depending on Δ, it behaves between Dijkstra's algorithm and Bellman–Ford.
a.denoising-autoencoder.summary: An autoencoder trained to reconstruct the clean input from a randomly corrupted version of it. Stacked layer by layer, it was used for unsupervised pretraining of deep networks.
a.densenet.summary: A convolutional network in which each layer receives the channel-wise concatenation of the feature maps of all preceding layers. Feature reuse reduces the number of parameters.
a.des.summary: A block cipher with a 56-bit key and a 16-round Feistel structure. It became a US federal standard in 1977.
a.dfp.summary: An early quasi-Newton (variable metric) minimization method that updates an approximation of the inverse Hessian with a rank-two correction computed from gradient changes.
a.dfs.o0.note: A method devised in the 19th century, recorded by Lucas
a.dfs.o0.title: Trémaux's maze-solving method
a.dfs.o0.venue: Recorded in Édouard Lucas, Récréations mathématiques Vol. 1
a.dfs.summary: A graph traversal that goes as deep as possible before backtracking. It is the backbone of many graph algorithms.
a.dial.summary: A shortest-path algorithm for small non-negative integer edge weights that replaces Dijkstra's priority queue with an array of buckets indexed by distance, running in O(E + V·C) time, where C is the maximum edge weight.
a.diamond-square.summary: An algorithm that generates fractal terrain heightmaps by starting from the heights at the grid corners and repeatedly filling square centers (diamond step) and edge midpoints (square step) with the average of neighboring values plus a random displacement, reducing the displacement magnitude at each level.
a.diffie-hellman.summary: A public-key protocol that relies on the hardness of the discrete logarithm problem to let two parties agree on a shared secret over an eavesdropped channel.
a.diffusion-model.summary: A generative model that defines a forward diffusion process gradually adding noise to data and learns the reverse process to generate samples. It was inspired by non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
a.dijkstra-mutex.summary: A mutual exclusion algorithm that guarantees, using only shared-memory reads and writes, that at most one of N processes is in its critical section. It guarantees freedom from deadlock: some process always eventually enters.
a.dijkstra.summary: A single-source shortest-path algorithm for graphs with nonnegative weights that grows the set of vertices with finalized shortest distances one vertex at a time.
a.dinic.summary: An algorithm that computes maximum flow in O(V²E) by repeatedly building level graphs and blocking flows.
a.discrete-frechet.summary: Distance that minimizes the longest link over all order-preserving couplings of the vertex sequences of two polylines, computed in O(pq) time by dynamic programming over a p x q table. It is used as an approximation of the continuous Fréchet distance.
a.distance-transform.summary: A transform that labels each pixel of a binary image with its distance to the nearest background (or foreground) pixel. The classic sequential algorithm propagates local distances in a forward and a backward raster scan.
a.distributed-ray-tracing.summary: A ray tracing method that stochastically distributes rays over pixel area, lens aperture, time, reflection and refraction directions, and light source area. It obtains anti-aliasing, depth of field, motion blur, glossy reflection and soft shadows within a single framework.
a.divide-and-conquer-delaunay.summary: Algorithm that sorts the points by x, splits them in half, recursively triangulates each half, and merges the two Delaunay triangulations by adding cross edges from the lower common tangent upward. It runs in O(n log n) time.
a.divide-and-conquer-voronoi.summary: Algorithm that splits the point set in two, recursively builds the Voronoi diagram of each half, and merges them along the dividing chain. It runs in O(n log n) time in the plane and underlies solutions to proximity problems such as closest pair and minimum spanning tree.
a.dixon-factorization.summary: A factorization method that collects random x for which x² mod n is smooth over a small prime base and combines them through linear dependencies of exponent vectors into a congruence of squares. It is known as a factoring algorithm with a rigorously proven subexponential running time.
a.dmc.summary: A compression method that counts next-bit probabilities in each state of a bit-level finite-state Markov model, grows the model by cloning states reached through frequently used transitions, and codes the bits with arithmetic coding.
a.doo-sabin.summary: A subdivision surface scheme that creates new vertices inside each face and generates new faces corresponding to the original faces, edges and vertices; in regular regions it converges to a uniform biquadratic B-spline surface. It handles polygon meshes of arbitrary topology, and the original paper analyzed its behavior near extraordinary points.
