a.dormand-prince.summary: An embedded Runge–Kutta pair that obtains fifth- and fourth-order solutions from the same stages to estimate the error and adapt the step size. It is the method behind MATLAB's ode45 and SciPy's RK45.
a.dot-product-attention.summary: Global and local attention that computes alignment scores as the dot product of the decoder state and the encoder states.
a.double-array-trie.summary: A trie representation that encodes state transitions in two integer arrays, BASE and CHECK, so that each transition takes a few array accesses. It is compact and fast, and is used for dictionaries in morphological analyzers and similar tools.
a.double-dqn.summary: An algorithm that applies Double Q-learning's reduction of overestimation to deep Q-learning by selecting the target action with the online network and evaluating it with the target network.
a.double-metaphone.summary: A phonetic encoding algorithm that extends Metaphone to produce two codes, a primary and an alternate, for each word. It accounts for alternative pronunciations of names originating from languages other than English.
a.double-q-learning.summary: An algorithm that keeps two Q functions, selecting the maximizing action with one and evaluating it with the other, to reduce the overestimation bias caused by Q-learning's max operator.
a.double-ratchet.o0.note: First used in 2013 under the name Axolotl Ratchet; it was renamed and published as a specification in 2016.
a.double-ratchet.summary: A key-management algorithm for end-to-end encryption that derives a new key for every message with a symmetric-key ratchet and refreshes the root key with a Diffie–Hellman ratchet whenever a reply arrives. It provides forward secrecy and post-compromise security and is the core of the Signal Protocol.
a.douglas-rachford.summary: A splitting scheme that solves problems involving the sum of two operators by alternating implicit steps for each operator. First proposed as an alternating-direction implicit method for heat conduction, it was later extended to monotone operators and convex optimization.
a.dpo.summary: An alignment method that trains a language model directly on preference pairs with a classification loss defined by log-probability ratios between the policy and a reference model, without a reward model or reinforcement learning.
a.dqn.summary: A deep reinforcement-learning algorithm that approximates the action-value function with a convolutional neural network and trains it with Q-learning updates on samples drawn from an experience replay buffer. It learned Atari games from raw screen pixels.
a.dragon4.summary: A floating-point-to-string conversion algorithm that uses arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic to generate decimal digits and stops at the shortest digit string that reads back to the same value.
a.dropout.summary: A regularization technique that randomly disables neurons during training and scales the weights at inference to prevent co-adaptation.
a.dsa.summary: A US federal standard signature scheme that reduces signature size by restricting ElGamal signatures to a prime-order subgroup.
a.dsatur.summary: A greedy graph-colouring heuristic that next colours the vertex whose neighbours already use the largest number of distinct colours (its saturation degree), breaking ties by degree.
a.dsst-persistence.o0.note: The journal version appeared in Journal of Computer and System Sciences 38(1), 1989.
a.dsst-persistence.summary: General techniques that make a linked data structure persistent, so that past versions remain accessible after updates. The work introduced the fat-node, node-copying and node-splitting methods and, applying them to red–black trees, obtained persistent search trees that use O(1) amortized space per update.
a.dual-contouring.summary: An isosurface extraction method that places one vertex per cell at the position minimizing a quadratic error function built from the intersection points and normals (Hermite data) on sign-changing grid edges, and forms a face for each sign-changing edge by connecting the vertices of the surrounding cells. Unlike marching cubes, it preserves sharp edges and corners.
a.dual-pivot-quicksort.o0.title: Dual-Pivot Quicksort proposal
a.dual-pivot-quicksort.summary: A quicksort variant that uses two pivots to partition the array into three segments. It was adopted as Java 7's sort for arrays of primitive types.
a.dual-quaternion-skinning.summary: A skinning method that represents joint transformations as unit dual quaternions and blends them by a weighted average followed by normalization, yielding a rigid transformation. It reduces the volume loss of linear blend skinning at similar cost.
a.duan-sssp.summary: A deterministic algorithm that solves single-source shortest paths on directed graphs with non-negative real weights in O(m log^{2/3} n) time in the comparison-addition model. It recursively solves a bounded multi-source shortest path (BMSSP) problem and uses Bellman–Ford-style relaxation to reduce the number of vertices to process, surpassing Dijkstra's O(m + n log n) bound on sparse graphs.
a.dueling-dqn.summary: A Q-network architecture that splits into a state-value stream and an action-advantage stream and combines them to output Q values. It learns state values efficiently even in states where the choice of action matters little.
a.durand-kerner.summary: An iterative method that finds all roots of a polynomial at once by updating approximations to every root simultaneously. It can also be obtained by applying the multidimensional Newton method to the system given by Vieta's formulas.
a.dutch-national-flag.summary: The problem of splitting an array holding three kinds of values into three regions in a single pass, and the partitioning algorithm that solves it. It is used for three-way partitioning in quicksort when many keys are equal.
a.duval-lyndon.summary: An algorithm that computes, in linear time and constant extra space, the Lyndon factorization of a string into a lexicographically non-increasing sequence of Lyndon words. It is used as a subroutine for computing least rotations and BWT variants.
a.dwyer-delaunay.summary: Divide-and-conquer Delaunay triangulation algorithm with a modified partitioning scheme that runs in expected O(n log log n) time on uniformly distributed input while keeping an O(n log n) worst case.
a.ear-clipping.summary: Polygon triangulation that repeatedly cuts off an 'ear', a triangle formed by a convex vertex and its two neighbours that contains no other vertex. It rests on the two ears theorem, which states that every simple polygon has at least two non-overlapping ears; a straightforward implementation runs in O(n^2) time.
a.earley.summary: An algorithm that parses arbitrary context-free grammars in O(n³), and unambiguous grammars in O(n²), by maintaining state sets as a chart.
a.earliest-deadline-first.summary: A real-time scheduling scheme that dynamically gives the highest priority to the ready task with the nearest deadline. Periodic tasks meet all deadlines whenever total utilization is at most 1.
a.eax.summary: A two-pass AEAD mode combining counter-mode encryption with OMAC authentication. It uses a single key and was designed to remove practical limitations of CCM.
a.ebcot.summary: An image coding method that divides wavelet subbands into small code blocks, codes each block independently with three coding passes per bit plane and context-based binary arithmetic coding, and then chooses each block's truncation points by rate-distortion optimization to form quality layers. It is the core coding engine of JPEG 2000.
a.ecc.summary: Public-key cryptography that uses the discrete logarithm problem in the group of points on an elliptic curve over a finite field, achieving the same security with shorter keys.
a.ecdsa.o0.title: Proposed in response to the NIST DSS proposal
a.ecdsa.summary: A digital signature scheme that carries DSA over to elliptic curve groups.
a.ecn.summary: A scheme in which routers mark congestion in the IP header instead of dropping packets, and receivers echo the mark back so that senders reduce their rate without loss. It was later standardized as RFC 3168.
a.eddsa.summary: A variant of the Schnorr signature over twisted Edwards curves. Deterministic nonces rule out randomness failures entirely.
a.edge-function-rasterization.summary: A polygon rasterization method that represents each triangle edge as a linear edge function and decides coverage from the signs of the functions at pixel centers. Because edge functions can be evaluated incrementally in screen coordinates, many pixels can be tested in parallel.
a.edmonds-blossom.summary: An algorithm that computes a maximum matching in a general graph in polynomial time by contracting odd-length alternating cycles (blossoms) found during the augmenting-path search into single vertices and expanding them later. It also underlies weighted matching algorithms.
a.edmonds-karp.summary: A maximum-flow algorithm that guarantees O(VE²) time by choosing augmenting paths in Ford–Fulkerson as BFS shortest paths.
a.eertree.summary: A data structure whose nodes are the distinct palindromic substrings of a string, whose edges add the same character to both ends, and whose suffix links point from each node to its longest proper palindromic suffix. It is built online one character at a time, in linear time for a fixed-size alphabet.
a.efficientnet.summary: A compound scaling method that grows network depth, width and input resolution together with a single coefficient, and the CNN family built with it. The baseline B0 model was designed by neural architecture search.
a.eight-point-algorithm.summary: Estimates the essential matrix (or, for uncalibrated cameras, the fundamental matrix) from eight or more point correspondences between two views by solving a linear system. Combined with Hartley's coordinate normalization it becomes numerically stable.
a.eisel-lemire.o0.note: The algorithm is named after Michael Eisel, who wrote the first implementation, and Lemire, the paper's author.
a.eisel-lemire.summary: A string-to-floating-point conversion algorithm that multiplies the decimal significand by precomputed 128-bit approximations of powers of ten, converting most inputs to correctly rounded floats with one or two 64-bit integer multiplications and handing only rare undecidable cases to a slower method.
a.eke.summary: The first password-authenticated key-exchange protocol: ephemeral public-key values such as Diffie–Hellman shares are exchanged encrypted under the shared password, yielding a session key that resists offline dictionary attacks even with a weak password.
a.elastic-net.summary: A regularized regression that combines L1 and L2 penalties. Like the lasso it yields sparse solutions, while tending to select groups of correlated variables together.
a.elgamal.summary: A discrete-logarithm-based public-key scheme that extends Diffie–Hellman key agreement to encryption and signatures.
a.elias-delta.summary: A universal integer code that writes the binary length of an integer with the Elias gamma code, followed by the binary digits without the leading 1. It is shorter than the gamma code for large integers, taking about log2 n + 2 log2 log2 n bits.
a.elias-gamma.summary: A universal integer code that writes a positive integer n as a run of zeros one shorter than its binary length, followed by the binary representation of n. It encodes integers with no known upper bound in about 2 log2 n bits.
a.elkan-k-means.summary: A k-means acceleration that maintains upper and lower bounds on point–center distances via the triangle inequality to skip unnecessary distance computations. It produces the same result as the standard Lloyd algorithm.
a.elman-network.summary: A simple recurrent network that copies the previous hidden state into context units fed back alongside the next input. It is the prototype of the basic RNN layer used today.
a.em.summary: A general algorithm that finds maximum-likelihood estimates from incomplete data by alternating between computing the posterior expectations of latent variables (E) and maximizing over the parameters (M).
a.ensemble-kalman-filter.summary: A Monte Carlo data-assimilation method that, instead of propagating the error covariance directly, advances an ensemble of states through the nonlinear model and performs the Kalman update with the ensemble's sample covariance. It is used for problems with very high state dimension such as weather and ocean forecasting.
a.environment-mapping.summary: A technique that stores the surrounding environment as a texture indexed by direction and approximates mirror reflection by looking up that texture along the surface's reflection vector. It renders reflections without tracing reflected rays.
a.epaxos.summary: A Paxos-family state-machine replication protocol without a fixed leader, in which any replica can propose commands and the dependencies between commands are agreed upon as well, so that non-conflicting commands commit in a single fast-path round.
a.epidemic-gossip.summary: A technique for maintaining replicated data in which each node periodically exchanges updates with randomly chosen peers, spreading information like an epidemic. It covers anti-entropy and rumor mongering, plus death certificates for deletions.
a.epnp.summary: A PnP solver that expresses the 3-D points as weighted sums of four virtual control points and recovers the camera pose from n known 3-D–2-D correspondences in O(n) time.
a.epoch-based-reclamation.summary: A memory-reclamation technique for lock-free data structures that keeps a global epoch counter and per-thread active epochs, and frees a retired node only after every thread has moved past the epoch in which it was retired.
a.eppstein-k-shortest-paths.o0.note: A preliminary version appeared at FOCS 1994.
a.eppstein-k-shortest-paths.summary: An algorithm that lists the k shortest paths, allowing repeated vertices, in O(m + n log n + k) time by organizing the sidetrack edges that leave a shortest-path tree into a heap-structured path graph.
a.eppstein-loffler-strash.summary: A maximal-clique listing algorithm whose outer level follows a degeneracy ordering and whose inner level uses pivoting Bron–Kerbosch. It runs in O(dn3^(d/3)) time on graphs of degeneracy d.
a.euclidean-algorithm.summary: An algorithm that computes the greatest common divisor of two integers by repeatedly replacing the larger number with its remainder modulo the smaller.
a.euler-tour-tree.summary: A dynamic-tree data structure that stores the Euler tour of each tree in a balanced binary search tree and handles edge insertions and deletions by splitting and concatenating tour sequences. It answers connectivity and subtree-aggregate queries in O(log n) time and is used in fully dynamic graph connectivity algorithms.
a.ewa-splatting.summary: A rendering method that treats each point of a point-based surface as an elliptical Gaussian reconstruction kernel and projects and composites it with an elliptical weighted average (EWA) filter combined with a screen-space low-pass filter. It renders textured surfaces from point samples without aliasing.
a.exp-golomb.summary: A variable-length integer code that splits integers into buckets of exponentially growing size, writing the bucket index in unary and the offset within the bucket in fixed length. The order-0 exp-Golomb code is used for syntax elements in H.264/AVC and HEVC bitstreams.
a.expectiminimax.summary: An extension of minimax that inserts chance nodes representing random events between max and min nodes and takes the expected value of the children at chance nodes. Used for games with elements of chance such as dice.
a.exponential-search.summary: A search for unbounded arrays that doubles the search range to find an upper bound and then performs binary search within it.
a.extended-kalman-filter.summary: A nonlinear state estimator that linearizes the nonlinear state-transition and measurement functions with Jacobians around the current estimate and applies the Kalman prediction and update equations. It was developed at NASA Ames Research Center for navigation of a circumlunar vehicle.
a.extendible-hashing.summary: A dynamic hashing scheme made of buckets and a directory indexed by leading hash bits. An overflowing bucket is split on its own, and the directory is doubled only when needed.
a.extra-trees.summary: An ensemble method that grows trees on the full training set, choosing at each node the best among candidate splits whose features and cut-points are both drawn at random.
a.ezw.summary: An embedded image coding method that codes wavelet coefficients bit plane by bit plane from the most significant, representing a coefficient and all its descendants at the same orientation with a single 'zerotree' symbol when they are all below the threshold. The bitstream can be truncated at any point and decoded at the quality reached so far.
a.fabrik.summary: An inverse kinematics solver that moves the end of a joint chain to the target and repeatedly repositions joints along straight lines, first from the end to the root and then from the root to the end, so that bone lengths are preserved. It computes with points and distances only, without rotation angles or matrices.
a.factorization-machines.summary: A general-purpose predictor that models all pairwise feature interactions with factorized weights given by dot products of low-dimensional latent vectors. It can estimate interactions under high sparsity and is computed in linear time.
a.fair-queuing.summary: Packet scheduling that keeps a separate queue per flow (or source) and serves them in turn so that link bandwidth is shared fairly among flows. Demers et al. emulated bit-by-bit round robin to also correct for differing packet lengths.
a.falcon-signature.summary: A lattice-based hash-and-sign signature that samples short lattice vectors over NTRU lattices using fast Fourier sampling. Its public keys and signatures are small, and NIST selected it for standardization under the name FN-DSA.
a.farneback-optical-flow.summary: Dense optical flow estimation that approximates each pixel neighborhood by a quadratic polynomial (polynomial expansion) and derives displacement from how the coefficients change between two frames.
a.fast-corner.summary: A detector that declares a pixel a corner if n contiguous pixels on the 16-pixel circle of radius 3 around it are all sufficiently brighter or darker than the center. A machine-learned decision tree orders the tests, making it very fast.
a.fast-multipole-method.summary: An algorithm that approximates N-body interactions in nearly O(N) time by grouping the influence of distant clusters of particles into multipole and local expansions.
a.fast-rcnn.summary: An object detector that runs the convolutional network once over the whole image, pools per-proposal features with RoI pooling, and trains classification and bounding-box regression jointly.
a.fast-wavelet-transform.summary: A linear-time algorithm that decomposes a signal into multiresolution wavelet coefficients by repeatedly applying low-pass and high-pass filters with downsampling. It is used in image compression (JPEG 2000) and signal denoising.
a.fasta.summary: A heuristic sequence similarity search method that uses a lookup table to find short words (k-tuples) shared by the query and database sequences and scores only the regions concentrated on the same diagonal. It was first presented as FASTP for protein searches.
a.faster-rcnn.summary: An object detector that generates region proposals with a Region Proposal Network sharing the convolutional features and combines it with Fast R-CNN. It removes the need for an external proposal algorithm.
a.fastica.summary: An independent component analysis algorithm that separates independent components by finding, with fixed-point iterations on whitened data, the directions that maximize non-Gaussianity (kurtosis or negentropy approximations).
a.fastpfor.summary: A PFor-family integer compression scheme that gathers exception values per page, grouped by bit width, and bit-packs them separately, with decoding done using SIMD instructions.
a.fasttext.summary: An extension of skip-gram that represents each word as a bag of character n-grams and builds word vectors as sums of n-gram vectors. It can produce vectors for out-of-vocabulary words.
a.fcn.summary: A semantic segmentation network that converts the fully connected layers of a classification network into convolutions and upsamples to produce per-pixel predictions. Skip connections fuse shallow-layer features to recover detail.
a.feldman-vss.summary: A scheme that publishes discrete-log commitments to the coefficients of a Shamir secret-sharing polynomial so that each participant can verify its share non-interactively. It underlies distributed key generation and threshold signatures.
a.felzenszwalb-distance-transform.summar: Computes the distance transform of a function sampled on a grid as the lower envelope of parabolas, in linear time per dimension. Applying it along each dimension in turn yields the exact squared Euclidean distance transform.
a.felzenszwalb-segmentation.summary: Segmentation on a graph whose vertices are pixels and whose edge weights are neighbor differences; it scans edges in increasing weight order and merges regions by comparing internal and between-region differences. It runs in time nearly linear in the number of edges.
a.fenwick-tree.summary: An array-based tree that partitions ranges by the lowest set bit to answer prefix-sum queries and perform point updates in O(log n).
a.fft.o0.note: Origin confirmed by Heideman, Johnson, and Burrus (1984)
a.fft.o0.venue: Unpublished manuscript (included in the 1866 collected works)
a.fft.summary: An algorithm that computes the discrete Fourier transform of length N in O(N log N) by recursively decomposing it into smaller transforms.
a.fiat-shamir.summary: A technique that turns an interactive identification or proof protocol into a non-interactive proof or digital signature by replacing the verifier's random challenge with a hash of the messages exchanged so far. It is used in Schnorr signatures and most modern zero-knowledge proof systems.
a.fibonacci-coding.summary: A universal integer code that writes an integer in its Zeckendorf (Fibonacci) representation, which never has two consecutive 1s, and appends a 1 so that '11' marks the end of each codeword. A bit error affects only a few neighboring codewords.
a.fibonacci-heap.summary: A heap that defers work to support decrease-key in amortized O(1) time. It improved the theoretical bounds of Dijkstra's and Prim's algorithms.
a.fibonacci-search.summary: A search on sorted arrays that narrows the interval at positions given by Fibonacci numbers. Split points are computed with additions and subtractions only, without division.
a.fiduccia-mattheyses.summary: A partition-improvement heuristic that moves one vertex at a time, finding the maximum-gain vertex with a bucket structure, so that each pass takes time linear in the network size. It also applies to hypergraph (netlist) partitioning.
a.finger-tree.o0.note: Volume 16(2) is the 2006 issue; Crossref records 2005, the year of online publication.
a.finger-tree.summary: A purely functional sequence built from 2-3 trees with fingers at both ends. It supports amortized constant-time insertion and deletion at either end and logarithmic-time concatenation and splitting, and uses monoid annotations to implement many other structures.
a.fischer-heun-rmq.summary: A method that splits an array into blocks and lets blocks with the same Cartesian-tree shape share precomputed tables, giving linear preprocessing and constant-time range-minimum queries on general arrays without the ±1 restriction. It is applied to LCA and longest-common-extension (LCE) queries.
a.fisher-yates.o0.note: It was originally presented as a pencil-and-paper procedure for producing random permutations with a table of random numbers.
a.fisher-yates.summary: An algorithm that shuffles an array so that every permutation is equally likely by swapping, from the end, each position i with a random position in 0..i. The in-place O(n) form for computers was published by Durstenfeld.
a.fist.summary: Practical polygon triangulation algorithm that augments ear clipping with geometric hashing and handling of degeneracies and floating-point errors. It also handles polygons with holes.
a.five-point-algorithm.summary: A minimal solver that computes the relative pose between two calibrated cameras from only five point correspondences by finding the roots of a tenth-degree polynomial, yielding up to ten essential-matrix candidates. It is mainly used as a hypothesis generator inside RANSAC.
a.fks-perfect-hashing.summary: A two-level perfect hashing scheme for a static key set: a first-level hash splits the keys into buckets, and each bucket gets a collision-free second-level hash, giving worst-case O(1) lookups in linear space.
a.flajolet-martin.summary: A probabilistic counting method that approximates the number of distinct elements from the trailing zero-bit patterns of hash values.
a.flash-attention-2.summary: An improved FlashAttention that raises GPU utilization by reducing non-matmul operations and parallelizing across the sequence dimension as well.
a.flash-attention.summary: An exact attention implementation that computes attention tile by tile in SRAM and combines the tiles with an online softmax, reducing HBM reads and writes.
a.fletcher-checksum.summary: A checksum that maintains two modular running sums, the sum of the data words and the sum of those sums, so that it detects ordering errors better than a simple sum.
a.flexible-paxos.summary: A generalization of Paxos showing that it remains safe as long as the phase-1 (leader election) quorums intersect the phase-2 (replication) quorums, without either needing to be a majority. Replication quorums can thus be made smaller to reduce latency.
a.floyd-rivest.summary: A selection algorithm that finds the k-th smallest element by narrowing the range with two bounds chosen from a small sample. It uses n + min(k, n-k) + o(n) comparisons on average.
a.floyd-steinberg.summary: Error-diffusion dithering that quantizes each pixel and distributes the quantization error to four right and lower neighbors with weights 7/16, 3/16, 5/16 and 1/16. Widely used to render continuous-tone images with a limited palette.
a.floyd-warshall.summary: An algorithm that computes all-pairs shortest paths by O(V³) dynamic programming, admitting intermediate vertices one at a time.
a.fm-index.summary: A full-text index that combines the BWT with a rank-query structure to count pattern occurrences, while compressed, in time proportional to the pattern length.
a.ford-fulkerson.summary: A maximum-flow method that sends flow along each augmenting path it finds in the residual graph.
a.forney-algorithm.summary: A method that, once the error locations are known, computes the error value at each location directly from the error-evaluator polynomial and the derivative of the error-locator polynomial. It is used in the final step of Reed–Solomon decoding.
a.fortuna.o0.note: Presented in the book's chapter on random number generation as an improved design over Yarrow.
a.fortuna.summary: A cryptographic pseudorandom number generator that collects entropy into 32 pools and draws on them at different rates at each reseed, so it recovers to a secure state without estimating entropy. Designed as an improvement on Yarrow, it is used in the FreeBSD kernel random number generator.
a.fortune.summary: An algorithm that constructs the Voronoi diagram in O(n log n) using a sweep line and a parabolic beach line.
a.fp-growth.summary: An algorithm that compresses transactions into a prefix tree (FP-tree) ordered by item frequency and then recursively mines conditional pattern bases to find frequent patterns without candidate generation.
a.fractional-cascading.summary: A technique for searching the same value in many sorted lists: each list is augmented with a fraction of the elements of the next and linked by pointers, so that after one binary search every further search takes constant time. Searching k lists takes O(log n + k) time.
a.frame-of-reference.summary: An integer compression scheme that stores the minimum (reference value) of each block of values and bit-packs each value's difference from it using the fewest bits needed for the block's range. It allows random access and fast decoding at block granularity and is used in databases and indexes.
a.frank-wolfe.summary: A constrained optimization method that, at each iteration, minimizes a linear approximation of the objective over the feasible set and moves toward that solution. It stays feasible without projections.
a.funk-svd.o0.note: Published as a blog post during the Netflix Prize competition.
a.funk-svd.summary: A recommender matrix factorization that learns user and item latent-factor vectors from the observed ratings only, using regularized stochastic gradient descent, and predicts missing ratings by their dot product.
a.furer.summary: An integer multiplication algorithm that reduces the log log n factor of Schönhage–Strassen to 2^O(log* n) using an FFT over a ring with complex roots of unity.
a.fusion-tree.o0.note: The journal version appeared in Journal of Computer and System Sciences 47(3), 1993.
a.fusion-tree.summary: A B-tree-like integer search structure for the word RAM in which each node packs w^(1/5) keys into a single word and compares them at once. It finds predecessors among n keys in O(log n / log w) time.
a.fxaa.o0.note: The first page is dated February 2009, but the document's change history records 25 January 2011 as the initial release.
a.fxaa.summary: A single-pass post-process anti-aliasing method that detects edge pixels from luminance contrast in the final image, searches along the edge for its endpoints, and resamples with a subpixel offset based on that position to reduce aliasing. Implemented as a single shader, it is inexpensive.
a.g1-gc.summary: A generational, region-based garbage collector that divides the heap into equal-sized regions, estimates the garbage in each by concurrent marking, and evacuates the regions with the most garbage first within a pause-time goal. It is the default collector in Java HotSpot.
a.gabow-scc.summary: A path-based algorithm that finds strongly connected components in linear time by maintaining two stacks during depth-first search: one of vertices and one of path boundaries. The same approach also yields biconnected components.
a.gae.summary: A method that estimates advantages as a sum of temporal-difference residuals weighted by powers of (γλ). The parameter λ trades off the bias and variance of the policy-gradient estimate.
a.gale-shapley.summary: An algorithm that finds a stable matching by having members of one side propose in order of preference while members of the other side tentatively hold only the best proposal received so far. It yields the stable matching that is optimal for the proposing side.
a.galil-rule.summary: A rule for Boyer–Moore search that uses the period of the pattern to avoid re-comparing a part already known to match. It guarantees worst-case linear time even when all occurrences are reported.
a.gan.summary: A generative model based on a minimax game in which a generator learns to fool a discriminator while the discriminator learns to tell real samples from generated ones.
a.garner-crt.summary: A method for the Chinese remainder theorem that recovers an integer from its residues modulo pairwise coprime moduli by computing mixed-radix coefficients one at a time. It is used to combine the results of multi-modular computations into one integer.
a.gat.summary: A graph neural network in which each node computes learned attention coefficients over its neighbors and aggregates their features as a weighted sum. Multiple attention heads are used together.
a.gauss-seidel.summary: An iterative method for linear systems that updates the unknowns one by one, immediately using the values already updated. It converges for diagonally dominant or symmetric positive-definite matrices and is used as a smoother in multigrid.
a.gaussian-splatting.o0.note: It was also released the same year as arXiv:2308.04079.
a.gaussian-splatting.summary: A method that represents a scene as many 3D Gaussians with position, covariance, opacity and spherical-harmonic color, and renders and optimizes them by differentiable rasterization that projects them to the screen, sorts them by depth per tile and alpha-composites them. It renders radiance fields at real-time rates without a neural network.
a.gcm-siv.summary: An AEAD scheme that combines GCM's polynomial hash with the SIV approach for nonce-misuse resistance. Confidentiality degrades gracefully when a nonce repeats, and it was standardized as RFC 8452.
a.gcm.summary: An AEAD scheme combining counter-mode encryption with an authentication tag computed by a polynomial hash over GF(2^128) (GHASH). It is widely used with AES in TLS, IPsec and SSH.
a.gcn.summary: A graph neural network that stacks layers aggregating neighbor features through a normalized adjacency matrix followed by a linear transform. It was derived as a first-order approximation of spectral graph convolutions.
a.gelu.summary: The activation function x·Φ(x), which multiplies the input by the standard normal cumulative distribution function. It is widely used in Transformer models such as BERT and GPT.
a.general-number-field-sieve.summary: A factorization algorithm that extends the number field sieve from integers of special form to arbitrary integers. It is the fastest known classical method for integers beyond roughly 100 digits and underlies RSA key-length estimates.
a.generational-gc.summary: A garbage collector that, based on the hypothesis that most objects die young, collects the young generation frequently and the old generation rarely.
a.gentry-fhe.summary: The first fully homomorphic encryption scheme, supporting unlimited additions and multiplications by adding bootstrapping (homomorphically evaluating its own decryption circuit to reduce noise) to an ideal-lattice somewhat homomorphic scheme.
a.geohash.summary: Geographic coordinate encoding that interleaves the bits obtained by alternately halving the latitude and longitude ranges and writes them as a base-32 string. A longer shared prefix means a nearby area, so proximity queries can be done with prefix searches.
a.ggx.summary: A normal distribution function that models microfacet normals as distributed like the surface of an ellipsoid of revolution; its longer tail than the Beckmann distribution reproduces the gradual falloff around highlights. Walter et al. presented it under the name GGX in a microfacet model that includes refraction, and Trowbridge and Reitz had published the same distribution earlier.
a.gibbs-sampling.summary: An MCMC method that samples each variable in turn from its conditional distribution with all other variables held fixed.
a.gicp.summary: ICP variant that models the error of each correspondence probabilistically using local covariances around the points. It contains point-to-point and point-to-plane ICP as special cases and takes the local planar structure of both surfaces into account.
a.gillespie-algorithm.o0.note: The 1977 J. Phys. Chem. paper 'Exact stochastic simulation of coupled chemical reactions', which restates the direct method, is widely cited.
a.gillespie-algorithm.summary: A stochastic simulation algorithm that, from the propensity of each reaction, draws the time to the next reaction and which reaction occurs, producing sample trajectories that exactly follow the chemical master equation.
a.girvan-newman.summary: A divisive method that finds hierarchical community structure by repeatedly removing the edge with the highest edge betweenness and splitting the graph.
a.gist.summary: An index structure that lets the meaning of keys be defined by a few extension methods such as Consistent, Union, Penalty and PickSplit, so that B+-trees, R-trees and others can be implemented within one balanced-tree framework. PostgreSQL's GiST indexes follow this design.
a.givens-rotation.summary: A plane rotation that zeroes one matrix entry at a time. It is used for QR factorization, for updating sparse or structured matrices, and inside eigenvalue algorithms.
a.gjk.summary: An algorithm that computes the distance and collision between two convex bodies by iteratively testing, with simplices, whether their Minkowski difference contains the origin.
a.gk-quantile-summary.summary: A deterministic quantile summary that maintains tuples of values and rank-range information over a stream, answering any quantile query within an error of εN.
a.glove.summary: A word-embedding method trained by weighted least-squares regression so that dot products of word vectors fit the logarithms of global word co-occurrence counts.
a.glr.summary: Generalized LR parsing that, when the LR table has conflicts, forks the stack to follow all possibilities in parallel while sharing common parts in a graph-structured stack, handling ambiguous or nondeterministic context-free grammars.
a.glu.summary: A gating layer that multiplies one linear projection of the input elementwise by the sigmoid of another. It was introduced in gated convolutional language models.
a.glushkov-construction.summary: A construction that creates an ε-free NFA with one state per symbol position in a regular expression, defining transitions from the first, last and follow relations between positions. The number of states is one more than the number of symbol occurrences in the expression.
a.gmres.summary: An iterative method for nonsymmetric linear systems that selects, within a Krylov subspace built by the Arnoldi process, the iterate minimizing the residual norm. The restarted variant GMRES(m) is widely used.
a.goertzel.summary: An algorithm that computes a single frequency component of the DFT with a second-order recursive filter. It is used when only a few frequencies are needed, as in DTMF tone detection in telephony.
a.goldberg-radzik.summary: A single-source shortest-path algorithm that improves Bellman–Ford by scanning, in each pass, the relevant vertices in a topological order of the admissible-edge graph. It allows negative weights and keeps the O(VE) worst-case bound.
a.golden-section-search.summary: A one-dimensional search for the extremum of a unimodal function that compares function values at two points dividing the interval in the golden ratio, shrinking the interval by a constant factor each step. It is the limiting form of Fibonacci search.
a.goldwasser-micali.summary: The first probabilistic public-key cryptosystem, encrypting one bit at a time based on the quadratic residuosity problem. Semantic security was first defined and proved together with this scheme.
a.golomb-coding.summary: An entropy code that represents an integer, given a positive parameter m, as a quotient in unary and a remainder in truncated binary. It is near-optimal for geometrically distributed run lengths and prediction residuals.
a.golub-kahan-bidiagonalization.summary: A method that reduces a matrix to bidiagonal form by applying orthogonal transformations from both sides. It is the basis of SVD computation and of least-squares iterative methods such as LSQR.
a.golub-reinsch-svd.summary: An SVD algorithm that first bidiagonalizes the matrix with Householder transformations and then computes the singular values by shifted QR iteration. It is the classical standard for dense SVD.
a.golub-welsch.summary: An algorithm that computes the nodes and weights of Gaussian quadrature from the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the symmetric tridiagonal (Jacobi) matrix formed from the three-term recurrence of the orthogonal polynomials.
a.gomory-hu-tree.summary: A method that builds, with n−1 maximum-flow computations, a weighted tree encoding the minimum cut values between all pairs of vertices of an undirected graph; the smallest edge weight on the tree path between two vertices equals their minimum cut value.
a.good-thomas-fft.summary: An FFT algorithm that, when the length is a product of coprime factors, reindexes the data via the Chinese remainder theorem to turn the DFT into a multidimensional DFT without twiddle-factor multiplications.
a.googlenet.summary: A 22-layer convolutional network built by stacking Inception modules that run 1×1, 3×3 and 5×5 convolutions and pooling in parallel. It won the ILSVRC 2014 classification task.
a.gorilla.summary: A compression scheme for time series that encodes timestamps as delta-of-deltas and floating-point values as variable-length bit strings based on the leading and trailing zero counts of their XOR with the previous value. Proposed for Facebook's in-memory time series database Gorilla, it is used by many time series databases such as Prometheus.
a.gotoh.summary: An algorithm that computes sequence alignment under affine gap scores, with separate costs for opening and extending a gap, in O(mn) time using three dynamic programming matrices. It reduced the cubic time of the earlier method with general gap functions to quadratic.
a.gouraud-shading.summary: A technique that shades curved surfaces smoothly by linearly interpolating intensities computed at the vertices across the polygon interior.
a.gpt.summary: A language model that generatively pretrains a Transformer decoder on next-token prediction and then fine-tunes it for each task.
a.grabcut.summary: Foreground extraction that estimates foreground and background color distributions with Gaussian mixture models inside a user-drawn rectangle and iterates graph-cut segmentation. It cuts out objects with minimal user input.
a.grace-hash-join.summary: A join algorithm that partitions both relations by a hash of the join key into buckets small enough to fit in memory and then hash-joins each pair of corresponding buckets. It is used for joining relations larger than memory.
a.gradient-boosting.summary: Boosting by gradient descent in function space, sequentially fitting weak learners to the negative gradient (pseudo-residuals) of the loss function and adding them.
a.gradient-descent.summary: An optimization method that finds a minimum by repeatedly moving in the direction opposite to the gradient of the objective function.
a.graham-scan.summary: An algorithm that computes the convex hull in O(n log n) by sorting points by polar angle about the lowest point and then using a stack to eliminate right turns.
a.gram-schmidt.summary: A procedure that builds an orthonormal basis by successively subtracting from each vector its components along the previously constructed orthogonal vectors. It underlies QR factorization and the orthogonalization step of Krylov subspace methods.
a.graph-cut-segmentation.summary: Interactive binary segmentation that treats user-marked foreground and background seeds as hard constraints and finds the minimum cut of a graph built from regional and boundary costs. A max-flow algorithm yields the globally optimal solution.
a.graphsage.summary: An inductive graph neural network that learns functions which sample neighbors and aggregate their features with mean, LSTM or pooling aggregators, so it can embed nodes unseen during training.
a.greiner-hormann.summary: Polygon clipping algorithm that inserts the intersection points of two polygons into each polygon's linked vertex list, marks every intersection as entry or exit, and then traces the lists to extract the result. It handles self-intersecting polygons, and simple modifications yield union and difference.
a.grid-file.summary: A file structure that divides a multidimensional key space into grid cells using per-axis interval boundaries (scales) and maps the cells to disk buckets through a directory. Exact-match queries need two disk accesses.
a.grisu.summary: An algorithm that converts floating-point numbers to short decimal representations quickly using only precomputed approximations of powers of ten and extended-precision arithmetic on 64-bit integers. Grisu3 detects the roughly 0.5% of inputs for which shortness cannot be guaranteed and hands them to a slower method.
a.groth16.summary: A pairing-based zk-SNARK whose proofs consist of only three group elements. It needs a per-circuit trusted setup, but verification takes only a few pairings, and it is widely used for zero-knowledge proofs in blockchains such as Zcash.
a.group-norm.summary: A normalization that divides channels into groups and normalizes by the mean and variance within each group of each sample. It is independent of batch size, so it works with small batches.
a.grouped-query-attention.summary: A generalization between multi-head and multi-query attention that groups query heads and shares keys and values within each group.
a.gru.summary: A simplified recurrent unit that learns long-term dependencies comparably to LSTM using only two gates, update and reset.
a.guibas-stolfi-delaunay.summary: Algorithm that defines the quad-edge data structure for planar subdivisions and its primitive operations, and uses them to build the Delaunay triangulation (Voronoi diagram) by divide and conquer in O(n log n) time. Its only geometric predicates are the orientation (CCW) and InCircle tests.
a.guided-filter.summary: An edge-preserving filter that computes the output as a local linear model of a guidance image. It is computed with box filters only, running in O(N) time regardless of kernel size.
a.gusfield.summary: A method that computes a Gomory–Hu tree, as well as an equivalent flow tree, with n−1 maximum-flow computations on the original graph without node contractions. Libraries such as NetworkX and JGraphT use it to compute Gomory–Hu trees.
a.h3.summary: Hierarchical geospatial indexing system that projects the Earth onto the faces of an icosahedron, tiles it with hexagonal (and a few pentagonal) cells, and subdivides so that each finer resolution has cells of about one seventh the area. Each cell is identified by a 64-bit integer index.
a.halley-method.summary: A root-finding method that uses the function value together with its first and second derivatives, converging cubically near a simple root.
a.halton-sequence.summary: A multidimensional low-discrepancy sequence that assigns a distinct prime base to each dimension and uses as coordinates the radical inverse of the index, its base-b digits mirrored about the radix point. It extends the van der Corput sequence to many dimensions.
a.hamming-code.summary: A linear block code that adds parity-check bits, indexed by binary positions, to the data bits so that the position of a single-bit error can be located and corrected. The extended form also detects double-bit errors.
a.hamming-distance.summary: The number of positions at which the corresponding symbols of two equal-length strings differ. It was introduced as the minimum-distance notion for error-detecting and error-correcting codes.
a.hamt.summary: A trie that uses successive chunks of a key's hash as the index at each level and represents each node as a bitmap plus a compact array holding only the children that exist. It is used for immutable hash maps in languages such as Clojure and Scala.
a.hardware-transactional-memory.summary: A hardware synchronization mechanism that extends the cache-coherence protocol so that reads and writes to multiple memory locations execute as a single atomic transaction that aborts on conflict. It was proposed to make lock-free data structures easier to build.
a.harel-tarjan-lca.summary: An algorithm that preprocesses a tree in linear time so that the lowest common ancestor (LCA) of any two nodes can be found in constant time. It decomposes the tree into paths to reduce the problem to LCA computation in complete binary trees, and was the first to achieve these bounds.
a.harris-corner.summary: Detects corners as points where intensity changes strongly in both directions, using the response det(M) − k·trace(M)² of the second-moment (structure tensor) matrix M of local gradients.
a.harris-linked-list.summary: A lock-free sorted linked list that first logically deletes a node by setting a mark bit in its next pointer and then physically unlinks it with compare-and-swap (CAS).
a.harvey-van-der-hoeven.summary: An algorithm that multiplies integers in O(n log n) using multidimensional FFT techniques, attaining the bound of a long-standing conjecture.
a.hash-chaining.o0.title: IBM internal memo (chained hashing)
a.hash-chaining.o0.venue: Cited as the origin in Knuth, TAOCP Vol. 3 §6.4
a.hash-chaining.summary: A hash table that selects a bucket with a hash function and links colliding keys in a linked list.
a.hazard-pointers.o0.note: The journal version titled with the name 'hazard pointers' is IEEE TPDS 15(6), 2004 (doi:10.1109/TPDS.2004.8).
a.hazard-pointers.summary: A memory-reclamation technique for lock-free data structures in which each thread publishes the addresses of nodes it is accessing in shared hazard pointers, and a node is freed only when no hazard pointer refers to it.
a.hdbscan.summary: An algorithm that builds a hierarchy of density-based clusters over the mutual reachability distance and extracts a flat clustering by selecting the most stable clusters. It finds clusters of differing density without DBSCAN's ε parameter.
a.he-init.summary: An initialization that sets the weight variance to 2/n_in for layers with ReLU-family activations. The same paper also introduced PReLU, a rectifier with a learnable negative slope.
a.heapsort.o0.note: In the same year, R. W. Floyd improved heap construction in Algorithm 245 Treesort 3
a.heapsort.summary: An in-place sort that builds a binary heap and repeatedly extracts the maximum. It runs in O(n log n) worst-case time.
a.heavy-path-decomposition.summary: A technique that calls an edge heavy when the child's subtree holds more than half of its parent's subtree, partitioning the tree into heavy paths. Every node-to-root path contains only O(log n) light edges, so path queries reduce to a few interval queries.
a.heckel-diff.summary: A linear-time algorithm that finds differences by pairing, as anchors, lines that occur exactly once in each of the two files and then extending matches around them. It also detects block moves and is used in diff libraries for updating UI lists, among others.
a.held-karp.summary: An exact dynamic-programming algorithm for the traveling salesman problem that computes an optimal tour in O(n²·2ⁿ) time, using as states the minimum cost of a path that starts at the origin, visits every vertex of a set S, and ends at a vertex v.
a.hertel-mehlhorn.summary: Approximation algorithm that obtains a convex partition of a simple polygon by successively removing diagonals of a triangulation whose removal keeps the merged pieces convex. The number of pieces is at most four times the optimum.
a.hierholzer.o0.note: Published after Hierholzer's death in 1871 from his manuscript, communicated by Chr. Wiener; the Crossref metadata also lists Wiener as an author.
a.hierholzer.summary: An algorithm that constructs an Eulerian circuit in linear time by starting from a vertex, following unused edges to form a closed trail, and repeatedly splicing in new closed trails started from vertices on the trail that still have unused edges.
a.hight.summary: A lightweight 64-bit block cipher developed in Korea for low-power, resource-constrained devices. It uses a 128-bit key and is a generalized Feistel network built only from 8-bit addition, rotation and XOR.
a.highway-hierarchies.summary: A route-planning technique that exploits the property that, away from the source and target, shortest paths in road networks use only highway-like edges; preprocessing builds a hierarchy of highway networks on which exact shortest-path queries are answered quickly with bidirectional search.
a.highway-network.summary: A network architecture whose learned transform and carry gates decide how much of the input passes unchanged to the next layer. It made networks hundreds of layers deep directly trainable with gradient descent.
a.hilbert-curve.summary: Space-filling curve obtained by dividing a square into four cells and recursively subdividing each with a rotated or reflected copy of the same pattern. Because points close on the curve are also close in the plane, it is used in indexes that order multidimensional data along one dimension.
a.hilbert-r-tree.summary: An R-tree variant that orders entries by the Hilbert-curve value of their rectangle centers when placing them in nodes. The ordering allows B+-tree-like deferred splitting, in which entries are shared with sibling nodes, raising space utilization.
a.hindley-milner.summary: A method that assigns type variables to an unannotated program, solves the constraints by unification and generalizes types at let-bindings, inferring the most general type while allowing parametric polymorphism. Algorithm W is its classic implementation.
a.hirschberg.summary: A divide-and-conquer algorithm that computes the longest-common-subsequence dynamic program forward on one half and backward on the other, finds the optimal split point and recurses on both sides. It keeps quadratic time while reducing space to linear.
a.history-heuristic.summary: A move-ordering technique that accumulates depth-dependent scores for moves that caused cutoffs or were best during search and tries high-scoring moves first in other positions. It improves the pruning efficiency of alpha–beta.
a.hits.summary: A link analysis algorithm that computes hub and authority scores through mutually reinforcing iteration.
a.hkdf.summary: A key derivation function that uses HMAC to concentrate the entropy of input keying material in an extract step and then produces keys of the required length in an expand step. It is used in TLS 1.3, Signal and WireGuard and standardized as RFC 5869.
a.hmac.summary: A construction that builds a message authentication code by wrapping a hash function twice, with an inner and an outer key.
a.hmc.summary: An MCMC method that introduces auxiliary momentum variables, simulates Hamiltonian dynamics with leapfrog integration and proposes the trajectory endpoint, which is accepted by the Metropolis criterion. In high-dimensional continuous distributions it moves farther than random-walk proposals.
a.hnsw.summary: A graph-based index that stacks multiple layers of proximity graphs, each element appearing up to a randomly chosen top layer, and finds approximate nearest neighbors by descending greedily from the top layer. It is widely used in vector search libraries and databases.
a.hog.summary: A feature descriptor that divides an image into small cells, builds a histogram of gradient orientations per cell, normalizes them over overlapping blocks, and concatenates the results. It was proposed for pedestrian detection together with a linear SVM.
a.hollow-heap.summary: A heap in which decrease-key creates a new node instead of moving the old one, leaving the original as an empty (hollow) node. Using lazy deletion and a DAG structure, it obtains the amortized bounds of Fibonacci heaps.
a.hopcroft-karp.summary: An algorithm that finds a maximum matching in a bipartite graph in O(E√V) time by repeatedly building a layered graph of shortest augmenting paths with BFS and augmenting along a maximal set of vertex-disjoint shortest paths found with DFS.
a.hopcroft-minimization.summary: An algorithm that obtains the minimal DFA in O(n log n) time by iteratively refining a partition of the states, using only the smaller of each pair of split blocks as the next splitter. Here n is the number of states, and the bound assumes a fixed-size alphabet.
a.hopcroft-tarjan-bcc.o0.note: The paper that presented a biconnected-components algorithm together with the strongly connected components algorithm.
a.hopcroft-tarjan-bcc.summary: A linear-time algorithm that finds the articulation points and biconnected components of an undirected graph using depth-first discovery order and low values.
a.hopcroft-tarjan-planarity.summary: A linear-time algorithm that decides whether a graph can be drawn in the plane without crossings by splitting it into paths with depth-first search and embedding them one at a time.
a.hopcroft-tarjan-triconnected.summary: A linear-time algorithm based on depth-first search that divides a biconnected graph into triconnected components along its separation pairs.
a.hopfield-network.summary: A recurrent network of binary neurons with symmetric weights that update asynchronously so as to lower an energy function. Stored patterns act as attractors, giving a content-addressable associative memory.
a.hopscotch-hashing.summary: An open-addressing hash table that keeps every element within a fixed neighborhood of its home bucket by moving empty slots closer. Neighborhoods are tracked with bitmaps, and the design targets concurrent implementations.
a.hormann-agathos-pip.summary: Algorithm that counts ray–edge crossings together with their direction to obtain the winding number of a point with respect to an arbitrary, possibly self-intersecting polygon. It handles the even–odd rule and the winding-number rule in one framework.
a.horn-quaternion.summary: Closed-form solution of the absolute orientation problem, recovering the rotation, translation and scale between two coordinate systems from corresponding points, by taking as the unit quaternion the eigenvector of a 4x4 symmetric matrix that belongs to its largest eigenvalue.
a.horn-schunck.summary: Computes optical flow at every pixel by variationally minimizing an energy that combines the brightness-constancy constraint with a global smoothness term on the flow field. It obtains a dense flow field through iterative computation.
a.horner-method.o0.note: The same scheme was used earlier, for example by Ruffini (1809) and by Qin Jiushao in 13th-century China.
a.horner-method.summary: A method that rewrites a polynomial in nested form so that a degree-n polynomial is evaluated with n multiplications and n additions. The original paper used it to solve equations numerically.
a.horspool.summary: A practical string search that simplifies Boyer–Moore by keeping only the bad-character rule.
a.hotp.summary: A one-time password algorithm that truncates the HMAC-SHA-1 of a shared secret key and an incrementing counter into a 6- to 8-digit number. It underlies hardware tokens and authenticator apps and is the basis of TOTP.
a.hotstuff.summary: A leader-based BFT consensus protocol that commits blocks by chaining quorum certificates of votes collected by the leader. Its communication cost on leader replacement is linear in the number of nodes, and its phases can be pipelined.
a.hough-transform.o0.note: Recasts the line-detection idea of Hough's 1962 patent in the (ρ, θ) parameterization and extends it to curves such as circles.
a.hough-transform.summary: A detection method in which each edge point votes for all line (or curve) parameters passing through it, and shapes are found as peaks in the accumulator array. Duda and Hart represented lines with the normal (ρ, θ) parameterization.
a.householder-qr.summary: A QR factorization that reduces a matrix to upper-triangular form by applying a sequence of Householder reflections. Being numerically stable, it is the standard QR method in libraries such as LAPACK.
a.hpke.summary: A hybrid public-key encryption standard that encapsulates a shared secret with a KEM, derives keys with a KDF and encrypts messages with an AEAD. It supports sender-authenticated and pre-shared-key modes and is used in TLS ECH and MLS.
a.hu-tucker.summary: An algorithm that, under the constraint that symbol order is preserved, finds a binary tree with minimum weighted path length, that is, an optimal alphabetic code. It is the order-preserving counterpart of Huffman coding and also builds optimal search trees whose weights lie on the leaves.
a.huffman.summary: A greedy algorithm that builds a prefix code of minimum average code length by repeatedly merging the two least frequent symbols.
a.hungarian.summary: An algorithm based on the theorems of Kőnig and Egerváry that solves minimum-cost perfect matching in bipartite graphs (the assignment problem) in polynomial time.
a.hunt-szymanski.summary: An algorithm that computes the longest common subsequence quickly on inputs with few matches by processing only pairs of matching positions.
a.hybrid-hash-join.summary: A join algorithm that partitions relations by hashing as in the GRACE hash join but keeps the hash table of the first partition in memory and joins it immediately during partitioning, reducing disk I/O.
a.hybrid-logical-clock.summary: A clock that combines physical clock values with a logical counter, producing timestamps that preserve causality while staying close to physical time. Its divergence from physical time is bounded by the clock-synchronization error.
a.hyperloglog-pp.summary: An improved HyperLogLog that adds 64-bit hashes, bias correction for small cardinalities, and a sparse representation.
a.hyperloglog.summary: A cardinality estimation algorithm that combines LogLog registers with a harmonic mean to reduce the standard error.
a.hystart.summary: A method that watches ACK-train spacing and RTT increases during slow start to find the point at which to leave slow start before losses occur. It is included in the Linux CUBIC implementation.
a.icp.o1.note: Independently proposed the same iterative registration, minimizing point-to-tangent-plane distances (point-to-plane).
a.icp.summary: Registration algorithm that matches every point of one point cloud to its closest point on the other cloud (or surface), computes the rigid transformation minimizing the sum of squared distances between the pairs, applies it, and repeats until convergence.
a.id3.summary: An algorithm that builds a decision tree by recursively splitting each node on the attribute with the highest information gain.
a.ida-star.summary: A search that repeats depth-first search with a gradually increasing bound on f = g + h, achieving the optimality of A* with linear memory.
a.idea.o0.note: First proposed under the name IPES (Improved PES) and later renamed IDEA.
a.idea.summary: A block cipher with 64-bit blocks and a 128-bit key. Its rounds mix three algebraically incompatible operations: XOR, addition modulo 2^16 and multiplication modulo 2^16+1.
a.ifds.summary: An analysis framework that turns interprocedural dataflow problems with distributive transfer functions over a finite set of facts into reachability along realizable paths in an exploded supergraph, solving them precisely in polynomial time.
a.immix.summary: A mark-region garbage collector that divides the heap into blocks and smaller lines, marks lines containing live objects, bump-allocates into free lines, and opportunistically evacuates fragmented blocks to defragment.
a.implicit-als.summary: A recommendation method that converts implicit feedback such as clicks or views into binary preferences with confidence weights and solves a weighted least-squares factorization of the full user–item matrix by alternating least squares.
a.implicitly-restarted-arnoldi.summary: An eigenvalue method that restarts an Arnoldi factorization at fixed size by implicitly applying shifted QR steps, filtering out unwanted eigen-directions. It is the core algorithm of ARPACK.
a.importance-sampling.summary: A Monte Carlo variance-reduction technique that draws samples from a tractable proposal distribution instead of the target and estimates expectations by weighting each sample with the ratio of the two densities.
a.improved-perlin-noise.summary: A revision of the original Perlin noise that reduces its artifacts using a quintic interpolation function and a fixed set of gradients.
a.infomap.summary: A community-detection method that finds the partition minimizing the expected description length (the map equation) of a random walk encoded with a two-level, module-based code.
a.insertion-sort.summary: A sort that inserts elements one at a time into the sorted prefix. It is fast on nearly sorted input and serves as the small-subarray stage of many hybrid sorts.
a.instance-norm.summary: A normalization that computes the mean and variance over spatial dimensions separately for each channel of each sample. It was proposed to replace batch normalization in style-transfer generator networks.
a.instant-ngp.o0.note: It was also released the same year as arXiv:2201.05989.
a.instant-ngp.summary: A multiresolution hash encoding that maps input coordinates onto grids at several resolutions, stores trainable feature vectors for grid vertices in hash tables, and feeds the interpolated features into a small neural network. It reduced the training of neural graphics primitives such as NeRF to seconds.
a.interpolation-search.summary: A search that assumes a distribution of key values and chooses the next probe position by linear interpolation. It takes O(log log n) on average for uniformly distributed keys.
a.introselect.summary: A selection algorithm that starts as quickselect and switches to an algorithm with a guaranteed worst-case bound when partitioning makes too little progress. It is used to implement std::nth_element in libstdc++.
a.introsort.summary: A hybrid sort that starts with quicksort and switches to heapsort when the recursion depth exceeds a limit, guaranteeing O(n log n) worst-case time.
a.ips4o.summary: A comparison-based sort that makes Super Scalar Samplesort in-place through block-wise distribution and extends it to run in parallel on multiple threads.
a.isolation-forest.summary: An anomaly-detection method that builds many trees recursively splitting the data on random features and random split values, scoring points as anomalous when the average path length needed to isolate them is short.
a.isomap.summary: A nonlinear dimensionality-reduction technique that approximates geodesic distances on the manifold by shortest paths in a neighborhood graph and then applies classical MDS to obtain low-dimensional coordinates.
a.iterated-register-coalescing.summary: A register-allocation algorithm for graph coloring that interleaves simplification with conservative coalescing so that as many move instructions as possible are eliminated without hurting colorability.
a.jacobi-eigenvalue.summary: A method for symmetric matrices that repeatedly applies plane rotations to drive the off-diagonal entries toward zero, yielding eigenvalues and eigenvectors. Variants include the one-sided Jacobi SVD.
a.jacobi-method.summary: An iterative method for linear systems that updates all unknowns simultaneously using only the previous iterate, dividing by the diagonal entries. It converges for diagonally dominant matrices and also serves as a smoother in multigrid.
a.jacobson-rtt-estimator.summary: A method that updates a smoothed mean and mean deviation of round-trip-time samples with exponentially weighted moving averages and sets the retransmission timeout (RTO) from their sum. It underlies the TCP RTO computation of RFC 6298.
a.jaro-similarity.summary: A measure that scores the similarity of two strings between 0 and 1 from the number of characters matching within a window and the number of transpositions among them. It was devised for comparing names in census record linkage.
a.jaro-winkler.summary: A measure that adds to the Jaro similarity a bonus proportional to the length of the common prefix of the two strings, up to four characters. It rates names that agree at the beginning as more similar and is widely used in record linkage.
a.jarvis-judice-ninke.summary: Error-diffusion dithering that spreads the quantization error over 12 neighboring pixels across the current row and the next two rows. Its wider kernel than Floyd–Steinberg yields smoother patterns at a higher computational cost.
a.jarvis-march.summary: An output-sensitive convex hull algorithm that, from the current vertex, selects as the next vertex the point with all other points on one side.
a.jenkins-traub.summary: A polynomial root-finding algorithm that finds roots one at a time with a three-stage variable-shift iteration and deflates the polynomial. Its implementations RPOLY for real and CPOLY for complex coefficients have been widely used.
a.johnson-cycles.summary: An algorithm that lists all elementary circuits of a directed graph in O((n+e)(c+1)) time, where c is the number of circuits, by fixing start vertices in turn and maintaining blocking marks.
a.johnson.summary: An all-pairs shortest-path algorithm that computes vertex potentials with Bellman–Ford, reweights the edges to be nonnegative, and then runs Dijkstra's algorithm from every vertex.
a.jonker-volgenant.summary: A linear assignment algorithm that builds an initial assignment with column reduction and augmenting row reduction, then completes it by finding Dijkstra-like shortest augmenting paths for the remaining rows. It applies to both dense and sparse cost matrices.
a.jpeg.summary: The baseline method of the lossy still-image compression standard, which divides an image into 8×8 blocks, applies the discrete cosine transform (DCT), quantizes the coefficients with a quantization table, and entropy-codes them in zigzag order with run lengths and Huffman codes.
a.jump-consistent-hash.summary: A hash that consistently assigns keys to n buckets with a few lines of arithmetic and no storage.
a.jump-point-search.summary: A technique that speeds up A* on uniform-cost grids by pruning symmetric paths and expanding only jump points.
a.jump-search.summary: Searches a sorted array by jumping ahead in fixed steps (typically √n) to find the block that contains the target, then scanning that block sequentially.
a.k-means-pp.summary: A k-means initialization that picks each subsequent initial center with probability proportional to its squared distance from the existing centers, guaranteeing an O(log k) approximation.
a.k-means.o1.venue: Bell Labs technical memo (published in IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 28(2), 1982)
a.k-means.summary: A clustering method that repeatedly assigns each point to its nearest center and moves each center to the mean of its assigned points.
a.k-nearest-neighbors.o0.note: Circulated as a USAF School of Aviation Medicine technical report and reprinted in International Statistical Review in 1989.
a.k-nearest-neighbors.summary: A nonparametric method that predicts a new sample's label by majority vote (or the average, for regression) over its k closest training samples. It has no training phase beyond storing the data.
a.kabsch.summary: Method that computes, in closed form from the correlation matrix of two corresponding sets of vectors (points), the rotation matrix that minimizes the weighted sum of squared distances between them. It is used for RMSD computation when comparing molecular structures.
a.kahan-summation.summary: A summation method that reduces accumulated rounding error by collecting the low-order part lost in each floating-point addition in a separate compensation variable and feeding it back into the next addition.
a.kalman-bucy-filter.summary: The continuous-time optimal filter that formulates the Kalman filter for linear stochastic systems in continuous time, with the error covariance governed by a Riccati differential equation.
a.kalman-filter.summary: An optimal recursive estimator for linear Gaussian state-space models that alternates a prediction step and a measurement update to compute the state estimate and its error covariance. It is widely used in navigation, tracking, control and signal processing.
a.kangarootwelve.summary: An extendable-output hash function that reduces the Keccak permutation to 12 rounds and adds tree hashing. It is faster than SHA-3 and can process long inputs in parallel.
a.karatsuba.summary: The first subquadratic multiplication algorithm, which reduces the product of two n-digit numbers to three n/2-digit products and runs in O(n^1.585).
a.karger-stein.summary: A randomized algorithm that finds a global minimum cut with high probability in Õ(n²) time by contracting random edges until about n/√2 vertices remain and then recursing twice independently.
a.karmarkar.summary: A polynomial-time interior-point method for linear programming that is efficient in practice, using projective transformations and an interior path.
a.karn-algorithm.summary: An RTT estimation rule that takes no RTT sample from the ACK of a retransmitted segment and keeps the backed-off timeout until a fresh sample is obtained. It avoids the bias caused by retransmission ambiguity.
a.karney-geodesic.summary: Algorithm that solves the direct and inverse geodesic problems on an ellipsoid of revolution using series expanded to arbitrary order together with Newton's method. It converges for all inputs, including nearly antipodal points, and is implemented in GeographicLib.
a.karp-min-mean-cycle.summary: An algorithm that computes the minimum cycle mean of a directed graph in O(nm) time by finding, with dynamic programming, the minimum weight of walks with exactly k edges and applying a closed-form characterization.
a.kasai-lcp.summary: An algorithm that computes, from a string and its suffix array, the array of longest-common-prefix (LCP) lengths between adjacent suffixes in linear time. It scans suffixes in text order and uses the fact that the LCP value decreases by at most one from the previous suffix.
a.katz-centrality.summary: A centrality index that rates a vertex's status by summing all walks reaching it, weighting each walk of length k by the k-th power of an attenuation factor.
a.kcf-tracker.summary: A correlation-filter tracking method that exploits the circulant structure of translated samples to diagonalize a kernel ridge regression tracker in the Fourier domain, enabling fast training.
a.kd-tree.summary: A multidimensional binary search tree that bisects space along alternating coordinate axes. It is used for nearest-neighbor and range queries.
a.kdb-tree.summary: A multidimensional disk index that combines the space partitioning of k-d trees with the balanced, paged structure of B-trees. All leaves lie at the same depth and each node corresponds to one disk page.
a.kerberos.summary: An authentication protocol that adds timestamps to the Needham–Schroeder symmetric-key protocol and provides single sign-on to network services through tickets issued by an authentication server and a ticket-granting server. It was developed at MIT's Project Athena and is used in Windows Active Directory and elsewhere.
a.kernel-density-estimation.summary: A nonparametric method that estimates a probability density by placing a kernel function at each sample and normalizing their sum. The bandwidth controls the smoothness of the estimate.
a.kernel-pca.summary: A nonlinear dimensionality-reduction technique that performs principal component analysis in a high-dimensional feature space defined implicitly by a kernel function. It is computed as an eigenvalue problem of the kernel matrix.
a.kernighan-lin.summary: A graph-bisection heuristic that reduces the cost of edges crossing the partition by repeating passes in which the vertex pair with the largest swap gain between the two parts is exchanged in turn.
a.keys-cubic-convolution.summary: Interpolates values by applying a piecewise cubic polynomial kernel to the surrounding 4×4 pixels. Keys showed that the kernel with parameter a = −0.5 is third-order accurate, and the bicubic interpolation in many imaging libraries uses this kernel family.
a.kildall-dataflow.summary: A general framework for global dataflow analysis that keeps a lattice value at each program point and repeatedly applies transfer functions and meet operations from a worklist until a fixed point is reached.
a.kirkpatrick-seidel.summary: Divide-and-conquer planar convex hull algorithm that first finds the hull edge (bridge) crossing the dividing line and only then recurses ('marriage before conquest'). It is output-sensitive, running in O(n log h) time for h hull vertices.
a.kll-sketch.summary: A quantile sketch that compresses samples in a hierarchy of compactors with exponentially decreasing capacities, each discarding a random half of its sorted items. It achieves optimal space for streaming quantile approximation.
a.kmp.o1.note: Joint publication including Knuth's independent discovery
a.kmp.summary: A string search that uses a failure function to reuse information about already matched prefixes, finding a pattern in O(n + m) without backing up in the text.
a.knowledge-distillation.summary: A model compression method that transfers knowledge by training a small student model to match the soft probability distribution produced by a large teacher model with a high-temperature softmax.
a.kosaraju-scc.o0.title: Unpublished (circulated via Aho, Hopcroft, and Ullman's lecture materials)
a.kosaraju-scc.summary: An algorithm that finds strongly connected components by running DFS twice, once on the original graph and once on its transpose.
a.kruskal.summary: A minimum spanning tree algorithm that scans edges in order of weight and accepts only those that do not create a cycle.
a.kzg-commitment.summary: A pairing-based commitment scheme that commits to a polynomial with a single group element and proves its value at any point with another single group element. It is used in zk-SNARKs such as PLONK and in Ethereum's EIP-4844 data blobs.
a.l-bfgs-b.summary: An optimization algorithm that extends L-BFGS to simple bound constraints by combining gradient projection with a generalized Cauchy point search. It is widely used for box-constrained optimization, for example in SciPy.
a.l-bfgs.summary: A quasi-Newton method that represents the BFGS inverse-Hessian approximation implicitly by storing only a few recent step and gradient-difference vectors. It is used for large-scale optimization with many variables.
a.l-system.o0.note: Part II, "Mathematical models for cellular interactions in development II. Simple and branching filaments with two-sided inputs" (doi:10.1016/0022-5193(68)90080-5), appeared in the same issue.
a.l-system.summary: A parallel string-rewriting system that applies production rules to every symbol of a string simultaneously, originally proposed to model the development of multicellular organisms. Combined with a turtle-graphics interpretation, it is used for the procedural generation of plants and fractal shapes.
a.label-propagation.summary: A near-linear-time algorithm in which each vertex repeatedly adopts the label most common among its neighbours; once labels converge, vertices sharing a label form a community.
a.label-smoothing.summary: A regularization that trains against the one-hot target mixed with a uniform distribution in a fixed proportion. It discourages the model from producing overconfident outputs.
a.lalr.summary: A parsing method that merges LR(1) states with identical cores to reduce table size to that of LR(0). It is used by yacc and bison.
a.lamb.summary: An optimizer that scales Adam's update for each layer by the ratio of the weight norm to the update norm. It was proposed to train BERT with very large batches.
a.lamport-bakery.summary: An N-process mutual exclusion algorithm in which, like tickets at a bakery, each process takes a number larger than all current ones and processes enter the critical section in increasing order of number. It works even when reads and writes of shared variables are not atomic.
a.lamport-clock.summary: A technique that uses a logical clock, increasing monotonically with each event, to produce a total order consistent with the causal (happened-before) order in a distributed system.
