a.lamport-signature.summary: A one-time digital signature built only from a one-way function. For each message bit the signer reveals the preimage of one of two published hash values, and it became the starting point for hash-based signatures.
a.lancaster-stemmer.summary: An iterative stemming algorithm that looks up a matching rule in a table indexed by the final letter of the word and deletes or replaces the suffix, repeating until no rule applies. Its rules are kept in a separate table and can be replaced.
a.lanczos-algorithm.summary: An iterative method that reduces a Hermitian (symmetric) matrix to tridiagonal form on a Krylov subspace. It is used to compute extreme eigenvalues of large sparse matrices.
a.lanczos-approximation.summary: A formula that approximates the gamma function by a short rational series with a few coefficients multiplied by power and exponential factors. It is used to compute the gamma function in many math libraries.
a.laplacian-eigenmaps.summary: A technique that solves a generalized eigenvalue problem of the weighted Laplacian of a neighborhood graph to obtain a low-dimensional embedding that keeps nearby points close. It is also called spectral embedding.
a.laplacian-pyramid.summary: A multiresolution representation that stores, at each level, the difference between the Gaussian-smoothed, downsampled image and the upsampled next coarser level. The original image can be reconstructed exactly, and it is used for image coding and blending.
a.lars.summary: A regression algorithm that grows coefficients in the direction of the variable most correlated with the current residual and, once another variable becomes equally correlated, proceeds along the direction equiangular to them. A small modification computes the entire lasso solution path efficiently.
a.lasso.summary: A regression that adds an L1-norm penalty on the coefficients to the least-squares objective. It sets some coefficients exactly to zero, performing shrinkage and variable selection at once.
a.latent-diffusion.summary: An image generation method that trains a diffusion model in the latent space of a pretrained autoencoder and injects conditions such as text through cross-attention. It is the basis of Stable Diffusion.
a.latent-dirichlet-allocation.summary: A generative Bayesian topic model in which each document is a mixture of topics with proportions drawn from a Dirichlet distribution and each topic is a distribution over words. It is fitted with variational inference or Gibbs sampling.
a.latent-semantic-analysis.summary: A technique that projects a term–document matrix into a low-dimensional semantic space via truncated singular value decomposition, so that documents and queries can be compared semantically even when they share no words.
a.latin-hypercube.summary: A stratified sampling method that divides the range of each input variable into n equal-probability intervals and randomly permutes the intervals per variable so that each interval is used exactly once across n samples.
a.lawson-flip.o0.note: The same paper appeared that year as 'Software for C1 Surface Interpolation' in Mathematical Software III, edited by J. R. Rice.
a.lawson-flip.summary: Method that turns an arbitrary triangulation into the Delaunay triangulation by repeatedly flipping the diagonal of the convex quadrilateral formed by two adjacent triangles whenever a local criterion (max-min angle, empty circumcircle) is violated. It is the legalization step of incremental Delaunay triangulation codes.
a.layer-norm.summary: A normalization method that uses statistics over all hidden units of a single sample instead of the batch, so it works independently of batch size.
a.lazy-code-motion.summary: A partial-redundancy-elimination method that uses only unidirectional dataflow analyses to place computations as early as needed for optimality and then delays them as late as possible to reduce register pressure, giving computationally optimal placements with minimal lifetimes.
a.lbg.summary: An algorithm for designing vector quantizer codebooks that repeatedly assigns training vectors to their nearest codevector and updates each codevector to the centroid of its region. It generalizes Lloyd's algorithm to vectors and uses an initialization that grows the codebook by splitting.
a.lcg.o0.venue: Proceedings of the 2nd Symposium on Large-Scale Digital Calculating Machinery (published 1951)
a.lcg.summary: A generator that produces pseudorandom numbers via the recurrence x ← (a·x + c) mod m.
a.ldpc.o1.note: The same author's journal publication of the thesis work.
a.ldpc.summary: A linear block code whose parity-check matrix is mostly zeros, decoded by iterative probabilistic message passing on its Tanner graph. It performs close to the Shannon limit and is used in Wi-Fi, DVB-S2, 5G data channels and elsewhere.
a.lea.summary: A 128-bit block cipher developed in Korea. Built only from addition, rotation and XOR (ARX), it is fast on general-purpose processors and has been adopted as a Korean national standard.
a.leaky-bucket.summary: A traffic policing and shaping scheme that keeps a counter per user, incremented when a packet is sent and decremented periodically, and discards the packet if the counter exceeds a threshold. It limits average rate and burst size.
a.leftist-heap.summary: A heap-ordered binary tree in which, at every node, the null-path length (distance to the nearest missing child) of the left child is at least that of the right child. Two heaps are merged along their right spines in O(log n) time.
a.lehmer-gcd.summary: A method that speeds up the Euclidean algorithm on large integers by computing several quotient steps from single-precision leading digits, reducing the number of multiprecision operations. It is used for GCD computation in multiprecision integer libraries.
a.leiden.summary: A community-detection algorithm that inserts a partition-refinement phase between Louvain's local-moving and aggregation phases, guaranteeing that the communities found are internally connected.
a.lenet.summary: A convolutional neural network that recognized handwritten ZIP codes by training convolution and subsampling layers end to end with backpropagation.
a.lengauer-tarjan.summary: An algorithm that computes the immediate dominator of every vertex of a flowgraph in almost linear time by using depth-first numbering and semidominators. It is used to build dominator trees in compilers.
a.lenstra-ecm.summary: A factorization algorithm that computes a smooth scalar multiple of a point on a random elliptic curve modulo n and obtains a factor via gcd when a modular inversion fails. Its running time depends mainly on the size of the factor found, so it is used to find small factors of large numbers.
a.levenberg-marquardt.summary: A method for nonlinear least-squares problems that adds a damping term to Gauss–Newton, interpolating between gradient descent and Gauss–Newton steps. It is used in curve fitting and camera calibration.
a.levenshtein-automaton.summary: A method for building, in time linear in the word length, a deterministic finite automaton that accepts all strings within Levenshtein distance n of a given word. Traversing it together with a dictionary automaton quickly yields spelling-correction candidates.
a.levenshtein-distance.summary: An edit distance that defines the difference between two strings as the minimum number of insertions, deletions, and substitutions.
a.levinson-recursion.summary: A recursive algorithm that solves linear systems with a Toeplitz matrix in O(n²) operations by increasing the order one step at a time. It is used for linear prediction coefficients and autoregressive model fitting.
a.lex-bfs.summary: A variant of breadth-first search that chooses the next vertex by comparing lexicographic labels built from the order of already visited neighbours. It is used to find a perfect elimination ordering of a chordal graph in linear time.
a.liang-barsky.summary: Line clipping algorithm that, using a parametric segment representation, solves one inequality per boundary of an axis-aligned clip rectangle (box) and only updates the entering and leaving parameters. Intersection coordinates are computed only for the final interval.
a.library-sort.o0.note: The journal version appeared in Theory of Computing Systems in 2006.
a.library-sort.summary: An insertion sort that leaves gaps in the array so that each insertion shifts fewer elements. It runs in O(n log n) time with high probability.
a.lightgbm.summary: Gradient boosting accelerated by Gradient-based One-Side Sampling (GOSS) and Exclusive Feature Bundling (EFB).
a.lin-kernighan.summary: A heuristic that improves traveling-salesman tours with a variable-depth search, extending a chain of edge exchanges step by step while the cumulative gain stays positive instead of fixing the number of exchanged edges in advance.
a.linear-blend-skinning.summary: A method that deforms a mesh with a skeleton by transforming each vertex with the matrices of several influencing joints and linearly combining the results with weights. It is simple and fast on GPUs but suffers volume loss, known as the candy-wrapper artifact, at strongly twisted joints.
a.linear-counting.summary: A probabilistic counting method that sets bitmap bits from hash values and estimates the number of distinct elements from the fraction of empty bits. It is accurate for small cardinalities and is used for the small range in HyperLogLog++.
a.linear-discriminant-analysis.summary: A method that finds the linear projection maximizing the ratio of between-class to within-class variance, used for classification or dimensionality reduction. Under Gaussian classes with a shared covariance it gives the Bayes-optimal linear classifier.
a.linear-hashing.summary: A directoryless dynamic hashing scheme that grows the table gradually by splitting buckets one at a time in a fixed order. Records that overflow are kept in overflow chains.
a.linear-probing.o0.title: Open-addressing hashing in the IBM 701 assembler
a.linear-probing.o0.venue: Cited as the origin in Knuth, TAOCP Vol. 3 §6.4
a.linear-probing.summary: An open-addressing hash table that examines the next slot sequentially on a collision.
a.linear-scan.summary: Register allocation that sweeps once over live intervals in order of start point, keeping a list of active intervals and spilling the one that ends furthest away when registers run out. Faster than graph coloring, it is widely used in JIT compilers.
a.linear-sieve.summary: A sieve that finds primes in O(n) by crossing out each composite exactly once, via its smallest prime factor.
a.link-cut-tree.o0.note: The journal version appeared in Journal of Computer and System Sciences 26(3), 1983.
a.link-cut-tree.summary: A dynamic-tree data structure that maintains a forest of rooted trees under link and cut by decomposing them into paths kept in auxiliary search trees. It handles path queries and updates in O(log n) time per operation and was used to speed up maximum-flow algorithms.
a.link-state-routing.summary: A routing approach in which each router floods the state of its adjacent links throughout the network and computes routes with a shortest-path-first (SPF) calculation on the collected topology. It was first introduced as the new ARPANET routing algorithm and underlies OSPF and IS-IS.
a.lion.summary: An optimizer that applies updates of uniform magnitude using only the sign of an interpolation between the momentum and the current gradient. It was discovered by program search and keeps less optimizer state than Adam.
a.lirs.summary: A buffer cache replacement algorithm that classifies blocks as LIR (low) or HIR (high) by inter-reference recency, the number of other blocks referenced between a block's last two references, and evicts HIR blocks first.
a.lkh.summary: A traveling-salesman heuristic that strengthens Lin–Kernighan by restricting candidate edges with α-nearness derived from 1-tree lower bounds and by using sequential 5-opt exchanges as the basic move.
a.ll-parsing.summary: Deterministic top-down parsing that reads input left to right, builds a leftmost derivation and chooses which production to apply from only k tokens of lookahead. It is implemented as recursive-descent or table-driven predictive parsers.
a.lll.summary: A polynomial-time algorithm that finds a short, nearly orthogonal basis of a lattice by alternating size reduction of Gram–Schmidt coefficients with basis swaps governed by the Lovász condition. It is used in polynomial factorization, integer relation finding and cryptanalysis.
a.lmo-prime-counting.summary: An algorithm that reorganizes the φ(x, a) computation of the Meissel–Lehmer method into special-leaf sums evaluated with a segmented sieve, computing π(x) in O(x^(2/3+ε)) time and O(x^(1/3+ε)) space.
a.lobpcg.summary: A method for extreme eigenpairs of symmetric eigenproblems that repeatedly applies the Rayleigh–Ritz procedure on the subspace spanned by the current iterates, the preconditioned residuals and the previous search directions.
a.local-binary-patterns.summary: Encodes, for each pixel, whether its neighbors are brighter than the center as a bit code, and uses the histogram of these codes over a region as a texture feature. It is simple to compute and robust to monotonic illumination changes.
a.local-outlier-factor.summary: A density-based anomaly-detection method that scores outlierness by the ratio comparing a point's local reachability density with those of its k nearest neighbors.
a.locally-linear-embedding.summary: A nonlinear dimensionality-reduction technique that computes weights reconstructing each point from its neighbors and then finds, via an eigenvalue problem, the low-dimensional coordinates best reconstructed by the same weights.
a.loco-i.summary: A low-complexity lossless image compression algorithm that predicts each pixel with the edge-detecting median predictor (MED) from neighboring pixels, corrects context-dependent bias, and codes the residuals with Golomb-type codes whose parameters adapt per context. It uses a run mode in flat regions and became the basis of the JPEG-LS standard.
a.logistic-regression.o0.note: Applied the logistic function to dose–response data in bioassay and introduced the term 'logit'.
a.logistic-regression.o1.note: Formulated the logistic model as a general framework for regressing binary responses on explanatory variables.
a.logistic-regression.summary: A regression model that passes a linear predictor through the logistic (sigmoid) function to model the probability of a binary outcome. Coefficients are usually fitted by maximum likelihood, and it is widely used as a classifier.
a.loglog.summary: An algorithm that estimates the number of distinct elements in log-log memory by recording the maximum run of leading zeros of hashes in multiple registers.
a.loop-subdivision.summary: An approximating subdivision surface scheme for triangle meshes that inserts a new point on each edge to split every triangle into four and updates positions as weighted averages of neighboring points. In regular regions it converges to a C2 surface based on quartic box splines.
a.lora.summary: A method that freezes the pretrained weights and trains only a product of low-rank matrices, greatly reducing the number of fine-tuning parameters.
a.lossy-counting.summary: A frequent-items algorithm that divides the stream into buckets of width 1/ε and prunes small counts at each bucket boundary, guaranteeing frequency estimates within an error of εN.
a.lottery-scheduling.summary: A randomized proportional-share scheduling scheme that gives each task lottery tickets in proportion to its share and picks the task to run at each scheduling decision by a random draw.
a.louds.summary: A succinct tree representation that visits the nodes in breadth-first order and writes each node's number of children in unary (that many 1s followed by a 0), using about 2n bits. Parent and child navigation is done with rank and select on the bit string, and it is used in tries such as MARISA.
a.louvain.summary: A multilevel community-detection algorithm that alternates a phase of moving vertices to neighbouring communities to increase modularity locally with a phase of aggregating each community into a single vertex.
a.lpa-star.summary: An incremental version of A* that, when edge costs change, reuses the unaffected parts of the previous search and re-expands only locally inconsistent vertices. Its first search produces the same result as A*.
a.lpc.summary: A coding method that estimates, for each frame, the coefficients of an all-pole filter predicting each speech sample as a linear combination of the previous p samples, so that speech can be analyzed and synthesized from the predictor coefficients and an excitation signal alone. It is used in speech codecs and in the prediction stage of lossless audio compressors such as FLAC.
a.lr-parsing.summary: A bottom-up parsing method that reads input left to right using a stack and a state automaton, producing a rightmost derivation in reverse.
a.lru-k.summary: A buffer replacement algorithm that records the time of each page's K-th most recent reference and evicts the page for which that time is oldest. It distinguishes frequently used pages from one-time references better than LRU.
a.lsh.summary: Finds approximate nearest neighbors in high dimensions using families of hash functions designed so that nearby points collide in the same bucket with higher probability than distant points.
a.lsm-tree.summary: An index that increases write throughput by accumulating writes in an in-memory component and sequentially merging them into sorted on-disk components.
a.lsoda.summary: An ODE integrator that detects stiffness at run time and switches automatically between Adams methods for nonstiff phases and BDF for stiff phases.
a.lsqr.summary: An iterative method for sparse linear equations and least-squares problems based on Golub–Kahan bidiagonalization. It is analytically equivalent to conjugate gradients on the normal equations but numerically more reliable.
a.lstm.o0.note: Forget gate added by Gers et al. (2000)
a.lstm.summary: An architecture that controls a cell state with input, forget, and output gates, mitigating the vanishing gradient problem in recurrent neural networks.
a.lt-code.summary: The first practical fountain code: it generates an unlimited stream of encoded symbols, each the XOR of a randomly chosen number of source symbols, and the source can be recovered from slightly more symbols than its size.
a.lucas-kanade.summary: An image registration method that assumes constant flow within a small window, solves the brightness-constancy equations by least squares, and estimates displacement between images with Newton-type iterations based on a Taylor expansion. Widely used for tracking sparse feature points.
a.lucas-lehmer.o0.note: The paper was published in parts across issues 2–4 of volume 1 of the American Journal of Mathematics; this DOI is the part in issue 2.
a.lucas-lehmer.summary: A deterministic test that declares the Mersenne number M_p = 2^p−1 prime exactly when s_{p−2} ≡ 0 (mod M_p), where s₀ = 4 and s_{k+1} = s_k²−2. It is used in searches for Mersenne primes.
a.lucifer.summary: An early IBM block cipher using a Feistel structure. It is the predecessor of DES.
a.luhn-algorithm.o0.note: The patent was filed in 1954 and granted in 1960.
a.luhn-algorithm.summary: A modulus-10 check that doubles every second digit starting from the second-rightmost, adds the digits, and chooses the check digit so that the total is a multiple of ten. It is used for credit-card numbers, IMEIs and more.
a.lz4.summary: A compression method that maximizes decompression speed by using only byte-aligned LZ77 sequences without entropy coding.
a.lz77.summary: A dictionary compression method that references the longest match within a sliding window of previously seen data as a (distance, length) pair.
a.lz78.summary: A dictionary compression method that explicitly grows its dictionary by parsing the input into an existing dictionary entry plus one character.
a.lzma.o0.title: LZMA compression in 7-Zip
a.lzma.summary: A compression method that combines LZ77 matching over a large dictionary with context-model-based range coding. It is the core of the 7z and xz formats.
a.lzmw.summary: A variant of LZ78-family dictionary compression that adds, as each new dictionary entry, the concatenation of the previous match and the current match. Long strings enter the dictionary faster than in LZW.
a.lzp.summary: An LZ77 variant that predicts, from a hash of the context formed by the preceding few bytes, the earlier position where the same context occurred, and sends only the match length against that position. Since the match position is never transmitted, there is no offset coding cost.
a.lzrw1.summary: An LZ77-family compression algorithm that checks only the single candidate position found by hashing the next three bytes and immediately updates that hash table entry. By limiting the search to one probe it compresses very quickly.
a.lzss.summary: A variant that reduces the waste in LZ77 by emitting literals as-is when a match is shorter than the cost of a reference.
a.lzw.summary: A dictionary compression method that eliminates the explicit character output of LZ78 by initializing the dictionary with all single characters. It was used in GIF and Unix compress.
a.m-tree.summary: A balanced, paged tree for metric spaces that groups objects under routing objects with covering radii, using only the distance function. It grows dynamically through insertions and supports range and k-nearest-neighbor queries.
a.madgwick-filter.summary: An orientation filter for IMU and MARG sensors that corrects the attitude quaternion integrated from gyroscope rates with a single gradient-descent step on an error function against accelerometer (and magnetometer) measurements. Its low cost makes it popular on microcontrollers.
a.maekawa-algorithm.summary: A distributed mutual exclusion algorithm that assigns each node a voting set (quorum) of about √N nodes such that any two sets intersect, and lets a node enter the critical section once every member of its own set has granted permission.
a.mamba.summary: A sequence model built from selective state space layers whose parameters depend on the input, computed with a hardware-aware parallel scan in time linear in the sequence length. Its layers are stacked without attention.
a.manacher.summary: An algorithm that finds the longest palindrome around every center in linear time by reusing the symmetry of previously computed palindrome radii.
a.mapreduce.summary: A distributed data processing model in which the user writes only a map function that turns input into key-value pairs and a reduce function that merges values with the same key, while the system automatically handles partitioning, shuffling and fault recovery by re-execution on large clusters.
a.marching-cubes.summary: An algorithm that extracts a surface mesh by triangulating each cube of a 3D grid using a table of the patterns in which the isosurface passes through it.
a.mark-sweep.summary: A tracing garbage collector that marks objects reachable from the roots and then reclaims unmarked objects.
a.marr-hildreth.summary: Detects edges as the zero crossings of the image filtered with a Laplacian of Gaussian (LoG). Using Gaussians of several sizes yields edges at multiple scales.
a.marsaglia-polar.summary: A method that picks a uniform point (V₁, V₂) inside the unit circle by rejection and, with s = V₁²+V₂², returns V·√(−2 ln s / s), producing two standard normal variates without trigonometric functions.
a.marsaglia-tsang-gamma.summary: A gamma variate generator that, for shape α ≥ 1, sets d = α−1/3 and c = 1/√(9d), proposes d(1+cx)³ from a normal variate x and accepts it with a simple squeeze test followed by a log test. For α < 1 it multiplies a sample for α+1 by U^(1/α).
a.martinez-rueda.summary: Polygon Boolean operation algorithm that processes the edges of two polygons with a plane sweep, subdivides edges at intersection points, and labels each edge fragment as inside or outside the other polygon to compute intersection, union, difference and XOR. It runs in O((n+k) log n) time for k intersections.
a.mask-rcnn.summary: An instance segmentation method that adds to Faster R-CNN a branch predicting an object mask for each region of interest. It introduced RoIAlign to remove the misalignment of RoI pooling.
a.masstree.summary: A concurrent main-memory index that splits keys into 8-byte slices, builds a B+-tree for each layer, and links the layers like a trie. Optimistic concurrency control based on version numbers lets reads proceed without locks.
a.matula-beck.summary: A linear-time algorithm for the smallest-last ordering, which lists vertices in the reverse of the order in which minimum-degree vertices are repeatedly removed. It is used to compute graph degeneracy and as a greedy colouring order.
a.maximum-cardinality-search.summary: A graph search that always picks next the vertex with the largest number of already numbered neighbours. It is used to test chordality of graphs and acyclicity of hypergraphs in linear time.
a.mccreight-algorithm.summary: An algorithm that uses suffix links to build a suffix tree, starting from the longest suffix, in linear time and with little memory.
a.mceliece.summary: A code-based public-key cryptosystem based on the hardness of decoding random linear codes. A disguised generator matrix of a secret Goppa code serves as the public key, and the scheme is believed to resist quantum computers.
a.mcs-lock.summary: A FIFO spin lock in which each waiting thread appends a node to a linked-list queue and spins only on a flag in its own node. Cache-coherence traffic per acquisition stays constant regardless of the number of processors.
a.mcts.summary: A game tree search that accumulates the results of random playouts in a tree to progressively search promising moves more deeply.
a.md4.summary: A hash function that produces a 128-bit digest with three rounds of 32-bit word operations. It became the template for the later MD5 and SHA family designs.
a.md5.summary: A 128-bit hash that strengthens MD4 with a fourth round and unique additive constants. Collision attacks now make it unsuitable for security purposes.
a.mdct.o1.note: Follow-up paper applying the time-domain aliasing cancellation filter bank to transform coding.
a.mdct.summary: A critically sampled lapped transform that maps blocks of length 2N, overlapping by 50%, to N coefficients; the time-domain aliasing of neighboring blocks cancels on overlap-add (TDAC). It is the transform used in audio codecs such as MP3, AAC, Vorbis and Opus.
a.mean-shift-tracking.summary: Tracks a target by running mean-shift iterations that maximize the Bhattacharyya coefficient between the target's color histogram and that of the candidate region. It tracks non-rigid objects in real time.
a.mean-shift.summary: A method that repeatedly moves each point toward the kernel-weighted mean of nearby samples to locate the modes of the density. Points that converge to the same mode form one cluster, and it is also used for image segmentation and tracking.
a.median-cut.summary: Color quantization that repeatedly splits boxes in color space at the median of their longest axis so each box holds a similar number of pixels, then uses each box's average color as a palette entry. Commonly used to build GIF and PNG palettes.
a.median-of-medians.summary: An algorithm that solves the selection problem in worst-case linear time by using the median of the medians of groups of five as the pivot.
a.megiddo-lp.summary: Deterministic algorithm that, for fixed dimension d, repeatedly pairs up constraints and uses medians to discard a constant fraction of them (prune and search), solving linear programs in time linear in the number n of constraints.
a.mehrotra-predictor-corrector.summary: A primal–dual interior-point technique that uses an affine-scaling predictor direction to choose the centering parameter, then adds a corrector, computing both with a single matrix factorization. It became the basis of practical interior-point LP solvers.
a.meissel-lehmer.summary: An algorithm that computes the prime-counting function π(x) through Legendre's formula and recursion on the partial sieve function φ(x, a), without enumerating all primes up to x. Meissel devised it and Lehmer simplified it for computer calculation.
a.melkman.summary: Online algorithm that maintains the convex hull of a simple (non-self-intersecting) polyline in a deque as vertices arrive one by one. It processes the whole polyline in linear time.
a.merge-insertion.summary: A sort that compares elements in pairs, recursively sorts the larger ones and then binary-inserts the smaller ones in a prescribed order, using a nearly minimal number of comparisons.
a.merge-path.summary: A parallel merging method that views the merge of two sorted arrays as a path on a grid, cuts the path evenly along diagonals and uses binary search to find the range each processor merges independently.
a.merge-sort.o0.title: Merge sort program for the EDVAC (unpublished manuscript)
a.merge-sort.o0.venue: Cited as the origin in Knuth, TAOCP Vol. 3
a.merge-sort.summary: A divide-and-conquer sort that splits the array in half, sorts each half, and merges them in linear time. It runs in O(n log n) worst-case time and is stable.
a.merkle-damgard.summary: A construction that builds a collision-resistant hash by chaining a fixed-length compression function over padded blocks.
a.merkle-signature.summary: A hash-based signature that binds many one-time signature public keys into a Merkle tree so that one public key can sign many messages. A signature contains a one-time signature and the authentication path to the root.
a.merkle-tree.o0.note: Publicly described in the CRYPTO ’87 paper "A Digital Signature Based on a Conventional Encryption Function"
a.merkle-tree.summary: A tree in which each parent is the hash of its children's hashes. A single root hash verifies the integrity of large volumes of data.
a.mersenne-twister.summary: A twisted GFSR pseudorandom number generator whose period is the Mersenne prime 2^19937−1.
a.metaphone.summary: A phonetic encoding algorithm that converts a word into a sequence of consonant symbols approximating its pronunciation, using context-dependent transformation rules that reflect English spelling. It handles English pronunciation rules in more detail than Soundex.
a.metis.summary: A multilevel graph-partitioning scheme that coarsens the graph step by step through vertex matchings, partitions the smallest graph, and then uncoarsens it while locally refining boundary vertices at each level.
a.metropolis-hastings.summary: A generalization of the Metropolis algorithm that corrects the acceptance probability to allow asymmetric proposal distributions.
a.metropolis-light-transport.summary: A rendering method that performs Metropolis sampling in the space of light paths, mutating paths incrementally to draw samples distributed in proportion to their contribution. It is effective when important paths are hard to find, such as in scenes lit through a narrow opening.
a.metropolis.summary: A sampling method that constructs a Markov chain with the Boltzmann distribution as its stationary distribution by accepting proposed states with a probability determined by the energy difference.
a.michael-scott-queue.summary: A lock-free FIFO queue in which multiple threads concurrently enqueue and dequeue using head and tail pointers and compare-and-swap (CAS). The same paper also presents a two-lock queue with separate locks for head and tail.
a.miller-rabin.summary: A primality test that writes n−1 as 2^s·d and checks a strong Fermat condition for chosen bases to detect composites. Miller presented it as a deterministic test under the generalized Riemann hypothesis, and Rabin as a randomized test with random bases.
a.min-area-rectangle.summary: Method that uses the property that a minimum-area rectangle enclosing a closed curve (point set) has a side collinear with an edge of the convex hull, so only the directions of the hull edges need to be examined.
a.min-max-heap.summary: An array-based complete binary tree whose even levels follow min-heap order and odd levels max-heap order. It is a double-ended priority queue that finds both the minimum and the maximum in constant time and deletes either in O(log n) time.
a.min-mean-cycle-canceling.summary: A variant of the cycle-canceling algorithm that always cancels a residual cycle of minimum mean cost, which bounds the number of iterations strongly polynomially for the minimum-cost circulation problem.
a.minhash.summary: Estimates set similarity using the fact that, under a random permutation (hash) of the elements, the probability that two sets have the same minimum equals their Jaccard similarity.
a.mini-batch-k-means.summary: A k-means variant that updates cluster centers using small random mini-batches instead of the full data set. Per-center decreasing learning rates greatly reduce computation on large data.
a.minimap2.o1.note: Journal version with the same title.
a.minimap2.summary: A sequence alignment method that finds minimizer seeds, chains them with dynamic programming and fills the regions between chained seeds with SIMD-based alignment. It is used for long reads, spliced reads and genome-to-genome alignment.
a.minimax.o0.note: Theoretical basis is von Neumann's 1928 minimax theorem
a.minimax.summary: A search that assumes the opponent plays optimally and alternately takes the maximum and minimum evaluation at each move of the game tree.
a.minimizer.summary: A sequence sampling technique that picks, for every w consecutive k-mers, the smallest one under a fixed order as a representative. Common substrings of length at least w+k−1 share a representative, so it reduces index size while remaining usable for sequence comparison.
a.minres.summary: An iterative method for symmetric, possibly indefinite, linear systems that minimizes the residual norm using the Lanczos process. SYMMLQ was proposed in the same paper.
a.mipmapping.summary: A texture filtering technique that precomputes a pyramid of textures, each at half the previous resolution, to reduce aliasing under minification.
a.misra-gries.summary: A deterministic frequent-items algorithm that uses only k−1 counters to find candidates for every item occurring more than n/k times in a stream. It generalizes the majority vote algorithm.
a.mixture-of-experts.summary: A model that jointly trains several expert networks and a gating network that weights them for each input. The input space becomes partitioned so that each expert specializes in a region.
a.ml-dsa.summary: A digital signature based on module-lattice problems (Module-LWE and Module-SIS). The 'Fiat–Shamir with aborts' technique keeps signatures from leaking information about the secret key, and NIST standardized it as FIPS 204.
a.ml-kem.summary: A key-encapsulation mechanism based on the learning-with-errors problem over module lattices (Module-LWE). A Fujisaki–Okamoto transform makes it secure against chosen-ciphertext attacks, and NIST standardized it as FIPS 203.
a.mlaa.summary: A post-process anti-aliasing method that finds color discontinuities in the rendered image, classifies them into L-, Z- and U-shaped patterns, and blends pixels on both sides of each edge according to its shape. It works from the final image alone, without extra samples.
a.mobilenet.summary: A lightweight convolutional network that factors standard convolutions into depthwise and 1×1 pointwise convolutions to cut computation. Width and resolution multipliers trade size against accuracy.
a.moller-trumbore.summary: An algorithm that solves directly for the barycentric coordinates and distance of a ray–triangle intersection, deciding the hit with only cross and dot products and without storing the triangle's plane equation. Its low memory use and speed have made it widespread in ray tracers.
a.momentum.summary: Gradient descent that accumulates previous update directions like inertia, damping oscillations across ravines and accelerating convergence.
a.monotone-chain.summary: A variant of Graham scan that sorts points by x-coordinate and scans the upper and lower hulls separately.
a.monotone-polygon-triangulation.summary: Triangulation method that splits a simple polygon into monotone pieces with a plane sweep and then triangulates each monotone piece in linear time using a stack. The overall running time is O(n log n).
a.monte-carlo.o0.note: Devised around 1946 at Los Alamos together with Ulam and von Neumann
a.monte-carlo.summary: A method that approximates quantities such as integrals and expected values by averaging random samples.
a.montgomery-multiplication.summary: A technique for modular multiplication without trial division: operands are mapped to Montgomery form scaled by R = 2^k, and the REDC reduction computes T·R^(−1) mod N using only multiplications and shifts. It is widely used in public-key implementations based on modular exponentiation.
a.moore-minimization.summary: A DFA minimization algorithm that starts by splitting states into accepting and non-accepting ones and repeatedly separates states whose transitions on some symbol lead to different blocks, until the partition no longer changes. Its worst-case time is O(n²) for a fixed alphabet.
a.morsel-driven-parallelism.summary: A query execution technique for many-core machines that splits input into small fragments (morsels), dispatches them dynamically to worker threads, and executes query pipelines in parallel with attention to NUMA locality.
a.mosse-tracker.summary: Tracks a target with a correlation filter, learned and updated in the Fourier domain, that minimizes the sum of squared error between its output on target images and a desired Gaussian response. It runs at very high frame rates.
a.move-to-front.summary: A transform that outputs each symbol's position in a list and moves the most recently used symbol to the front, turning local repetitions into small numbers.
a.mpqs.o0.note: The paper credits the idea of using multiple polynomials to Peter Montgomery.
a.mpqs.summary: A variant of the quadratic sieve that sieves over many quadratic polynomials instead of one, keeping the sieved values small. Because the work is split into short sieve intervals, it is easy to parallelize.
a.mrg32k3a.summary: A pseudorandom generator that combines two third-order multiple recursive generators with moduli close to 2³². It has a period of about 2¹⁹¹ and is easy to split into streams, so it is widely used in simulation software.
a.mser.summary: Detects connected regions, among those arising as the threshold is varied, whose area changes least with the threshold. It provides region features robust to viewpoint and illumination changes.
a.mtd-f.summary: A search algorithm that repeatedly runs null-window alpha–beta searches with a transposition table, narrowing upper and lower bounds until they converge on the minimax value. The closer the first guess f is, the fewer iterations it needs.
a.mu-law.summary: A companding method that compresses a signal value x logarithmically, in proportion to ln(1 + μ|x|)/ln(1 + μ), before uniform quantization, assigning more quantization steps to small amplitudes. The form with μ = 255 is the μ-law of ITU-T G.711 used in North American and Japanese telephone networks.
a.muller-method.summary: A root-finding method that takes the next approximation as a root of the quadratic through the three most recent points. Because it can reach complex roots, it is used for polynomial root finding.
a.multi-query-attention.summary: Attention in which all heads share a single key and value projection, reducing memory bandwidth during decoding.
a.multigrid.o1.note: Not the first publication, but the paper that systematized multigrid as an adaptive multilevel technique and made it widely known.
a.multigrid.summary: An iterative method that solves discretized elliptic PDEs by alternating relaxation sweeps with coarse-grid corrections on a hierarchy of grids. Variants include algebraic multigrid (AMG).
a.multikey-quicksort.o0.note: The paper notes that the basic ideas behind the algorithm date back at least to the 1960s.
a.multikey-quicksort.summary: A string sort that partitions three ways (less, equal, greater) on the character at the current position and recurses on the equal group with the next character. It combines quicksort and radix sort.
a.multilevel-feedback-queue.summary: A CPU scheduling scheme with several queues of different priority, in which a job that uses up its time quantum is moved to a lower queue, favoring short interactive jobs. It was first used in the CTSS time-sharing system.
a.multiple-importance-sampling.summary: A method that combines samples drawn with several sampling techniques into a single Monte Carlo estimator using weights such as the balance heuristic or the power heuristic. It keeps the variance of the combined estimator low even where any single technique alone would have high variance.
a.murmurhash.o0.note: First released in 2008; the current version, MurmurHash3, was completed in 2011.
a.murmurhash.summary: A family of non-cryptographic hash functions that mix the input with repeated multiply and rotate steps. The current version, MurmurHash3, provides 32-bit and 128-bit outputs and is used in many libraries and data systems.
a.mvcc.o0.note: The theory and algorithms of multiversion concurrency control were systematized by Bernstein and Goodman, ACM TODS 8(4), 1983 (doi:10.1145/319996.319998).
a.mvcc.summary: A concurrency-control technique that keeps multiple versions of each data item, creating a new version on every write, and lets each transaction read the version appropriate to its point in time, so that reads and writes do not block each other.
a.myers-bit-vector.o1.note: Journal version with the same title.
a.myers-bit-vector.summary: An approximate string matching algorithm that represents the differences between adjacent cells in a column of the edit-distance dynamic programming matrix as bit vectors and updates them a machine word at a time. It runs in O(⌈m/w⌉n) time for pattern length m and word size w.
a.myers-diff.summary: A diff algorithm that finds a shortest edit script in O(ND) by advancing the furthest-reaching point on each diagonal of the edit graph. It is the default algorithm of git diff.
a.myers-miller.summary: An algorithm that applies Hirschberg's divide-and-conquer technique to Gotoh's affine-gap alignment to obtain an optimal global alignment in linear space. Its running time remains O(mn).
a.nagle-algorithm.summary: A TCP sending rule that, while previously sent data remains unacknowledged, holds back new small segments and coalesces them until an ACK arrives. It reduces networks being flooded with tiny packets.
a.naive-bayes.o0.note: An early study that automatically assigned documents to subject categories by Bayesian probability computed with word occurrences treated as independent.
a.naive-bayes.summary: A probabilistic classifier that assumes features are conditionally independent given the class and picks the class with the highest posterior probability via Bayes' theorem. It is widely used for text classification and spam filtering.
a.nakamoto-consensus.summary: A blockchain consensus scheme in which nodes append blocks by solving proof-of-work hash puzzles and accept the chain with the most cumulative work as the valid history, reaching agreement on transaction order without identified participants.
a.nauty.summary: A method that builds a search tree by refining vertex partitions to equitable partitions and prunes it with the automorphisms it discovers, producing a canonical labelling of the graph and generators of its automorphism group.
a.ndt.summary: Scan matching method that divides the space of a reference scan into grid cells, approximates the points in each cell by a normal distribution, and uses Newton's method to find the transformation maximizing the summed probability density of the new scan's points under these distributions. It does not compute explicit point correspondences.
a.needham-schroeder.summary: A key-distribution protocol in which two users obtain a shared session key and authenticate each other through a trusted authentication server. Both symmetric-key and public-key versions were presented, and it became the basis of Kerberos.
a.needleman-wunsch.summary: An algorithm that finds an optimal global alignment of two biological sequences by dynamic programming.
a.nelder-mead.summary: A derivative-free direct search method that seeks a function minimum by reflecting, expanding and contracting a simplex of n+1 vertices. It is distinct from the simplex method of linear programming.
a.neocognitron.summary: A hierarchical neural network that alternates layers of simple and complex cells to recognize patterns robustly under positional shifts. It is the prototype of the CNN.
a.nerf.summary: A novel view synthesis method that represents a scene with a multilayer perceptron mapping 3D position and viewing direction to density and emitted color, and trains it by comparing pixel colors, integrated along rays with classical volume rendering, against photographs. A positional encoding lets it represent high-frequency detail.
a.nesterov.summary: An accelerated gradient method that evaluates the gradient at the point reached by a momentum look-ahead step, guaranteeing O(1/k²) convergence on convex problems.
a.neumaier-summation.summary: An improved form of Kahan summation that computes the error relative to the larger of the two operands, so that lost bits are corrected even when the next term is larger than the running sum. Python's built-in sum() uses it for floats since version 3.12.
a.newton-method.summary: A root-finding method that iteratively updates the estimate to the x-intercept of the tangent line, converging quadratically near a simple root.
a.nice.summary: A normalizing-flow generative model that stacks additive coupling layers, each adding a function of one half of the input to the other half, so that inversion and the Jacobian determinant are easy to compute.
a.nicholl-lee-nicholl.summary: Two-dimensional line clipping algorithm that partitions the plane into a few regions depending on whether the segment's start point lies inside, in an edge region or in a corner region, and uses the region containing the end point to decide directly which boundaries are crossed, reducing the number of operations.
a.njw-spectral-clustering.summary: A spectral clustering algorithm that embeds points with the top k eigenvectors of the normalized affinity matrix, normalizes each row to unit length, and groups the rows with k-means.
a.nmf.o0.note: Proposed the method as 'positive matrix factorization' (PMF) for environmental data analysis.
a.nmf.o1.note: Introduced the name 'non-negative matrix factorization' and demonstrated parts-based representation learning.
a.nmf.summary: A factorization that approximates a non-negative matrix by the product of two low-rank non-negative matrices. It yields interpretable parts-based representations and is solved with methods such as multiplicative update rules.
a.node2vec.summary: A method that generates second-order random walks biased by a return parameter p and an in-out parameter q and learns vertex embeddings from them with SkipGram. With p = q = 1 the walks reduce to the uniform walks of DeepWalk.
a.noise-protocol.o0.note: This cites revision 34; earlier revisions had been published before it.
a.noise-protocol.summary: A framework for building authenticated key-exchange handshakes by composing Diffie–Hellman patterns such as IK and XX. It updates handshake state with the chosen hash, cipher and DH functions and is used in WireGuard, WhatsApp and the Lightning Network.
a.non-local-means.summary: Denoising that replaces each pixel with a weighted average of pixels whose surrounding patches are similar, searched over the whole image or a search window. It preserves repetitive textures and structures well.
a.nonlinear-conjugate-gradient.summary: An extension of the conjugate gradient method to minimizing general nonlinear functions, performing line searches along directions that combine the current gradient with the previous search direction. Update formulas include Fletcher–Reeves and Polak–Ribière.
a.normalized-cuts.summary: A graph partitioning method that normalizes the cut cost by each part's total connection to the whole graph and relaxes the resulting criterion into a generalized eigenvector problem of the graph Laplacian. It is used for image segmentation and spectral clustering.
a.nsw.summary: Builds a navigable small-world graph by connecting each new element to approximate nearest neighbors found in the existing graph, then answers approximate nearest-neighbor queries by greedy search on that graph.
a.ntru.summary: A lattice-based public-key cryptosystem whose security rests on the difficulty of finding short vectors in polynomial-ring lattices. Its operations are mainly polynomial multiplications, making it fast, and it laid the groundwork for many later lattice schemes.
a.nuts.summary: An MCMC method that sets the path length of Hamiltonian Monte Carlo automatically by repeatedly doubling the trajectory forward or backward and stopping once it starts to turn back on itself. It also adapts the step size by dual averaging and serves as the default sampler in Stan, PyMC and others.
a.oaep.summary: A padding scheme for public-key encryption that randomizes the plaintext with a two-round Feistel-like transform built from hash functions before applying a trapdoor permutation, usually RSA. It was adopted in PKCS #1 v2 as RSAES-OAEP.
a.obbtree.summary: Collision detection method that encloses an object's surface in a hierarchy of oriented bounding boxes (OBBs) and tests whether two OBBs overlap with a separating-axis test on at most 15 axes. The orientation of each OBB is given by the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix of the vertex distribution.
a.oblivious-transfer.o0.note: The oblivious-transfer concept itself was proposed earlier by Rabin (1981); this paper introduced the form in which one of two messages is chosen.
a.oblivious-transfer.summary: A protocol in which a sender offers two messages and the receiver obtains exactly one of them, without the sender learning which one and without the receiver learning the other. It is a basic building block of secure multiparty computation such as garbled circuits.
a.ocb.summary: An AEAD mode that provides encryption and authentication in one pass, using about as many block-cipher calls as there are plaintext blocks. A distinct offset is XORed into each block, enabling parallel processing.
a.octree-quantization.summary: Color quantization that inserts pixels into an octree indexed by the bits of their RGB values and merges the deepest nodes whenever the number of leaves exceeds the palette size. Its memory use stays proportional to the palette size.
a.octree.o0.note: Meagher first described the encoding in a 1980 technical report at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (RPI).
a.octree.summary: A tree that recursively subdivides three-dimensional space into eight cubic octants. It is used for solid modeling, point-cloud processing and spatial indexing.
a.odd-even-merge-sort.summary: A sorting network that merges odd and even positions separately, using O(n log² n) comparators.
a.one-class-svm.summary: A method that learns a hyperplane separating the data from the origin with maximum margin in feature space, estimating the support of unlabeled data and flagging points outside it as novelties.
a.onesweep.summary: An LSD radix sort for GPUs that uses a single-pass prefix sum in each digit-binning step to reduce global memory traffic. It is implemented in the radix sort of NVIDIA CUB.
a.opaque.summary: An asymmetric (augmented) password-authenticated key exchange that resists pre-computation attacks because, by using an oblivious pseudorandom function (OPRF), the server never exposes the salt. It combines the OPRF with an authenticated key exchange.
a.operator-precedence-parsing.summary: Bottom-up parsing for operator grammars in which precedence relations (yields, equal, takes precedence) are defined between pairs of terminals, and the handle to reduce is found from those relations alone.
a.optics.summary: A density-based cluster analysis that orders points by core distance and reachability distance, so that a single run reveals cluster structure at many density levels in a reachability plot. It reduces DBSCAN's dependence on a fixed ε.
a.optimistic-concurrency-control.summary: A concurrency-control technique in which a transaction runs its read phase without locks, then checks in a validation phase whether it conflicts with other transactions, and applies its writes in a write phase only if there is no conflict.
a.opus.summary: An interactive audio codec that combines a linear-prediction-based SILK layer and an MDCT-based CELT layer to code everything from speech to music over a wide range of bitrates with low delay. It is standardized as IETF RFC 6716 and is a mandatory-to-implement audio codec in WebRTC.
a.orb.summary: A feature detection and description method that combines oriented FAST keypoints with rotation-aware (steered) BRIEF descriptors. It was proposed as a much faster alternative to SIFT and SURF.
a.orca.summary: Collision avoidance that builds, for each other agent, a half-plane constraint sharing the avoidance responsibility equally, and solves a linear program for the velocity in the intersection of these half-planes closest to the preferred velocity. It handles large numbers of agents in real time.
a.ordered-dithering.summary: Dithering that binarizes each pixel by comparing it against a tiled threshold matrix (the Bayer matrix) indexed by pixel position. Each pixel is processed independently, making it easy to parallelize and implement in hardware.
a.oren-nayar.summary: A diffuse reflectance model that generalizes the Lambertian model by treating a rough surface as a collection of V-shaped grooves and accounting for masking, shadowing and interreflection between facets. It reproduces the flatter appearance of rough objects such as clay or the Moon compared with the Lambertian model.
a.otsu-thresholding.summary: Binarizes an image by choosing the threshold that maximizes the between-class variance of the gray-level histogram. It selects the threshold automatically without parameters.
a.p-stable-lsh.summary: Builds locality-sensitive hashes for L_p distance by projecting points onto random vectors drawn from a p-stable distribution and quantizing the projections into fixed-width intervals.
a.package-merge.summary: An algorithm for optimal prefix codes whose code lengths do not exceed L. It recasts the task as a coin collector's problem and repeats L rounds of 'packaging' the lightest pairs of items and 'merging' them into sorted order, computing length-limited Huffman codes in O(nL) time.
a.packrat-parsing.summary: A parsing method that memoizes the result of applying each rule at each input position in a backtracking recursive-descent parser, achieving linear time while allowing unlimited backtracking and lookahead.
a.paeth-predictor.o0.note: The PNG specification (W3C Recommendation, 1996) cites this article as the source of filter type 4.
a.paeth-predictor.summary: A pixel predictor that computes p = a + b − c from the left (a), upper (b) and upper-left (c) pixels and chooses whichever of the three is closest to p as the prediction. It was adopted as filter type 4 in PNG.
a.paged-attention.summary: An attention algorithm that, like operating-system virtual memory paging, splits the KV cache into fixed-size blocks stored in non-contiguous memory and addressed through a block table. It reduces memory waste in the vLLM serving system.
a.pagerank.summary: An algorithm that ranks the importance of web documents by the stationary distribution of a random surfer on the link structure.
a.paillier.summary: A probabilistic public-key cryptosystem based on the composite residuosity class problem. Multiplying ciphertexts adds the plaintexts, and this additive homomorphism is used in electronic voting and secure aggregation.
a.painters-algorithm.summary: A hidden-surface method that sorts polygons by depth and draws them from back to front so that nearer surfaces overwrite farther ones. Newell et al. added tests and splitting steps for polygons whose depth ranges overlap in order to establish the drawing order.
a.pairing-heap.summary: A self-adjusting heap built from a single multiway tree and pairwise merging that is simple to implement and performs well in practice.
a.pairwise-sorting-network.summary: A sorting network that first compares inputs in pairs, then recursively sorts the two halves and combines them. It has the same number of comparators and the same depth as Batcher's odd-even merge network.
a.paq.summary: A compression method that combines, by weighting, the next-bit predictions of many context models and codes each bit with binary arithmetic coding. Later versions learn the mixing weights online during coding.
a.parallel-tempering.o0.note: Swendsen and Wang's replica Monte Carlo is an early form that exchanges partial configurations between replicas.
a.parallel-tempering.o2.note: Proposed independently in physics under the name exchange Monte Carlo.
a.parallel-tempering.summary: An MCMC method that runs several replica chains at different temperatures in parallel and periodically swaps states between neighboring temperatures under a Metropolis criterion, improving mixing in multimodal distributions.
a.partial-redundancy-elimination.summary: An optimization that finds expressions redundant on only some paths using bidirectional dataflow equations and moves or inserts computations so that the redundancy disappears on all paths. It subsumes common-subexpression elimination and loop-invariant code motion.
a.particle-filter.summary: A sequential Monte Carlo state estimator that represents the posterior by a set of weighted particles and, at each time step, propagates the particles through the state model, weights them by the observation likelihood and resamples. It is used for nonlinear, non-Gaussian models.
a.patchmatch.summary: Quickly computes an approximate nearest-neighbor field between image patches by iterating propagation of good matches from neighboring pixels and random search, starting from a random initialization. Used for image completion, reshuffling, and stereo matching.
a.path-tracing.summary: A technique that computes global illumination by solving the rendering equation via Monte Carlo integration over random path samples.
a.patience-sorting.o0.note: It was posed in the problems section of SIAM Review; a follow-up item with the same title appeared in the same journal in 1963.
a.patience-sorting.summary: A sorting method that deals elements one by one onto piles according to a fixed rule and then merges the piles. The number of piles equals the length of the longest increasing subsequence.
a.paton-cycle-basis.summary: An algorithm that finds a fundamental set of cycles (a cycle basis) of an undirected graph by growing a spanning tree and forming one cycle for each non-tree edge.
a.patricia-trie.summary: A trie that compresses nodes with only one child and stores only the branching bits.
a.paxos.summary: A protocol that reaches consensus on a single value despite non-Byzantine failures through two phases of majority-quorum voting.
a.pbft.summary: A state-machine replication protocol that tolerates up to f Byzantine faults with 3f+1 replicas, fixing the order chosen by the primary through three message phases: pre-prepare, prepare and commit. It preserves safety even in asynchronous networks.
a.pbkdf2.summary: A function that derives a key from a password by repeatedly applying a pseudorandom function (typically HMAC).
a.pca.summary: A linear transformation that reduces dimensionality by rotating the data onto orthogonal axes ordered by decreasing variance.
a.pcg.o0.venue: Harvey Mudd College Technical Report HMC-CS-2014-0905
a.pcg.summary: A family of generators that applies a state-dependent permutation as the output function on an LCG state, achieving high statistical quality with a small state.
a.pcss.summary: A method that finds the average blocker depth in the shadow map, estimates the penumbra width from the light size by similar triangles, and then performs PCF with a kernel of that size, producing shadows that soften with distance from the contact point.
a.pdqsort.o0.note: C++ implementation released before the paper; adopted by the Rust and Go standard libraries
a.pdqsort.summary: An unstable hybrid sort that extends introsort to detect sorted, reverse-sorted, and repeated patterns, and shuffles pivots on adversarial inputs.
a.peano-curve.summary: The first space-filling curve, a continuous map from the unit interval onto the unit square. Geometrically it can be drawn by recursively dividing the square into 3x3 cells and visiting them in order.
a.pearson-hashing.summary: A string hash function that produces an 8-bit hash by mixing each input byte through XOR and a lookup in a 256-byte permutation table.
a.pedersen-commitment.o0.note: The commitment was introduced as a component of the paper's information-theoretically secure verifiable secret sharing scheme.
a.pedersen-commitment.summary: A discrete-logarithm-based commitment that hides a value m as g^m·h^r. It is information-theoretically hiding, computationally binding and additively homomorphic, so it is used in confidential transactions and zero-knowledge proofs.
a.peephole-optimization.summary: A local optimization that slides a small window over a few adjacent instructions of generated code and replaces redundant or inefficient sequences with shorter or faster ones.
a.peg.summary: A recognition-based formal grammar with prioritized choice, which tries alternatives in order and takes the first that succeeds, and syntactic predicates. It is unambiguous and can be processed in linear time with packrat parsing.
a.percentage-closer-filtering.summary: A shadow-map anti-aliasing method that, instead of averaging depth values first, performs the depth comparison at several nearby texels and filters the resulting fraction of shadowed tests. It reduces jagged shadow edges and produces soft boundaries.
a.perceptron.summary: A learning rule for a linear classifier that classifies by whether a weighted sum exceeds a threshold and, on a misclassification, adjusts the weights in the direction of the input.
a.percolator.summary: A distributed transaction protocol that provides cross-row, cross-table snapshot-isolation transactions on top of a distributed key-value store (Bigtable), using a timestamp oracle and a two-phase commit anchored on a primary lock. It also includes notifications for incremental processing.
a.perlin-noise.summary: A gradient noise that produces natural-looking textures by smoothly interpolating random gradients at lattice points.
a.perona-malik.summary: Anisotropic diffusion that iteratively smooths an image with a partial differential equation whose diffusion coefficient decreases with gradient magnitude. It smooths region interiors while preserving edges.
a.peterson-algorithm.summary: An algorithm that guarantees mutual exclusion between two processes using two intent flags and a single turn variable. It is simpler than Dekker's algorithm and is the standard textbook example in operating systems courses.
a.pfordelta.summary: An integer compression scheme that bit-packs most values of a block with a small fixed width b and stores the few values that do not fit in b bits separately as exceptions, patching them in afterwards. Because decoding is branch-free, it is used in column-store databases and inverted indexes.
a.pgz-decoder.summary: An algebraic decoding method for BCH and Reed–Solomon codes that builds a system of linear equations from the syndromes of the received word and solves it for the error-locator polynomial. Peterson developed it for binary BCH codes, and Gorenstein and Zierler extended it to non-binary codes.
a.phi-accrual-failure-detector.summary: A failure detector that estimates the distribution of heartbeat inter-arrival times and outputs the level of suspicion that a node has failed as a continuous value φ instead of a binary verdict. Applications decide by choosing a threshold.
a.philox.summary: A counter-based pseudorandom number generator that takes a counter and a key and applies several multiplication-based mixing rounds to produce random output. Because its only state is the counter, independent parallel streams are easy to create on GPUs and similar hardware.
a.phong-shading.summary: An illumination model and shading technique that interpolates normals per pixel and sums ambient, diffuse, and specular terms.
a.photon-mapping.summary: A two-pass global illumination method that first traces photons from light sources and stores where they hit surfaces, with their energy, in a photon map such as a kd-tree, and then estimates illumination during rendering from the density of nearby photons. It efficiently renders caustics, which converge slowly with path tracing.
a.pie.summary: Active queue management based on proportional-integral control that estimates queueing delay and periodically updates the drop probability from its deviation from a target delay and its trend. It was standardized as RFC 8033.
a.pinocchio.summary: A practical verifiable-computation system that compiles computations into quadratic arithmetic programs (QAPs) and verifies them with pairings. Constant-size proofs can be checked quickly, and it laid the groundwork for later zk-SNARK implementations.
a.plonk.summary: A zk-SNARK that checks circuit wiring with polynomial commitments and a permutation argument. A single universal, updatable trusted setup, independent of any particular circuit, serves many circuits.
a.plsa.summary: A probabilistic topic model that explains document–word co-occurrences as a mixture over latent topic variables and is trained with EM.
a.pohlig-hellman.summary: An algorithm that factors the group order, solves the discrete logarithm in each prime-power-order subgroup, and combines the results with the Chinese remainder theorem. It makes discrete logarithms easy when the group order has only small prime factors.
a.poisson-image-editing.summary: Seamlessly composites images by solving a Poisson equation that preserves the gradient field of the pasted region while matching boundary values to the target image. Used for seamless cloning and compositing.
a.poisson-surface-reconstruction.summary: A method that treats the normals of an oriented point cloud as samples of the gradient of an indicator function, solves a Poisson equation on an octree for the indicator function that fits them, and extracts its isosurface as the surface. Solving globally makes it robust to noise and yields watertight surfaces.
a.polar-code.o1.note: The journal version of the same paper.
a.polar-code.summary: A code that exploits channel polarization, placing information bits on the most reliable synthesized bit channels and frozen bits on the rest. It provably achieves the capacity of symmetric binary-input memoryless channels and is used for 5G control channels.
a.pollard-brent.summary: An improvement of Pollard's rho factorization that replaces Floyd's cycle detection with Brent's power-of-two cycle detection and batches several differences into one gcd. It reduces the function evaluations and gcds per iteration.
a.pollard-kangaroo.summary: An algorithm that finds a discrete logarithm known to lie in an interval [a, b] by making a tame and a wild pseudo-random walk meet. It takes about √w steps for an interval of width w.
a.pollard-p-minus-1.summary: A factorization algorithm that computes a^M mod n for a smooth exponent M and obtains a factor from gcd(a^M−1, n). It is effective when p−1 has only small prime factors for some prime factor p.
a.pollard-rho-log.summary: An algorithm that computes discrete logarithms by finding a collision in a pseudo-random walk that partitions group elements into three classes. It needs about √n time like baby-step giant-step but only near-constant memory.
a.pollard-rho.summary: An integer factorization algorithm that iterates a pseudo-random map such as x ↦ x²+c (mod n) and extracts a factor via a gcd when the sequence collides modulo a prime factor. It finds a small factor p in about √p steps.
a.poly1305.summary: A one-time MAC that produces a message authentication tag by polynomial evaluation over the prime field of order 2¹³⁰−5.
a.polyphase-merge-sort.summary: An external merge sort that distributes the initial runs over the tapes in unequal, Fibonacci-like counts and keeps merging onto the one empty tape at each phase. It reduces the number of merge passes when few tapes are available.
a.porter-stemmer.summary: A stemming algorithm that strips English suffixes by applying, in several steps, suffix rules conditioned on the measure of the word's consonant–vowel pattern. It is widely used in information retrieval to conflate words with the same stem.
a.position-based-dynamics.o0.note: The following year it appeared as a paper with the same title in the Journal of Visual Communication and Image Representation 18(2) (doi:10.1016/j.jvcir.2007.01.005).
a.position-based-dynamics.summary: A simulation method that first predicts positions from velocities, then projects particle positions directly onto constraints such as distance, bending and collision in a Gauss–Seidel manner, and finally recomputes velocities from the change in position. Unconditionally stable and easy to control, it is widely used for cloth and soft bodies in games.
a.position-based-fluids.summary: A method that formulates an incompressibility constraint keeping each particle's SPH-estimated density constant and solves it with the iterative constraint projection of position-based dynamics, simulating particle fluids stably even with large time steps.
a.powell-method.summary: A derivative-free multivariate minimization method that performs successive one-dimensional minimizations along a set of directions and updates the set so that the directions become mutually conjugate.
a.power-iteration.summary: A method that repeatedly multiplies a vector by the matrix and normalizes it to find the eigenvalue of largest magnitude and its eigenvector. It is used for large sparse matrices, for example in PageRank computation.
a.powersort.o0.note: The same paper also introduced Peeksort.
a.powersort.summary: A stable mergesort that detects natural runs and decides the merge order from the 'power' of the boundary between neighbouring runs. It adapts nearly optimally to existing runs and is used as the merge-ordering strategy of CPython's list.sort.
a.ppm.summary: An adaptive statistical compression method that estimates the next symbol's probability from contexts of several orders formed by the preceding symbols, sending an escape symbol and falling back to a shorter context when the symbol has not been seen in a longer one. The estimated probabilities are coded with arithmetic coding.
a.ppmd.summary: A compression method implementing PPMII, a PPM variant that initializes the statistics of new contexts by information inheritance and uses secondary escape estimation (SEE). Archivers such as 7-Zip and RAR offer it as a method for compressing text.
a.ppo.summary: A first-order policy-gradient algorithm that uses a clipped surrogate objective, limiting the probability ratio to an interval so that the policy does not change too much at once, while performing several minibatch updates on the same samples.
a.pratt-parsing.summary: Top-down operator-precedence parsing in which each token carries a binding power and prefix/infix handlers, and during recursive descent an expression is extended only while the next operator binds more tightly than the current threshold.
a.pregel.summary: A vertex-centric model for large-scale graph processing in which, in each superstep, every vertex updates its value from messages received in the previous step and sends messages to its neighbors, terminating when all vertices vote to halt.
a.present-cipher.summary: A lightweight 64-bit block cipher designed for minimal hardware area. It is a 31-round SPN using a single 4-bit S-box and a bit permutation, standardized in ISO/IEC 29192-2.
a.prim.o0.title: O jistém problému minimálním (letter to Borůvka)
a.prim.summary: A minimum spanning tree algorithm that starts from a single vertex and repeatedly adds the minimum-weight edge incident to the tree.
a.principal-variation-search.summary: An alpha–beta enhancement that searches only the first child (the principal variation) with the full window, tests the remaining children quickly with a null window, and re-searches only when a test fails. It is most effective when move ordering is good.
a.prioritized-experience-replay.summary: A replay scheme that samples transitions with large temporal-difference error more often from the experience replay buffer and corrects the resulting bias with importance-sampling weights.
a.priority-ceiling.summary: A real-time synchronization protocol that assigns each resource a ceiling equal to the highest priority of the tasks using it and grants a lock only when the ceiling condition holds, preventing deadlock and chained blocking.
a.priority-inheritance.summary: A real-time synchronization protocol that bounds priority inversion: when a low-priority task holds a resource blocking a higher-priority task, it temporarily inherits that task's priority.
a.priority-search-tree.summary: A tree that stores points so that it is a binary search tree on x and heap-ordered on y at the same time. It answers three-sided range queries in O(log n + k) time and supports updates in O(log n) time.
a.product-quantization.summary: A vector compression and approximate nearest-neighbor search technique that splits vectors into subspaces, quantizes each with its own k-means codebook, and approximates distances quickly from the combination of sub-codes.
a.progressive-meshes.summary: A multiresolution mesh representation that stores a mesh as a coarse base mesh obtained by repeated edge collapses together with the sequence of vertex splits that reverses them. Any level of detail can be recovered continuously, which supports progressive transmission and level-of-detail rendering.
a.proof-number-search.summary: A best-first search over AND/OR trees that keeps, for each node, the minimum number of leaves that must still be solved to prove or disprove it (proof and disproof numbers) and expands the most-proving node. Used to solve game positions as wins or losses.
a.prr.summary: A fast-recovery method that, during TCP loss recovery, sends new data in proportion to the data acknowledged so that the congestion window shrinks smoothly to its target. It is described in RFC 6937 and is the default behavior in Linux.
a.ptrs.summary: An algorithm that generates Poisson variates by the transformed rejection method: a uniform variate is mapped through an approximate inverse and then corrected with a squeeze-region test and a rejection step. It runs in constant expected time even for large means.
a.push-relabel.summary: A maximum-flow algorithm that maintains a preflow allowing excess at vertices, repeatedly pushing excess to neighbors one label lower and relabeling vertices that cannot push. It does not search for augmenting paths and has variants such as FIFO and highest-label selection.
a.q-coder.summary: An adaptive binary arithmetic coder implemented without multiplication, using additions, shifts and a state table for probability estimation. Its variants, the QM and MQ coders, are used in JBIG, JPEG and JPEG 2000.
a.q-learning.o0.note: First proposed in this PhD thesis; the convergence proof appeared in Watkins and Dayan (1992), doi:10.1007/BF00992698.
a.q-learning.summary: A model-free, off-policy reinforcement-learning algorithm that updates the action-value function Q by temporal differences toward the maximum action value of the next state.
a.qgram-distance.summary: The L1 distance between the occurrence-count vectors of the length-q substrings (q-grams) of two strings. It is computable in linear time and can be used to derive a lower bound on edit distance, which makes it useful for filtering in approximate search.
a.qhull.summary: A convex hull algorithm and implementation that generalizes Quickhull to arbitrary dimensions and is designed to handle numerical error.
a.qlora.summary: A fine-tuning method that trains LoRA adapters on top of a frozen pretrained model quantized to 4-bit NormalFloat. Double quantization and paged optimizers further reduce memory.
a.qoi.summary: A simple lossless image format that scans each pixel once and encodes it as one of: a run of the previous pixel, an index into a hash table of 64 recently seen colors, a small difference from the previous pixel, or the full RGB(A) value.
a.qr-algorithm.summary: An eigenvalue algorithm that repeatedly factors a matrix as QR and multiplies the factors in reverse order. Combined with Hessenberg reduction and shifts, it is the standard method for dense eigenvalue problems.
a.quadratic-probing.summary: An open-addressing collision strategy in which the probe offset grows as a quadratic function of the probe number. It reduces the primary clustering of linear probing.
a.quadratic-sieve.o0.note: A widely cited expository paper is 'The Quadratic Sieve Factoring Algorithm' in the EUROCRYPT '84 proceedings (LNCS 209, 1985).
a.quadratic-sieve.summary: A factorization algorithm that sieves values of x²−n for those that factor over a base of small primes and uses linear algebra to build a congruence of squares x² ≡ y² (mod n). It is a widely used general-purpose method for integers up to about 100 digits.
a.quadric-error-metrics.summary: A mesh simplification method that associates with each vertex a 4×4 quadric matrix representing the sum of squared distances to the planes of its surrounding faces and contracts vertex pairs in order of increasing cost. Fast and good at preserving shape, it is widely used in mesh simplification tools.
a.quadtree.summary: A tree that recursively divides two-dimensional space into four quadrants around a point or region. It is used for point lookup, region queries and image representation.
a.quick-search.summary: A Boyer–Moore-family string search algorithm that, after each attempt, determines the shift from the text character immediately following the current window. Characters inside the window may be compared in any order, and a shift can be as large as the pattern length plus one.
a.quickhull.summary: A divide-and-conquer convex hull algorithm that splits the region at the farthest point, discards interior points, and recurses.
a.quickselect.summary: A selection algorithm that applies quicksort's partitioning recursively to only one side, finding the kth element in linear average time.
a.quicksort.o0.note: Detailed analysis in The Computer Journal 5(1), 1962
a.quicksort.summary: A divide-and-conquer sort that partitions the array around a pivot and recursively sorts both sides. It runs in O(n log n) average time and sorts in place.
a.quotient-filter.o0.note: The name "quotient filter" was coined in this paper; the underlying compact hash table was described by Cleary (1984). An extended version appeared in PVLDB 5(11), 2012.
