a.quotient-filter.summary: An approximate membership filter that splits each hash into a quotient and a remainder, stores the remainder near the slot named by the quotient, and recovers the quotient using linear probing and metadata bits. It supports deletion, merging and resizing.
a.r-cnn.summary: An object detection method that extracts CNN features from each region proposal produced by selective search and classifies them with SVMs. The CNN is pretrained on large-scale classification data and fine-tuned for detection.
a.r-star-tree.summary: A spatial index that changes the R-tree insertion algorithm to jointly minimize the area, overlap and margin of node regions, and forcibly reinserts some entries of overflowing nodes. It is used in spatial index implementations such as SQLite and Boost.Geometry.
a.r-tree.summary: A height-balanced tree that groups spatial objects by minimum bounding rectangles. It is the standard index for spatial databases.
a.rabin-karp.summary: A string search that finds pattern candidates by updating the hash of the text window in constant time with a rolling hash.
a.rader-fft.summary: An algorithm that converts a prime-length DFT into a cyclic convolution of length p−1 via a primitive-root permutation.
a.radiosity.summary: A global illumination method that divides a scene into diffuse patches and computes interreflected lighting by solving a linear system for the energy exchange expressed with form factors between patches. It brought radiative heat-transfer techniques into graphics, and its solution is view-independent.
a.radix-heap.summary: A priority queue for monotone integer keys that places elements in buckets of exponentially growing width according to their difference from the last extracted minimum. It is used in Dijkstra's algorithm on graphs with integer edge weights at most C, and the paper also gives a variant running in O(m + n√log C) time.
a.radix-sort.o0.note: Mechanical radix sorting on punched-card machines was in use earlier
a.radix-sort.summary: A non-comparison sort that repeatedly applies a stable sort digit by digit. The canonical form applies counting sort starting from the least significant digit (LSD).
a.raft.summary: A consensus algorithm designed for understandability by separating leader election, log replication, and safety.
a.raita.summary: A variant of Boyer–Moore–Horspool search that compares the last, first and middle characters of the window before checking the rest. On natural-language text it detects mismatches early and reduces the number of comparisons.
a.ramalingam-reps.summary: A dynamic (incremental) shortest-path algorithm that, after edges are inserted, deleted, or reweighted, recomputes only the affected vertices. It was presented as DynamicSWSF-FP within a grammar-problem framework that generalizes the shortest-path problem.
a.ramer-douglas-peucker.summary: Line simplification algorithm that, if the farthest point from the segment joining a polyline's endpoints is farther than a tolerance, splits there and recurses, and otherwise drops all intermediate points.
a.random-forest.summary: An ensemble method that grows weakly correlated decision trees using bagged samples and random feature selection at each node, and combines them by voting.
a.random-subspace.summary: An ensemble method that trains a tree on each random subset of the features and combines the trees.
a.randomized-bst.summary: A binary search tree that inserts a new element at the root of a subtree with probability 1/(n+1), so the tree always has the same distribution as one built from a random insertion order. Nodes store subtree sizes instead of priorities, and union and split operations are supported.
a.randomized-svd.summary: A low-rank approximation method that multiplies the matrix by a random matrix to find a subspace approximating its range, then computes a small SVD on that subspace. It is used for dimensionality reduction of large data.
a.range-coding.summary: An entropy coding method that implements arithmetic coding with large integer ranges and byte-wise output.
a.range-tree.summary: A multilevel tree in which each node of a balanced binary search tree on one coordinate carries an auxiliary structure on the next coordinate for the points in its subtree. It answers d-dimensional orthogonal range queries in O(log^d n + k) time.
a.rank-pairing-heap.summary: A heap made of a list of half-trees, like a pairing heap, that uses node ranks for balance. Without cascading cuts it matches the amortized bounds of Fibonacci heaps: O(1) decrease-key and O(log n) delete-min.
a.rank-select-bitvector.summary: A succinct data structure that adds an o(n)-bit auxiliary index to an n-bit string so that the number of 1s up to a position (rank) and the position of the i-th 1 (select) can be found quickly. It is a basic building block of succinct trees, wavelet trees and compressed indexes.
a.ranlux.summary: A pseudorandom generator that reduces correlations in Marsaglia–Zaman subtract-with-borrow output by using a block of numbers and discarding the rest. The fraction discarded, the luxury level, trades speed for quality.
a.ransac.summary: A robust estimation method that repeatedly fits a model to a randomly drawn minimal sample, counts the inliers within an error tolerance, and keeps the model with the most support. Used to fit models to data with many outliers.
a.raptor-code.summary: A fountain code that first encodes the source symbols with a high-rate precode and then applies an LT code, giving linear-time encoding and decoding. It is used in standards such as RaptorQ (RFC 6330).
a.raptor.summary: A public-transit routing algorithm that, in round k, scans once each route serving stops improved in the previous round to update the earliest arrival times reachable with at most k−1 transfers, yielding journeys that are Pareto-optimal in arrival time and number of transfers. It works directly on timetable arrays without a priority queue.
a.ratcliff-obershelp.o0.note: The algorithm itself was developed in 1983 by Ratcliff and John A. Obershelp.
a.ratcliff-obershelp.summary: A similarity measure that finds the longest common substring of two strings and recursively applies the same step to the remaining parts on its left and right, counting matched characters. The similarity is twice the number of matched characters divided by the total length of both strings.
a.rate-monotonic-scheduling.summary: A real-time scheduling scheme that assigns higher fixed priorities to tasks with shorter periods. It is optimal among fixed-priority schemes, and n tasks always meet their deadlines if total utilization is at most n(2^(1/n)−1).
a.ray-casting.summary: A rendering technique that casts a ray from the viewpoint through each pixel and determines visibility and shading from the first object hit.
a.rc5.summary: A block cipher whose word size, number of rounds and key length are all parameters. Its core operation is the data-dependent bit rotation.
a.rc6.summary: A 128-bit block cipher derived from RC5 and submitted to the AES competition. It works on four 32-bit words and adds integer multiplication to data-dependent rotations.
a.rcu.o0.note: According to the Linux kernel's RCU bibliography (Documentation/RCU/RTFP.txt), this is the first publication of the DYNIX/ptx RCU mechanism; the conference paper under the name 'Read-Copy Update' is McKenney and Slingwine, PDCS 1998.
a.rcu.summary: A synchronization technique in which readers proceed without locks, while updaters modify a copy, swap in a pointer to it, and free the old version only after a grace period in which all pre-existing readers have finished. It is used extensively in the Linux kernel.
a.rdd.summary: An in-memory distributed data abstraction in which immutable partitioned collections are created only through coarse-grained transformations and the lineage of each dataset is recorded so that lost partitions can be recomputed. It is the core of Apache Spark.
a.re-pair.summary: An offline compression algorithm that builds a grammar (dictionary) by repeatedly replacing the most frequent pair of adjacent symbols with a new symbol until every pair occurs only once. It runs in linear time and is used in grammar-based compression and compressed data structures.
a.readers-writer-lock.summary: A synchronization scheme that allows multiple readers to access shared data concurrently while giving a writer exclusive access. There are reader-preference and writer-preference solutions.
a.realnvp.summary: A normalizing-flow model built from affine coupling layers that apply both scaling and translation, with a multi-scale architecture that allows exact log-likelihood evaluation and sampling.
a.recsplit.summary: A minimal perfect hashing method that recursively splits the key set into small pieces and finds a bijective hash for each leaf by exhaustive search. Its space usage comes close to the theoretical lower bound.
a.red-black-tree.summary: A self-balancing binary search tree that colors each node red or black and uses coloring rules to keep the height O(log n).
a.red.summary: Active queue management that tracks the average queue length with an exponentially weighted moving average and, between two thresholds, drops or marks packets early with a probability that grows with that average.
a.reed-solomon.summary: A non-binary linear code that treats the message as coefficients of a polynomial over a finite field and uses its values at many points as the codeword. With n−k check symbols it corrects up to (n−k)/2 symbol errors, and it is used in CDs, QR codes, storage devices and more.
a.reference-counting.summary: A memory management technique that counts the references to each object and reclaims it as soon as the count reaches zero.
a.regev-lwe.summary: A public-key cryptosystem built on the learning-with-errors (LWE) problem of solving noisy linear equations, which the paper introduced. Its security reduces to the quantum hardness of worst-case lattice problems, and it became the foundation of modern lattice cryptography.
a.reinforce.summary: A Monte Carlo policy-gradient algorithm that estimates the gradient of expected reward by multiplying the return of an episode by the gradient of the policy's log-probability, and updates the parameters of a stochastic policy by gradient ascent.
a.reinhard-tone-mapping.summary: An HDR tone mapping method that sets exposure from the scene's log-average luminance, compresses high luminances with a curve of the form L/(1+L), and optionally adds a local operator mimicking dodging and burning. It draws on the photographic Zone System.
a.relu.o0.note: First used as a mathematical abstraction of biological neural networks.
a.relu.o1.note: Used for visual feature extraction in a multilayered network.
a.relu.o2.note: Named rectified linear units and applied to restricted Boltzmann machines, popularizing the function in deep learning.
a.relu.summary: The activation function max(0, x), which passes positive inputs unchanged and outputs zero otherwise. By mitigating vanishing gradients it became the default activation in deep networks.
a.rendezvous-hashing.summary: Highest random weight hashing, which selects the node whose key–node pair has the largest hash weight.
a.reservoir-sampling-l.summary: A reservoir sampling algorithm that directly generates, from a geometric distribution, how many records to skip before the next replacement, maintaining the sample in O(k(1+log(N/k))) expected time.
a.reservoir-sampling.o0.note: The paper credits the basic reservoir algorithm (Algorithm R) to Alan Waterman; its main result is Algorithm Z.
a.reservoir-sampling.summary: A sampling technique that maintains a uniform random sample of size k in one pass over a stream whose length is not known in advance. Vitter's paper introduced Algorithm Z, which generates the number of records to skip directly.
a.resnet.summary: An architecture that adds identity shortcut connections so that layers learn residual functions, making it possible to train networks with hundreds of layers.
a.restir.summary: A method that resamples candidate light samples per pixel with weighted reservoir sampling and reuses the reservoirs across previous frames and neighboring pixels to estimate direct lighting from many lights in real time. It renders dynamic scenes with millions of lights using few rays per pixel.
a.reversible-jump-mcmc.summary: An MCMC method that handles proposals jumping between models of different dimension with a dimension-matching transformation and a Metropolis–Hastings acceptance probability that includes the Jacobian, performing model selection and parameter estimation together.
a.ribbon-filter.summary: A static approximate membership filter built by expressing each key as a linear equation whose coefficients form a short random band and solving the system by Gaussian elimination. It is implemented in RocksDB as an alternative to Bloom filters.
a.ricart-agrawala.summary: A distributed mutual exclusion algorithm in which a node wishing to enter the critical section sends a timestamped request to all other nodes and enters after receiving replies from all of them. Each entry costs 2(N−1) messages.
a.rice-coding.summary: An integer code that restricts the Golomb parameter to a power of two 2^k, so the remainder is written as k plain bits. Because it needs only bit operations, it is used to code residuals in lossless audio and image codecs such as FLAC.
a.richardson-extrapolation.summary: A technique that combines approximations computed with different step sizes according to the asymptotic error expansion, eliminating the leading error term to obtain a more accurate value. It underlies Romberg integration and extrapolation methods for ODEs.
a.ridders-method.summary: A bracketing root-finding method that multiplies the function by an exponential factor, determined from the value at the interval midpoint, to make it linear and then applies a false-position step. It keeps a bracket while converging quadratically per iteration.
a.ridge-regression.summary: A regression that adds a squared L2-norm penalty on the coefficients to the least-squares objective, shrinking them toward zero. It stabilizes estimates under multicollinearity.
a.ring-lwe.summary: A lattice problem, and encryption based on it, that moves LWE onto polynomial rings to shrink keys and computation. Its security reduces to the worst-case hardness of ideal-lattice problems, and it underlies many lattice and homomorphic schemes.
a.rip.o0.note: The specification documents the protocol used by the routed program of 4.3BSD.
a.rip.summary: A distance-vector routing protocol in which routers periodically exchange per-destination hop-count vectors with neighbors and update routes in the Bellman–Ford manner. Split horizon and related rules mitigate the count-to-infinity problem.
a.ripemd-160.summary: A 160-bit hash function that strengthens the MD4-family design with two parallel computation lines. It is used together with SHA-256 to derive Bitcoin addresses.
a.rlhf.summary: A method that learns a reward model from human comparisons between pairs of behavior segments and trains a policy with reinforcement learning on that reward. It was later used to align large language models.
a.rmsnorm.summary: A normalization that drops mean-centering from layer normalization and rescales activations only by their root mean square. Its lower cost has led to its use in large language models such as LLaMA.
a.rmsprop.summary: An adaptive optimizer that replaces the accumulated sum in AdaGrad with an exponential moving average, preventing the learning rate from decaying to zero.
a.roaring.summary: A compressed bitmap that splits a set of 32-bit integers into chunks by their upper 16 bits and stores each chunk as a sorted array or a bitmap depending on its cardinality (run containers were added later). Because its set operations are fast, it is used in systems such as Lucene, Spark and Druid.
a.roberta.summary: A language model that revisits BERT pretraining by removing next-sentence prediction and using dynamic masking, larger batches, and more data and training steps.
a.robin-hood-hashing.summary: A linear-probing technique that makes keys yield their slots to keys displaced farther from their home positions, reducing the variance of probe lengths.
a.romberg.summary: A numerical integration method that repeatedly applies Richardson extrapolation to trapezoidal-rule values with successively halved step sizes, building a triangular table of increasingly accurate estimates.
a.rope-string.summary: A data structure that represents a long string as a binary tree whose leaves hold short string pieces. Concatenation and substring extraction are done without copying the whole string.
a.rope.summary: A positional encoding that rotates query and key vectors by angles proportional to position so that relative position appears in their dot product.
a.rosenbrock-method.summary: Linearly implicit Runge–Kutta-type methods that use the Jacobian so that each stage requires only the solution of a linear system. They solve stiff ODEs without Newton iterations.
a.rsa-pss.summary: A probabilistic signature scheme that encodes the message with a hash and a random salt before signing it with RSA. It has a tight security proof relative to the RSA problem in the random-oracle model and is used in PKCS #1 v2.1 and TLS 1.3.
a.rsa.summary: A public-key encryption and digital signature scheme based on the assumed hardness of factoring large composite numbers.
a.rts-smoother.summary: A fixed-interval smoother that runs a Kalman filter forward in time and then recurses backward from the final time step to obtain smoothed state estimates and covariances that incorporate future observations.
a.runge-kutta-fehlberg.summary: An embedded Runge–Kutta method that estimates the local error from the difference between fourth- and fifth-order formulas sharing the same stages and adjusts the step size automatically.
a.runge-kutta.summary: One-step numerical methods for ordinary differential equations that evaluate the slope at several points within a step and combine them with weights. The classical fourth-order method (RK4) is widely used.
a.ruppert-refinement.summary: Delaunay refinement algorithm that repeatedly inserts the circumcenter of a triangle with a small angle into the Delaunay triangulation of a planar straight-line graph, splitting a boundary segment in half instead whenever the new point would encroach on the segment's diametral circle. It produces quality meshes with a guaranteed minimum angle.
a.rvo.summary: Multi-agent collision avoidance that modifies the velocity obstacle so that each agent, assuming the other reciprocates, chooses a velocity halfway between its current velocity and one outside the velocity obstacle. It reduces the oscillations that arise with plain velocity obstacles.
a.ryu.summary: A floating-point-to-string conversion algorithm that handles the bounds of the rounding interval with precomputed tables and fixed-width integer multiplications to produce the shortest round-trip decimal representation for every input.
a.s-hull.summary: Algorithm that sorts points by distance from a seed point, sweeps radially while growing a convex hull to build a non-overlapping triangulation, and then applies edge flips to obtain the Delaunay triangulation.
a.s4.summary: A sequence model that discretizes a continuous-time linear state space model and parameterizes the state matrix with a normal-plus-low-rank structure to process long sequences efficiently.
a.sa-is.summary: A suffix array construction algorithm that classifies suffixes as S-type or L-type, sorts only the LMS substrings first and then induces the order of the remaining suffixes from them. It runs in linear time and is implemented with little extra space.
a.sac.summary: An actor-critic algorithm that, under a maximum-entropy objective rewarding policy entropy as well as return, trains a stochastic actor and soft value-function critics off-policy from a replay buffer.
a.salsa.summary: A link-analysis method that ranks pages by the stationary distributions of random walks alternating between the hub side and the authority side of the link graph. It reduces the TKC effect, in which HITS concentrates scores on a dense subgraph.
a.salsa20.summary: A 20-round stream cipher built solely from addition, rotation, and XOR (ARX).
a.samplesort.summary: A sort that sorts a random sample to obtain several splitters, distributes the elements into the resulting buckets and sorts each bucket recursively. It generalises quicksort to many pivots and became a standard approach for parallel sorting.
a.sarsa.o0.note: Published under the name 'Modified Connectionist Q-Learning' (MCQ-L); the name SARSA was later given by Sutton.
a.sarsa.summary: An on-policy temporal-difference control algorithm that updates Q toward the value of the action actually taken next. Its name comes from the tuple (state, action, reward, next state, next action).
a.sbb-tree.summary: A balanced tree that represents a 2-3-4 B-tree as a binary tree. It is the direct predecessor of the red-black tree.
a.scanline-rendering.summary: A hidden-surface and rendering method that processes the image one horizontal scanline at a time and determines visible surfaces by sorting the polygon spans that intersect each scanline. It exploits coherence between adjacent scanlines with an active edge list.
a.scapegoat-tree.o0.note: Presented the same rebuilding scheme before Galperin and Rivest; Andersson later called it the general balanced tree.
a.scapegoat-tree.summary: A binary search tree that keeps no balance data in its nodes; when an insertion makes the tree too deep, it rebuilds the entire subtree of an unbalanced ancestor (the scapegoat). Searches take O(log n) worst-case time and updates O(log n) amortized time.
a.sccp.o0.note: An extended version operating on SSA form appeared under the same title in TOPLAS 13(2) in 1991.
a.sccp.summary: A constant-propagation algorithm that tracks SSA edges and executable control-flow edges together on worklists, discovering constant values and unreachable branches at the same time.
a.schieber-vishkin-lca.summary: An algorithm that maps a tree onto a complete binary tree using the lowest set bit of node numbers and finds the LCA with a few bit operations. It keeps linear-time preprocessing and constant-time queries while simplifying the Harel–Tarjan method, and it extends to parallel computation.
a.schlick-fresnel.summary: A formula that approximates Fresnel reflectance using the normal-incidence reflectance F0 and a (1 - cos θ)^5 term. Being much cheaper than the exact Fresnel equations, it is standard in real-time physically based shading.
a.schnorr-signature.summary: A short, efficient signature obtained by applying the Fiat–Shamir transform to a discrete-logarithm-based identification protocol.
a.schonhage-strassen.summary: An algorithm that multiplies integers in O(n log n log log n) using a number-theoretic FFT over a ring of integers modulo a Fermat number.
a.scrypt.summary: A memory-hard key derivation function that uses the Salsa20/8 core and a large memory array.
a.seam-carving.summary: Content-aware image resizing that finds connected pixel paths (seams) of minimum energy (gradient) by dynamic programming and removes or inserts them. It changes the aspect ratio while preserving important content.
a.seed.o0.note: Issued as a Telecommunications Technology Association (TTA) standard; RFC 4009 and RFC 4269 cite this standard as the source of SEED.
a.seed.summary: A 128-bit block cipher developed by Korea's KISA. It is a 16-round Feistel network that became a Korean national standard and was also published as an IETF RFC.
a.segment-tree.o0.note: An unpublished technical report, cited as the origin of the segment tree by de Berg et al., Computational Geometry: Algorithms and Applications.
a.segment-tree.summary: A data structure that builds a balanced binary tree over the elementary intervals defined by segment endpoints and stores at each node the segments that fully cover its range. It answers stabbing queries and is widely adapted for range-sum and range-minimum queries over arrays.
a.segmented-sieve.summary: A variant of the sieve of Eratosthenes that first finds the primes up to √N and then crosses out their multiples block by block over cache-sized segments of a range [L, R). It reduces memory to about O(√N), allowing primes to be enumerated over large ranges.
a.seidel-lp.summary: Randomized incremental linear programming algorithm that adds constraints in random order and, when a constraint violates the current optimum, recursively solves a problem of one lower dimension on that constraint's bounding hyperplane. It takes expected O(d! n) time in fixed dimension d.
a.seidel-trapezoidation.summary: Randomized incremental algorithm that inserts segments in random order while updating a trapezoidal decomposition together with a point-location structure. For a simple polygon it builds the trapezoidal decomposition in expected O(n log* n) time and uses it to triangulate the polygon.
a.self-organizing-map.summary: An unsupervised competitive-learning network that pulls the weights of the best-matching neuron and its lattice neighbors toward each input. It maps high-dimensional data onto a low-dimensional lattice while preserving topology.
a.selinger-optimizer.summary: A relational query optimization algorithm that estimates the cost of access paths and join methods with a cost model and uses dynamic programming over subsets of relations, together with 'interesting orders', to find the cheapest join order.
a.sellers-algorithm.summary: An approximate string search algorithm that sets the first row of the edit-distance dynamic programming table to zero so that a match may start at any text position. It finds the end positions of text substrings within distance k of the pattern in O(mn) time.
a.semaphore.o0.note: This English manuscript defines the P and V operations; the semaphore concept also appears in the earlier Dutch manuscript EWD74.
a.semaphore.summary: A synchronization primitive consisting of a non-negative integer with atomic P (wait) and V (signal) operations, used for mutual exclusion and synchronization between processes. It comes in binary and counting forms.
a.semi-global-matching.summary: Stereo matching that adds disparity-smoothness penalties to per-pixel matching costs, aggregates costs by dynamic programming along 1-D paths in several directions (typically 8 to 16), and sums them to choose disparities. It approximates global optimization while remaining fast.
a.sentencepiece.summary: A language-independent tokenizer and detokenizer that treats whitespace as an ordinary symbol and trains BPE or unigram language model subword models directly from raw text without pre-tokenization.
a.seq2seq.summary: A neural machine translation architecture in which an encoder RNN summarizes the input sequence as a vector and a decoder RNN generates the output sequence.
a.sequitur.summary: A linear-time algorithm that reads the input one symbol at a time and incrementally rewrites a context-free grammar so that two constraints hold: no pair of adjacent symbols appears more than once, and every rule is used more than once. The resulting grammar is used for compression and for inferring hierarchical structure.
a.serializable-snapshot-isolation.summar: A concurrency-control technique that tracks read-write antidependencies between transactions on top of snapshot isolation and aborts a transaction when a structure of two consecutive antidependencies that could lead to a non-serializable execution appears, guaranteeing serializability. It is used for PostgreSQL's SERIALIZABLE level.
a.serpent.summary: A 128-bit block cipher that was an AES finalist. It is a 32-round substitution–permutation network of 4-bit S-boxes and a linear transform, designed for bitslice implementation.
a.sethi-ullman.summary: A method that labels each node of an expression tree with the minimum number of registers needed to evaluate its subexpression and evaluates the more demanding child first, producing optimal code.
a.sfmt.summary: A pseudorandom generator that recasts the Mersenne Twister recurrence on 128-bit units so that SIMD instructions update several words at once. It is faster than the original Mersenne Twister at comparable periods.
a.sgd.summary: A stochastic approximation method for optimization that updates using the noisy gradient of a single sample or a minibatch instead of the full gradient.
a.sgdr.summary: A learning-rate schedule that decays the rate along a cosine curve and periodically resets it to its initial value. The restart period can grow over time.
a.sh-irradiance.summary: A method that exploits the fact that, when environment lighting is expanded in spherical harmonics, diffuse irradiance is approximated accurately by the first nine coefficients (up to order 2), so irradiance is computed as a quadratic polynomial in the surface normal. It is used for diffuse ambient lighting in real-time engines.
a.sha-1.summary: A 160-bit hash that follows the design principles of MD4. A practical collision was published in 2017.
a.sha-2.summary: The SHA-224/256/384/512 family of hashes, using the Merkle–Damgård construction and a Davies–Meyer compression function.
a.sha-3.o0.title: Keccak (SHA-3 competition submission)
a.sha-3.summary: A hash that applies the sponge construction to the Keccak-f permutation. It is the winner of the NIST SHA-3 competition.
a.shadow-mapping.summary: A technique that renders a depth buffer from the light's viewpoint and then determines shadows by comparing each screen pixel's distance to the light against it.
a.shadow-volumes.summary: A method that extrudes the silhouette edges of objects as seen from the light into polygonal volumes enclosing the shadowed region of space, and decides shadowing by whether a surface point lies inside such a volume. It later became widespread through real-time implementations using the stencil buffer.
a.shamir-secret-sharing.summary: A (k, n) threshold scheme that hands out n distinct points of a degree-(k−1) polynomial whose constant term is the secret, so that any k shares recover the secret by Lagrange interpolation. Fewer than k shares reveal nothing about the secret.
a.shamos-hoey.summary: Plane-sweep algorithm that processes segment endpoints in x order, keeps the segments crossing the sweep line in a balanced binary search tree, and tests only segments that become neighbours, deciding in O(n log n) time whether any two of n segments intersect.
a.shannon-fano.summary: A method that builds a prefix code by sorting symbols by probability and repeatedly splitting them into two groups of similar cumulative probability.
a.shellsort.summary: A sort that performs insertion sort on subsequences with decreasing gaps, moving elements long distances in a single step.
a.shi-tomasi.summary: A corner detector that selects points whose smaller eigenvalue of the structure tensor exceeds a threshold as good features to track. The selection criterion is derived from how a feature tracker operates.
a.shift-or.o1.note: Journal version with the same title.
a.shift-or.summary: A string search algorithm that keeps, in a single bit vector, which prefixes of the pattern match ending at the current text position, updating it with a shift and an OR for each character. When the pattern fits in a machine word it runs in time linear in the text length.
a.shunting-yard.summary: An algorithm that reads an infix expression from left to right, outputs operands immediately and pushes operators on a stack, popping stacked operators first according to precedence and associativity, to convert the expression to postfix (Reverse Polish) notation.
a.sieve-of-atkin.summary: A sieve that marks prime candidates by testing the number of solutions to quadratic forms.
a.sieve-of-eratosthenes.o0.title: As reported in Nicomachus, Introduction to Arithmetic
a.sieve-of-eratosthenes.summary: A sieve that finds all primes up to a bound by crossing out the multiples of each prime, starting from the smallest.
a.sift.summary: A local feature that finds keypoints as extrema in a difference-of-Gaussians scale space, assigns a dominant orientation, and builds a 128-dimensional descriptor from histograms of surrounding gradient orientations. It is invariant to scale and rotation.
a.sigma-key-exchange.summary: A family of authenticated key-exchange protocols following the 'SIGn-and-MAc' approach: parties sign the Diffie–Hellman values and MAC their identities, providing identity protection and mutual authentication. It underlies the signature modes of IKE (IPsec) and the design of the TLS 1.3 handshake.
a.simclr.summary: A self-supervised representation learning method that uses a contrastive loss to pull together the representations of two differently augmented views of the same image and push apart those of other images in the batch.
a.simhash.summary: A locality-sensitive hashing scheme that turns a vector into a bit string of signs with respect to random hyperplanes, so that the Hamming distance between bit strings estimates cosine similarity (angle). It is used for near-duplicate document detection.
a.simon-cipher.summary: A family of lightweight block ciphers optimized for hardware, published together with Speck. It is a Feistel structure using only bitwise AND, rotation and XOR.
a.simple-8b.summary: A word-aligned integer compression scheme that widens the Simple-9 word to 64 bits, packing several integers into a 60-bit payload under a 4-bit selector. Time series databases such as InfluxDB use it to compress integers.
a.simple-9.summary: A word-aligned integer compression scheme that splits each 32-bit word into a 4-bit selector and a 28-bit payload, packing small integers in one of nine layouts that divide the payload into 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 14 or 28 equal-width fields. It is used to compress document-gap lists in inverted indexes.
a.simplex-noise.summary: A gradient noise that uses a simplex lattice instead of a cubic lattice to reduce computation in higher dimensions.
a.simplex.o0.venue: In Activity Analysis of Production and Allocation (1951)
a.simplex.summary: A linear programming method that moves along the vertices of the feasible-region polytope in directions that improve the objective function.
a.simrank.summary: A method that computes the structural similarity of pairs of graph vertices from the recursive definition that two objects are similar if they are referenced by similar objects.
a.simulated-annealing.summary: A global optimization method that explores solutions under the Metropolis acceptance rule while gradually lowering the temperature, allowing it to escape local optima.
a.siphash.summary: An ARX-based keyed pseudorandom function designed to be fast on short inputs. It is used as the hash function in Python, Rust, the Linux kernel and elsewhere to defend hash tables against hash-flooding denial-of-service attacks.
a.siv.summary: A deterministic authenticated-encryption scheme that uses a PRF of the header and plaintext as a synthetic IV for counter-mode encryption. Even when a nonce repeats, nothing leaks beyond whether two messages are equal.
a.skew-heap.summary: A self-adjusting heap that stores no balance information and unconditionally swaps the children of every node on the merge path. Merge, insert and delete-min take O(log n) amortized time.
a.skip-list.summary: A data structure that probabilistically promotes elements through multiple levels of linked lists, achieving expected O(log n) search.
a.slab-allocation.summary: A memory allocation technique that keeps per-type caches of objects in their initialized state, backed by page-sized slabs, to reduce the cost of allocating, freeing and initializing kernel objects.
a.slab-method.summary: A method that treats a bounding volume as the intersection of slabs, the regions between pairs of parallel planes, and decides ray–box intersection by intersecting the ray's entry and exit parameter intervals for each slab. As the ray test for axis-aligned bounding boxes, it is widely used in BVH traversal.
a.slerp.summary: A method that interpolates between two unit quaternions along the great-circle arc of the 4D unit sphere at constant angular velocity. In rotation keyframe interpolation it avoids the gimbal problems and nonuniform speed of interpolating Euler angles.
a.slic.summary: Generates compact superpixels by placing seeds on a regular grid and running k-means restricted to local windows with a distance that combines CIELAB color and position. It runs in time linear in the number of pixels.
a.slice-sampling.summary: An MCMC method that draws a height uniformly under the density at the current point and then draws the next point uniformly from the region where the density exceeds that height, the slice. Stepping-out and shrinkage procedures locate the slice, so little step-size tuning is needed.
a.slink.summary: An algorithm that computes single-linkage hierarchical clustering in O(n²) time and O(n) memory. It adds points one at a time and updates the dendrogram in a pointer representation.
a.slotted-aloha.summary: A variant of ALOHA that divides time into packet-length slots and lets stations transmit only at slot boundaries, halving the vulnerable period. Its maximum throughput is about 1/e, twice that of pure ALOHA.
a.slr-parsing.summary: A simplified form of LR parsing that builds the LR(0) item-set automaton and decides reductions using the FOLLOW sets of nonterminals. Its tables are much smaller than those of canonical LR.
a.smaa.summary: A post-process anti-aliasing method that refines MLAA's shape-based edge blending for GPUs, improving edge detection with local contrast adaptation and diagonal pattern handling, and that can be combined with multisampling and temporal reprojection.
a.smith-waterman.summary: A dynamic programming method that finds the most similar subsegments of two sequences (local alignment) by never letting scores fall below 0.
a.smo.summary: An optimization algorithm that breaks the SVM dual quadratic program into the smallest possible subproblems, analytically updating just two Lagrange multipliers at a time. It trains SVMs without large matrix computations.
a.smoothsort.summary: An in-place variant of heapsort that keeps a sequence of heaps whose sizes are Leonardo numbers. It runs in O(n log n) in the worst case and close to O(n) on already sorted input.
a.snappy.summary: An LZ77-family compression format and implementation made only of byte-aligned literal and copy tags, with no entropy coding. It is designed to favor speed over compression ratio and is supported by systems such as Hadoop and Parquet.
a.snapshot-isolation.summary: An isolation level in which each transaction reads a consistent snapshot as of its start, and among concurrent transactions writing the same data only the first to commit succeeds. It is widely used in multiversion databases but permits the write-skew anomaly.
a.sobol-sequence.summary: A low-discrepancy quasi-random sequence built by combining, with binary XOR, direction numbers derived from a primitive polynomial for each dimension. It is widely used in quasi-Monte Carlo integration and design of experiments.
a.soft-heap.summary: An approximate priority queue that, for a chosen error rate ε, deliberately raises (corrupts) the keys of some elements to make operations cheaper. Insert takes O(log 1/ε) and the other operations constant amortized time, and it was used in a minimum spanning tree algorithm.
a.soft-margin-svm.summary: An extension that applies SVMs to data that is not linearly separable by allowing some misclassifications through slack variables.
a.software-transactional-memory.summary: A concurrency-control technique that groups shared-memory accesses into transactions in software, committing them atomically or aborting and retrying on conflict. It provides transactional memory without special hardware.
a.solovay-strassen.summary: A probabilistic primality test that checks whether the Jacobi symbol agrees with a^((n−1)/2) mod n for random bases a. A composite number is exposed by at least half of the bases in each trial.
a.sor.summary: An iterative method for linear systems that accelerates Gauss–Seidel iteration by scaling each update with a relaxation factor. Its theory of the optimal relaxation factor was developed alongside solvers for elliptic PDEs.
a.soundex.summary: A phonetic indexing scheme that encodes names by numbers assigned to groups of similar-sounding letters instead of by spelling. It groups surnames that sound alike under the same index; the widely used American form is a code of the first letter followed by three digits.
a.space-saving.o0.note: Published in the ICDT 2005 proceedings, which Crossref registers as issued in 2004.
a.space-saving.summary: A frequent-items and top-k algorithm that keeps a fixed number of counters; when an unmonitored item arrives, it takes over the smallest counter and increments it.
a.spake2.summary: A simple password-authenticated key exchange that masks each Diffie–Hellman value by multiplying it with a fixed element raised to the password. It completes in two messages and is implemented in BoringSSL and Magic Wormhole, among others.
a.spanning-tree-protocol.summary: A protocol in which bridges exchange configuration messages, elect a root bridge and block ports not on least-cost paths to the root, computing a loop-free spanning tree of an extended LAN in a distributed way.
a.sparse-transformer.summary: A Transformer that factorizes the attention matrix into fixed sparse (strided and fixed) patterns, reducing cost to O(n√n). It was applied to generating long sequences of images, audio and text.
a.sparsely-gated-moe.summary: A mixture-of-experts layer in which a gating network selects only the top-k experts for each input. It increases model capacity without a proportional increase in computation.
a.special-number-field-sieve.summary: A factorization algorithm for integers of special form such as r^e±s that sieves for elements smooth on both an algebraic number-field side and a rational side to build a congruence of squares. For such numbers it is asymptotically faster than the quadratic sieve.
a.speck-cipher.summary: A family of block ciphers designed by NSA researchers as lightweight ciphers for software. Its rounds use only addition, rotation and XOR (ARX), and several block and key sizes are offered.
a.speculative-decoding.o1.note: Independently proposed the same method at about the same time under the name speculative sampling.
a.speculative-decoding.summary: A method that speeds up autoregressive generation by letting a small draft model propose several tokens that the large model verifies in parallel, with an accept–reject scheme that preserves the large model's output distribution.
a.spfa.summary: A queue-based improvement of Bellman–Ford that enqueues and relaxes only vertices whose distances have changed.
a.sph.summary: A meshless Lagrangian simulation method that represents a fluid by particles carrying mass and approximates quantities such as density and pressure, and their gradients, by weighted sums of a smoothing kernel over neighboring particles to solve the equations of motion. Proposed in astrophysics, it is widely used for fluid simulation in graphics.
a.sphere-tracing.summary: A ray tracing method for implicit surfaces that repeatedly advances a ray by the value of a function bounding the distance to the surface (such as a signed distance function), finding the intersection without overshooting the surface. It is widely used to render scenes defined by distance functions in shaders.
a.sphincs.summary: A practical stateless hash-based signature. It uses a hypertree of stacked Merkle trees and the few-time signature HORST to sign many messages without managing signing-key state.
a.spiht.summary: An embedded image coding algorithm that codes wavelet coefficients in bit-plane order while partitioning spatial orientation trees into sets according to significance tests. It extends the zerotree concept of EZW to set partitioning in hierarchical trees.
a.splay-tree.summary: A self-adjusting binary search tree that rotates each accessed node up to the root, achieving amortized O(log n) time.
a.spline-interpolation.summary: A method that interpolates or approximates data with piecewise polynomials joined smoothly up to a given derivative order at the knots. Schoenberg introduced the name and concept of spline functions; cubic splines are widely used.
a.split-radix-fft.summary: An FFT variant that recursively splits the even-indexed terms with radix 2 and the odd-indexed terms with radix 4. For power-of-two lengths it uses fewer arithmetic operations than radix-2 or radix-4 schemes.
a.splitmix.summary: A splittable pseudorandom generator that outputs a Weyl sequence, formed by repeatedly adding a fixed odd gamma to a 64-bit state, passed through a bit-mixing function, and that can split off independent generators with new gammas. It is used in Java's SplittableRandom.
a.sponge-construction.summary: A hash construction that handles arbitrary-length input and output by iterating a fixed permutation in two phases, absorbing and squeezing.
a.spreadsort.summary: A hybrid sort that splits elements into many bins by key range, handles small bins with a comparison sort and recursively re-splits large bins. It is implemented in the Boost.Sort library.
a.square-cipher.summary: An SPN block cipher whose diffusion is designed around byte-wise substitution and column mixing. It is the direct predecessor of Rijndael.
a.srp.summary: A password-authenticated key-exchange protocol in which the server stores only a verifier rather than the password itself, and the parties establish mutual authentication and a session key in a way that resists dictionary attacks. It was standardized for TLS as TLS-SRP (RFC 5054), among others.
a.ssa-form.summary: An intermediate representation in which variables are renamed so that each is assigned exactly once in the program text, with φ-functions placed where control flow merges. It makes many optimizations sparse and simple.
a.ssao.summary: A real-time technique that approximates ambient occlusion by testing, using only the depth buffer, whether sample points around each pixel are occluded by scene geometry and taking the occluded fraction. Its cost scales with screen resolution independently of scene complexity.
a.stable-fluids.summary: A grid-based fluid simulation method that splits the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations into external forces, semi-Lagrangian advection, implicit diffusion and pressure projection, so that the solver does not blow up even with large time steps. It is designed for interactive graphics, favoring stability over accuracy.
a.stable-roommates.summary: An algorithm for the stable roommates problem, in which participants of a single set are paired, that either finds a stable matching or reports that none exists in O(n²) time, using a proposal phase that reduces preference lists followed by a phase that finds and eliminates rotations.
a.stacking.summary: An ensemble method that trains a higher-level learner (meta-model) to make the final prediction from the cross-validated predictions of several base learners.
a.station-to-station.summary: An authenticated key-exchange protocol in which each party signs the Diffie–Hellman exchange values and sends the signature encrypted under the new session key, achieving mutual authentication and key confirmation together.
a.steensgaard-analysis.summary: A unification-based, flow- and context-insensitive points-to analysis that merges the targets of both sides of an assignment into a single equivalence class. Using union–find, it runs in almost linear time.
a.steering-behaviors.summary: Defines simple steering forces such as seek, flee, arrival, wander, path following, and obstacle avoidance, and combines them to produce the motion of autonomous characters. It serves as basic movement logic in games and crowd simulation.
a.steffensen-method.summary: A root-finding and fixed-point acceleration method that replaces the derivative with a difference quotient of function values while retaining Newton-like quadratic convergence. It is closely related to Aitken's delta-squared process.
a.stochastic-fair-queuing.summary: An approximation of fair queuing that hashes flow identifiers into a fixed number of queues served round robin, periodically changing the hash function to limit the effect of collisions.
a.stoer-wagner.summary: An algorithm that finds a global minimum cut of an undirected graph with non-negative weights without max-flow computations: each phase adds vertices in maximum-adjacency order, records the cut separating the last two vertices, and then merges those two vertices.
a.straight-skeleton.summary: Skeleton formed by the traces of the vertices when all edges of a polygon move inward in parallel at the same speed (shrinking). It consists only of straight segments and is used for roof modelling and polygon offsetting, among other things.
a.strassen-mm.summary: An algorithm that computes a 2×2 block product with seven multiplications, reducing matrix multiplication to O(n^2.807).
a.stream-vbyte.summary: A byte-oriented integer compression scheme that collects the 2-bit control values giving each integer's byte length (1 to 4) in a stream separate from the data bytes, so that several integers can be decoded at once with SIMD shuffle instructions.
a.strict-fibonacci-heap.summary: A heap that achieves the time bounds of Fibonacci heaps in the worst case on the pointer machine model. Insert, meld, find-min and decrease-key take O(1) worst-case time and delete-min takes O(log n) worst-case time.
a.striped-smith-waterman.summary: A method that computes Smith–Waterman local alignment with vector instructions by laying out the query in a striped pattern matched to the SIMD register width. Vertical gap dependencies are handled by a lazy correction loop.
a.subset-construction.summary: A transformation that builds a deterministic finite automaton recognizing the same language as an NFA by taking each set of NFA states as a DFA state. In the worst case the number of states grows exponentially.
a.subtract-with-borrow.summary: A family of pseudorandom generators that adds a borrow (or carry) bit to a lagged Fibonacci recurrence, as in x_n = x_{n−s} − x_{n−r} − c_{n−1} (mod b), to obtain very long periods. The C++ standard's subtract_with_carry_engine implements it.
a.suffix-array.summary: An array of the starting positions of all suffixes of a string, sorted in lexicographic order. It uses less memory than a suffix tree.
a.suffix-automaton.summary: The minimal deterministic automaton that recognizes all substrings of a string. It has linear size and is built online.
a.suffix-tree.summary: A data structure that stores all suffixes of a string in a compressed trie, answering substring queries in time proportional to the pattern length.
a.super-scalar-samplesort.summary: A single-processor samplesort that lays the splitters out as an implicit search tree and computes each element's bucket with branch-free comparisons, reducing branch mispredictions.
a.surf.summary: A local feature that detects interest points with a box-filter approximation of the Hessian determinant computed on integral images and builds descriptors from Haar wavelet responses. It was designed to be faster to compute than SIFT.
a.surface-area-heuristic.o0.note: Used a surface-area-based cost estimate for the automatic construction of bounding volume hierarchies.
a.surface-area-heuristic.o1.note: Formalized the surface area heuristic as a construction criterion for space subdivision trees.
a.surface-area-heuristic.summary: A construction criterion for acceleration structures that estimates the expected intersection cost of candidate splits, assuming that the probability of a ray hitting a convex volume is proportional to its surface area, and picks the cheapest split. It is standard in building BVHs and kd-trees.
a.sutherland-hodgman.summary: Reentrant polygon clipping algorithm that filters the polygon's vertex list against each boundary (plane) of a convex clip region in turn, keeping only the inside part. The per-boundary stages can be chained as a pipeline for 2D polygon clipping and 3D view-volume clipping.
a.suurballe.summary: An algorithm that finds a pair of disjoint paths of minimum total length by computing a shortest path, reversing its edges and reweighting with reduced costs, computing a second shortest path in the modified graph, and cancelling the edges that the two paths share in opposite directions. Repeating the process extends it to k disjoint paths.
a.suzuki-abe-border-following.summary: A border-following algorithm that raster-scans a binary image, traces outer borders and hole borders, and also derives the nesting hierarchy among them. OpenCV's contour detection follows this method.
a.svd-plus-plus.summary: A collaborative-filtering model that augments latent-factor matrix factorization with an implicit-feedback term built from the set of items each user has rated.
a.svm.summary: A classifier that finds the hyperplane maximizing the margin between two classes and extends to nonlinear boundaries through kernels.
a.sweep-line-cdt.summary: Constrained Delaunay triangulation algorithm that sweeps the points in one direction, attaching triangles to an advancing front and restoring the Delaunay condition with edge flips, while inserting constraint edges during the sweep.
a.swendsen-wang.summary: A cluster Monte Carlo method for the Ising model that bonds aligned neighboring spins with probability 1−e^(−2βJ) to form clusters and flips every cluster independently at random. It greatly reduces critical slowing down near the critical point.
a.swiglu.summary: A GLU variant that replaces the sigmoid gate with the Swish function, used in Transformer feed-forward layers. It has been adopted by large language models such as LLaMA and PaLM.
a.swim.summary: A group membership and failure detection protocol in which each node periodically pings a random member, verifies non-responders through indirect pings via other members, and disseminates membership changes in an infection-style (gossip) manner.
a.swiss-table.o0.note: The same developers first presented it in a CppCon 2017 talk; this post announced its open-source release in Abseil in 2018.
a.swiss-table.summary: An open-addressing hash table that keeps a one-byte control byte holding part of the hash for each slot and compares 16 slots at once with SIMD. It probes group by group with quadratic probing and is implemented as Abseil's flat_hash_map and related containers.
a.switch-transformer.summary: A Transformer that simplifies mixture-of-experts routing to top-1, sending each token to a single expert. It was scaled to models with over a trillion parameters.
a.symmerge.summary: A stable merging algorithm that finds a split point in two sorted ranges by symmetric comparisons, rearranges them with a rotation and merges the parts recursively. It needs no extra buffer and is used by Go's sort.Stable.
a.t-digest.summary: A sketch that summarizes data as clusters (centroids) whose sizes are limited according to quantile position, estimating quantiles near the tails of a distribution especially accurately. Separately built summaries can be merged without loss of accuracy.
a.t-sne.summary: A dimensionality-reduction technique for visualization that defines pairwise similarities with Gaussian conditional probabilities in the high-dimensional space and a Student-t distribution in the embedding, then optimizes the embedding to minimize the KL divergence between them.
a.t5.summary: An encoder–decoder Transformer that casts every language task, such as translation, summarization and classification, as text-to-text. It is pretrained with a span-corruption objective on the large C4 corpus.
a.table-driven-crc.summary: A software method that precomputes a table of CRC updates for each byte (or group of bits) and computes the CRC with table lookups, shifts and XORs instead of bit-by-bit division.
a.taha-hanbury-hausdorff.summary: Algorithm for the exact Hausdorff distance between two point sets that stops the inner loop as soon as it finds a distance smaller than the current maximum for the outer point (early break) and uses random ordering, reducing the average amount of computation.
a.tango-tree.o0.note: A conference version with the same title appeared earlier at FOCS 2004.
a.tango-tree.summary: A binary search tree that stores the preferred paths of a reference tree in auxiliary red–black trees. It was the first structure shown to be within an O(log log n) factor of the optimal offline binary search tree on every access sequence.
a.tanh-sinh.summary: A numerical integration method that applies the trapezoidal rule after the change of variables x = tanh((π/2)·sinh t), which makes the integrand decay double-exponentially at both ends. It is used for integrals with endpoint singularities and for high-precision computation.
a.tarjan-bridges.summary: A linear-time algorithm that finds the bridges (cut edges) of an undirected graph by computing preorder numbers in a spanning forest and the range of numbers reachable from each subtree.
a.tarjan-offline-lca.summary: An offline algorithm that answers a batch of lowest-common-ancestor queries given in advance using a single depth-first traversal and a union–find structure. For n nodes and m queries it runs in nearly linear O((n + m) α(n)) time.
a.tarjan-scc.summary: An algorithm that finds the strongly connected components of a directed graph in linear time using a single DFS and low-link values.
a.taubin-smoothing.summary: A method that alternates a Laplacian smoothing step with a positive factor λ and one with a negative factor μ, so that it acts on the mesh like a low-pass filter. It greatly reduces the shrinkage caused by plain Laplacian smoothing.
a.tcp-newreno.o0.note: RFC 2582 states that the partial-ACK response was first proposed in this thesis, and standardized it under the name NewReno.
a.tcp-newreno.o1.note: The same author's conference publication of the thesis work.
a.tcp-newreno.summary: A modification of TCP fast recovery that, on a partial ACK, retransmits the next lost segment immediately instead of leaving recovery. It reduces timeouts when several packets are lost from one window.
a.tcp-slow-start.summary: TCP congestion control in which the sender grows its congestion window on each ACK, exponentially at first (slow start) and linearly past a threshold (congestion avoidance), and cuts it when loss is detected. Implemented in 4.3BSD-Tahoe, it became the basic framework of TCP congestion control.
a.tcp-vegas.summary: A delay-based TCP congestion control that estimates the queue built up along the path from the gap between expected and actual throughput and adjusts the congestion window before loss occurs.
a.td-lambda.summary: A learning method that updates value predictions from the difference between successive predictions (the temporal-difference error), using eligibility traces to share credit among past states in proportion to powers of λ.
a.td3.summary: An algorithm that reduces DDPG's overestimation by using the smaller of two critics' Q values as the target (clipped double Q), updating the policy and target networks less often, and adding noise to target actions.
a.tea.summary: A 64-bit block cipher designed to be implementable in a few lines of code. It uses a 128-bit key and iterates a Feistel structure of addition, shifts and XOR for 64 rounds (32 cycles).
a.telea-inpainting.summary: Inpainting that advances from the boundary of the damaged region inward with the fast marching method, filling each pixel from a weighted first-order approximation of its known neighbors. It quickly repairs small defects and scratches.
a.tfhe.summary: A fully homomorphic encryption scheme that uses LWE ciphertexts over the torus and gate-by-gate bootstrapping to refresh noise each time a Boolean gate is evaluated. It cut bootstrapping time below 0.1 seconds and was later extended with programmable bootstrapping.
a.theta-sketch.summary: A sketch framework that estimates the number of distinct elements by keeping only items whose hash values are below a threshold θ, and that also estimates the cardinalities of set expressions such as unions, intersections and differences.
a.theta-star.summary: A variant of A* for grids that, when expanding a node, sets a neighbor's parent to the current node's parent instead of the current node whenever there is line of sight, thereby finding any-angle paths not constrained to grid edge directions.
a.thompson-construction.summary: A construction that builds an NFA proportional in size to a regular expression by combining small NFA fragments with ε-transitions for concatenation, alternation and repetition. The original paper generated search code that tracks the set of states of this NFA simultaneously.
a.thorup-sssp.o0.note: A preliminary version appeared at FOCS 1997.
a.thorup-sssp.summary: An algorithm that solves single-source shortest paths in undirected graphs with positive integer weights in linear time on the word RAM by visiting vertices in buckets along a component hierarchy derived from a minimum spanning tree, instead of in Dijkstra's distance order.
a.three-phase-commit.summary: An atomic commit protocol that inserts a pre-commit phase between the voting and commit phases of two-phase commit, so that the remaining participants can decide the outcome without blocking when the coordinator fails.
a.threefry.summary: A counter-based pseudorandom number generator that mixes a counter and a key with a reduced number of the add–rotate–XOR rounds of the Threefish block cipher. It is used to create splittable random streams in parallel settings.
a.tiernan-cycles.summary: A search algorithm that finds all elementary circuits of a directed graph by extending paths depth-first and recording each path that closes back at its start vertex as a circuit.
a.tiger-hash.summary: A 192-bit hash function designed to be fast on 64-bit processors. It uses large S-box lookups and 64-bit arithmetic, and was used in the Tiger tree hash of file-sharing software.
a.timing-wheel.summary: A structure that places each timer in the slot of a circular array corresponding to its expiry time and advances through the slots like a clock hand to process expirations. The work presents hashed and multi-level hierarchical variants; the hashed variant starts and stops timers in O(1) time.
a.timsort.o0.title: listsort.txt — CPython list.sort implementation
a.timsort.summary: An adaptive stable sort that finds already sorted segments (runs) in the input, extends them with binary insertion sort, and combines them with galloping merges.
a.tinylfu.summary: A cache admission policy that estimates recent access frequency compactly with an approximate counting structure and admits a new item only if its frequency exceeds that of the eviction candidate. Counters are periodically halved so that old frequencies age out.
a.tls-1-3-handshake.summary: The TLS 1.3 handshake protocol, which sets up an encrypted session within one round trip using (EC)DHE key exchange, signature-based server authentication and an HKDF-based key schedule. Dropping static RSA key exchange makes forward secrecy the default, and pre-shared keys enable 0-RTT resumption.
a.tlsf.summary: A dynamic memory allocator for real-time systems that manages free blocks with two-level segregated lists by size class and bitmaps, performing allocation and deallocation in constant time.
a.tomita-pivot.summary: A Bron–Kerbosch-style maximal-clique enumeration algorithm that reduces branching by choosing a pivot whose neighbourhood covers the most candidates. Its worst-case time O(3^(n/3)) matches the maximum possible number of maximal cliques.
a.toms-748.summary: A bracketing root-finding algorithm that shrinks the enclosing interval by combining inverse cubic and quadratic interpolation steps. It has high asymptotic efficiency per function evaluation and is implemented in SciPy and Boost.
a.tonelli-shanks.summary: An algorithm that solves x² ≡ n (mod p) by writing p−1 = 2^s·q and using a quadratic non-residue to eliminate the error in the 2-power part step by step. It is widely used to compute square roots modulo a prime.
a.toom-cook.summary: A generalization of Karatsuba that multiplies numbers by treating them as polynomials in k pieces, evaluating at several points, and interpolating.
a.top-tree.o0.note: The general framework was later set out by the same authors in 'Maintaining information in fully dynamic trees with top trees', ACM Transactions on Algorithms 1(2), 2005.
a.top-tree.summary: A dynamic-tree data structure that hierarchically groups a tree into clusters and updates information by merging and splitting clusters when edges are linked or cut. User-defined cluster information lets it answer non-local queries such as paths, diameters and centers in O(log n) time.
a.topic-sensitive-pagerank.summary: A ranking method that precomputes several PageRank vectors, each with a teleportation distribution biased toward one topic, and combines them with weights that depend on the query context.
a.topological-sort.summary: An algorithm that finds a topological order of a directed acyclic graph by repeatedly removing vertices with in-degree 0.
a.tornado-code.summary: An erasure code built from a cascade of sparse bipartite graphs that recovers lost symbols in linear time by a simple chain of XOR-based substitutions from the received symbols.
a.torrance-sparrow.summary: A reflection model that treats a rough surface as a collection of randomly oriented V-shaped microfacets and explains off-specular reflection through the microfacet distribution, masking and shadowing, and Fresnel reflection. It became the theoretical basis of microfacet BRDFs in computer graphics.
a.total-variation-denoising.summary: A variational method that removes noise by minimizing the total variation (integral of gradient magnitude) of the image together with its deviation from the observed image. It preserves edges but can produce staircasing in smooth regions.
a.totp.summary: An algorithm that generates one-time passwords using the current time divided into fixed steps, such as 30 seconds, in place of HOTP's counter. Most two-factor authentication apps, including Google Authenticator, use it.
a.transformer.summary: A sequence model without recurrence that stacks scaled dot-product multi-head self-attention and feed-forward layers with residual connections and normalization.
a.treap.summary: A probabilistically balanced tree that satisfies the binary search tree property on keys and the heap property on random priorities.
a.treiber-stack.summary: A lock-free stack that performs push and pop without locks by updating the top-of-stack pointer with compare-and-swap (CAS). It is widely used as the simplest example of a non-blocking data structure.
a.tri-color-marking.summary: A GC technique that partitions objects into white, gray, and black and maintains an invariant so that marking can proceed concurrently with the program.
a.trie.summary: A tree whose edges are the individual characters of strings. Sharing common prefixes makes prefix search fast.
a.trpo.summary: A policy-optimization algorithm that maximizes a surrogate objective within a trust region bounding the average KL divergence between the new and old policies, improving the policy step by step without large drops in performance.
a.turbo-code.summary: An error-correcting code that encodes with two recursive systematic convolutional codes joined by an interleaver and decodes iteratively as two decoders exchange extrinsic information. It was the first practical code to approach the Shannon limit and was used in 3G and 4G mobile systems.
a.two-choice-hashing.summary: Computes two hash locations for each key and inserts it into the less loaded one. The maximum load drops exponentially compared with using a single random location.
a.two-opt.summary: A local-search technique for the traveling salesman problem that repeatedly removes two edges from the tour and reconnects it by reversing the segment between them, as long as the tour length decreases.
a.two-phase-commit.summary: A protocol that guarantees atomicity of distributed transactions by having a coordinator collect prepare votes and then direct all participants to commit or abort together.
a.two-phase-locking.summary: A concurrency-control technique in which each transaction goes through a growing phase that only acquires locks followed by a shrinking phase that only releases them, guaranteeing that concurrent executions are equivalent to some serial execution (serializability).
a.two-queue-replacement.summary: A buffer replacement algorithm that places newly arrived pages in a FIFO queue (A1in), records evicted page IDs in a ghost queue (A1out), and promotes only pages re-referenced from there into the main LRU queue (Am). It achieves performance close to LRU-2 at constant-time cost.
a.two-way-string-matching.summary: A string search algorithm that splits the pattern at a critical factorization, comparing the right part from left to right and then the left part from right to left. It guarantees worst-case linear time with constant extra space and is used in implementations such as glibc's strstr.
a.twofish.summary: A 128-bit block cipher that was an AES finalist. It is a 16-round Feistel network built from key-dependent S-boxes, an MDS matrix and the pseudo-Hadamard transform.
a.u-net.summary: A U-shaped convolutional network whose contracting and expanding paths are symmetric and joined by skip connections between feature maps of equal resolution. Proposed for biomedical image segmentation, it is also widely used as the backbone of diffusion models.
a.uct.summary: A Monte Carlo planning algorithm that balances exploration and exploitation at each tree node using the UCB1 bandit formula.
a.ukkonen-algorithm.summary: An algorithm that builds a suffix tree online in linear time, reading characters one at a time from left to right.
a.ukkonen-cutoff.summary: A technique for dynamic programming approximate pattern search with at most k errors that computes each column only down to the last row whose value does not exceed k. On random text its expected time is known to be O(kn).
a.ullmann.summary: An algorithm that finds subgraph isomorphisms by backtracking while repeatedly refining a matrix of possible vertex correspondences with neighbourhood conditions.
a.umac.summary: A fast MAC that compresses the message with the universal hash NH and masks the result with a pseudorandom value. It is a Wegman–Carter-style MAC used in OpenSSH as umac-64 and umac-128.
a.umap.summary: A nonlinear dimensionality-reduction technique that builds a fuzzy topological representation of the data from a k-nearest-neighbor graph and optimizes a low-dimensional embedding to minimize the cross-entropy against it.
a.umeyama.summary: Least-squares method that recovers the similarity transformation (rotation, translation and uniform scale) between two point patterns from the singular value decomposition of their covariance matrix, with a sign correction that guarantees a proper rotation rather than a reflection.
a.unification.summary: An algorithm that repeatedly finds the first disagreement between two terms and substitutes a term for a variable, computing the most general unifier that makes the terms equal or reporting that none exists. An occurs check prevents cyclic substitutions.
a.union-find.summary: A data structure that represents elements as trees of disjoint sets, performing union and find-representative operations in nearly constant time.
a.universal-hashing.summary: Chooses a hash function at random from a family so that, for any input, two distinct keys collide with small probability. It makes the expected performance of hash tables independent of the input distribution.
a.unscented-kalman-filter.o0.note: The name 'unscented' became widely known through Julier and Uhlmann's 1997 SPIE paper 'New extension of the Kalman filter to nonlinear systems'.
a.unscented-kalman-filter.summary: A nonlinear state estimator that uses the unscented transform in the Kalman filter: sigma points representing the mean and covariance are propagated directly through the nonlinear functions, and weighted averages give the predicted mean and covariance. It requires no Jacobians.
a.vae.o1.note: Independently proposed the same approach at about the same time.
a.vae.summary: A generative model whose encoder parameterizes an approximate posterior over latent variables and whose decoder parameterizes the data distribution, trained by optimizing the evidence lower bound with the reparameterization trick.
a.van-emde-boas-tree.summary: A tree that stores keys from an integer universe of size u by recursively splitting it into clusters of size √u. It supports insert, delete, predecessor and successor in O(log log u) time.
a.variance-shadow-maps.summary: A method that stores depth and squared depth in the shadow map, filters them, and approximates the shadowed fraction with an upper bound from Chebyshev's inequality computed from the mean and variance. The depth map itself can be prefiltered with mipmapping or blurring.
a.vatti-clipping.summary: General polygon clipping algorithm that sweeps the edges of both polygons from bottom to top, processing bound pairs that start at local minima and their intersections one scanbeam at a time to build the result. It handles concave, self-intersecting and holed polygons and is also used for Boolean operations such as union and difference.
a.vector-clock.summary: A logical clock that uses a vector of per-process counters to determine causality and concurrency between events exactly.
a.vectorized-query-execution.summary: A query execution model in which operators process vectors of hundreds to thousands of values at a time instead of single tuples, reducing interpretation overhead and making good use of CPU pipelines and caches.
a.velocity-obstacle.summary: A motion-planning method that computes, as a cone in velocity space, the set of robot velocities that would lead to collision with a moving obstacle (the velocity obstacle) and avoids collisions by choosing velocities outside it.
a.velocity-verlet.summary: A form of Verlet integration that updates positions and velocities together at the same time points. It is a standard integrator in molecular dynamics programs.
a.verlet-integration.o0.note: The paper that introduced the scheme to molecular dynamics and made it widely known; the same difference formula had been used earlier, for example by Størmer.
a.verlet-integration.summary: A second-order time integration method that computes the next position from the current and previous positions and the acceleration. Being time-reversible and symplectic, it is used in molecular dynamics and physics simulation.
a.vf2.summary: A graph and subgraph isomorphism algorithm that extends partial-mapping states depth-first and prunes them with feasibility rules. It keeps the memory for search states linear in the number of vertices.
a.vgg.summary: A convolutional neural network built by deeply stacking only 3×3 convolutions, demonstrating the effect of depth on performance.
a.viewstamped-replication.summary: A fault-tolerant state machine replication scheme based on a primary replica and a view-change protocol.
a.vincenty-formulae.summary: Iterative method, written with nested equations, for the inverse geodesic problem (distance and azimuths between two points on an ellipsoid of revolution) and the direct problem (destination from a start point, azimuth and distance). It may fail to converge for nearly antipodal points.
a.viola-jones.summary: Real-time object detection that selects Haar-like features, computed quickly from an integral image, with AdaBoost and chains stage classifiers into a cascade that rejects background windows early. It was widely used for face detection.
a.visvalingam-whyatt.summary: Line simplification algorithm that repeatedly removes the point whose triangle with its two neighbours has the smallest area (its effective area).
a.vit.summary: An image classifier that splits an image into fixed-size patches, linearly embeds them as tokens and processes the sequence with a standard Transformer encoder. With large-scale pretraining it performs comparably to convolutional networks.
a.viterbi.summary: An algorithm that uses dynamic programming to find the hidden state sequence of a hidden Markov model that best explains an observation sequence.
a.vitter-algorithm.summary: An update algorithm for dynamic Huffman coding that maintains the invariant that, among nodes of equal weight, leaves precede internal nodes. Its worst-case bound on the number of transmitted bits is smaller than that of the FGK algorithm.
a.volcano-iterator-model.o0.note: A comprehensive description of the Volcano system appeared in IEEE TKDE 6(1), 1994 (doi:10.1109/69.273032).
a.volcano-iterator-model.summary: A query execution model that implements each plan operator as an iterator with open, next and close methods, pulling one tuple at a time on demand from its parent, and encapsulates parallelism in an exchange operator.
a.volume-ray-casting.summary: A direct volume rendering method that casts a ray into the volume data for each pixel, samples it at regular intervals, and composites the colors and opacities assigned by a transfer function front to back (or back to front) to form the image. It is used to visualize scalar fields such as medical images.
a.vose-alias.summary: A variant of the alias method that builds the alias table in O(n) time by splitting cells into lists of below-average and above-average probabilities and pairing them off.
a.vp-tree.o0.note: Uhlmann called the structure a metric tree.
a.vp-tree.o1.note: Independently presented the same structure and named it the vp-tree.
a.vp-tree.summary: A tree for metric spaces that picks a vantage point and recursively splits the remaining points into inner and outer sets at the median distance from it. Nearest-neighbor search prunes branches using the triangle inequality.
a.wagner-fischer.summary: An algorithm that computes a generalized edit distance in O(nm) using a dynamic programming table over pairs of prefixes of the two strings.
a.wait-die.summary: A non-preemptive deadlock-prevention scheme that gives transactions start timestamps; on a lock conflict an older transaction waits while a younger one aborts (dies) and restarts with the same timestamp.
a.walktrap.summary: An agglomerative community-detection method that defines distances between vertices and communities from the probability distributions of short random walks and merges communities hierarchically on that basis.
a.wang-landau.summary: A Monte Carlo method that estimates the density of states directly by performing a random walk in energy space, multiplying the estimate g(E) at each visited energy by a modification factor until the histogram is flat, and gradually reducing the factor toward 1.
a.ward-method.summary: An agglomerative hierarchical clustering that successively merges the pair of clusters whose union gives the smallest increase in the total within-cluster sum of squares.
a.watershed.summary: Segmentation that treats a gradient-magnitude image as a topographic surface, floods it from its minima, and marks where different basins meet as boundaries. Vincent and Soille gave an efficient algorithm that sorts pixels by height and simulates immersion with FIFO queues.
