e.huffman>adaptive-huffman: As the title of Gallager's paper 'Variations on a theme by Huffman' indicates, it is a variant that makes Huffman coding adaptive in a single pass
e.huffman>brotli: RFC 7932 defines it as a combination of LZ77, Huffman coding, and second-order context modeling
e.huffman>bzip2: Uses Huffman coding as the final entropy stage
e.huffman>canonical-huffman: Presents a way to reassign the codewords of a prefix code such as a Huffman code in canonical order while keeping its code lengths
e.huffman>deflate: RFC 1951 defines Deflate as a combination of LZ77 and Huffman coding
e.huffman>hu-tucker: It adds an order-preservation constraint to the weighted path length minimization problem solved by Huffman coding
e.huffman>jpeg: JPEG baseline entropy-codes the quantized DCT coefficients with Huffman codes
e.huffman>package-merge: As its title states, it is an algorithm for optimal Huffman codes with an upper limit on code length
e.huffman>zstd: RFC 8878 compresses literals with Huffman coding
e.hungarian>auction-algorithm: A different approach to the same assignment problem based on price bidding.
e.hungarian>jonker-volgenant: It refines the Hungarian-type approach of solving the assignment problem with dual variables and shortest augmenting paths, adding initialization heuristics.
e.hunt-szymanski>heckel-diff: Addresses the same file-difference problem but uses unique lines as anchors instead of a longest common subsequence.
e.hunt-szymanski>myers-diff: A different approach to the same LCS/diff problem
e.hyperloglog>hyperloglog-pp: Presented as a practical improvement of HyperLogLog
e.hyperloglog>theta-sketch: Addresses the same distinct-count estimation problem; the theta sketch additionally supports estimates for set operations.
e.icp>coherent-point-drift: CPD addresses the same point set registration problem as ICP, using probabilistic correspondences from a Gaussian mixture model instead of closest-point matches.
e.icp>gicp: The paper states that it combines ICP and point-to-plane ICP into a single probabilistic framework.
e.icp>ndt: NDT addresses the same scan registration problem as ICP but registers against per-cell normal distributions instead of point correspondences.
e.id3>c4-5: Published by Quinlan as the successor to ID3
e.importance-sampling>particle-filter: The bootstrap particle filter is described as sequential importance sampling with an added resampling step
e.insertion-sort>binary-insertion-sort: Replaces only the insertion-point search with binary search; described in Knuth TAOCP Vol.3 §5.2.1
e.insertion-sort>library-sort: The paper shows that insertion sort with gaps left in the array (gapped insertion sort) runs in O(n log n) with high probability.
e.insertion-sort>shellsort: Shell presented it as a diminishing-increment method that performs insertion sort for each gap
e.instance-norm>group-norm: The paper describes instance normalization as the special case of group normalization with one channel per group
e.introsort>pdqsort: The paper introduces pdqsort as an extension of introsort
e.jacobi-eigenvalue>givens-rotation: Givens rotations use the same plane rotations as the Jacobi eigenvalue method as a tool for zeroing entries.
e.jacobi-method>gauss-seidel: The Gauss–Seidel method is described as a variant of Jacobi iteration that uses updated values immediately.
e.jaro-similarity>jaro-winkler: Winkler's paper presents a modification of Jaro's string comparator that adjusts it according to agreement on the leading characters.
e.jarvis-march>chan-hull: Combines per-group Graham scans with a Jarvis march
e.k-means>elkan-k-means: The paper presents an accelerated k-means that uses the triangle inequality to skip needless distance computations while giving the same result.
e.k-means>em: k-means can be interpreted as the hard-assignment limit of EM, but was historically devised first
e.k-means>k-means-pp: Presented as a method that changes only how k-means chooses its initial centers
e.k-means>lbg: The LBG algorithm is known as a generalization of Lloyd's quantizer design method to vector quantization
e.k-means>mini-batch-k-means: The paper scales k-means to large data by updating centers with small random batches.
e.k-means>njw-spectral-clustering: The NJW algorithm obtains clusters by running k-means on the normalized eigenvector embedding.
e.k-means>product-quantization: Product quantization quantizes vectors with a codebook learned by k-means in each subspace.
e.k-means>self-organizing-map: The self-organizing map tackles the same vector quantization problem as k-means, with prototype updates constrained by a neighborhood
e.k-means>slic: The SLIC paper states that it adapts k-means clustering in a combined color and position space with a locally restricted search
e.k-nearest-neighbors>local-outlier-fact: LOF estimates local density from each point's k-nearest-neighbor distances.
e.kabsch>horn-quaternion: Both solve the same problem of the optimal rotation between corresponding point sets in closed form; Horn uses unit quaternions instead of a rotation matrix.
e.kabsch>umeyama: Umeyama's method generalizes the optimal-rotation problem between corresponding point sets to a similarity transformation including scale and translation, and corrects the reflection issue.
e.kahan-summation>neumaier-summation: Neumaier analyzed Kahan(–Babuška) compensated summation and improved it to also compensate when a term is larger than the running sum
e.kalman-filter>ensemble-kalman-filter: Evensen presents a method that approximates the error-covariance forecast of the Kalman filter with a Monte Carlo ensemble
e.kalman-filter>extended-kalman-filter: The extended Kalman filter is described as a generalization that applies the Kalman filter after linearizing nonlinear models around the current estimate
e.kalman-filter>kalman-bucy-filter: Kalman and Bucy present the filter that carries the discrete-time Kalman filter results over to continuous-time systems
e.kalman-filter>rts-smoother: The RTS smoother adds a backward recursion to the forward estimates of the Kalman filter to obtain fixed-interval smoothed estimates
e.kalman-filter>unscented-kalman-filter: Julier and Uhlmann present the unscented-transform-based filter as a new extension of the Kalman filter to nonlinear systems
e.karatsuba>toom-cook: Karatsuba is the special case of Toom–Cook with two pieces (Knuth TAOCP Vol.2 §4.3.3)
e.karger-stein>stoer-wagner: It solves the same global minimum cut problem deterministically instead of by random contraction.
e.karmarkar>mehrotra-predictor-corrector: Mehrotra's method is an implementation technique for primal–dual interior-point methods that developed after Karmarkar's work.
e.karn-algorithm>jacobson-rtt-estimator: RFC 6298 specifies Jacobson's RTO computation together with Karn's algorithm.
e.katz-centrality>pagerank: Both indices rank vertices by an attenuated combination of walks over the adjacency matrix.
e.kd-tree>grid-file: The grid file addresses the same multidimensional key search problem as the k-d tree, without evidence of direct derivation.
e.kd-tree>kdb-tree: Robinson built the K-D-B-tree by combining k-d tree partitioning with the balanced structure of B-trees.
e.kd-tree>surface-area-heuristic: MacDonald and Booth applied a surface-area cost criterion to building axis-aligned space subdivision trees
e.kd-tree>vp-tree: The VP-tree extends k-d-tree-style partitioning to metric spaces by splitting on distance to a vantage point instead of a coordinate axis.
e.kdb-tree>bkd-tree: The Bkd-tree paper maintains, in a logarithmic scheme, static k-d trees laid out in blocks as in the K-D-B-tree.
e.kernel-density-estimation>mean-shift: The paper estimates the gradient of a kernel density estimate and moves points toward the modes of the density.
e.kernighan-lin>fiduccia-mattheyses: It replaces the pair-swapping passes of Kernighan–Lin with single-vertex moves and a bucket structure, making each pass linear-time.
e.kernighan-lin>metis: It uses Kernighan–Lin-type refinement to improve boundary vertices during uncoarsening.
e.kildall-dataflow>abstract-interpretati: Abstract interpretation semantically generalizes the dataflow-analysis framework of fixed-point computation on lattices.
e.kildall-dataflow>ifds: IFDS extends distributive dataflow problems interprocedurally and solves them precisely as graph reachability.
e.kildall-dataflow>partial-redundancy-el: Partial redundancy elimination decides insertion and deletion points by solving bit-vector dataflow equations.
e.kildall-dataflow>sccp: Wegman–Zadeck constant propagation improves Kildall-style iterative constant propagation with SSA and executable-edge tracking.
e.kirkpatrick-seidel>chan-hull: Both solve the same output-sensitive planar convex hull problem in O(n log h); Chan's algorithm reaches the same bound with a simpler method.
e.kmp>aho-corasick: Generalizes the KMP failure function to a trie of the pattern set (standard textbook account)
e.kmp>booth-rotation: Described as finding the least rotation by adapting the Knuth–Morris–Pratt failure-function preprocessing.
e.kmp>boyer-moore: Contemporary linear-time single-pattern search, but based on a different principle
e.kmp>two-way-string-matching: The authors describe the algorithm as intermediate between Knuth–Morris–Pratt and Boyer–Moore.
e.kruskal>felzenszwalb-segmentation: The paper notes that processing edges in weight order to merge regions is closely related to Kruskal's minimum spanning tree algorithm
e.kzg-commitment>plonk: The PLONK paper uses the KZG (Kate) scheme as its polynomial commitment
e.l-bfgs>l-bfgs-b: The L-BFGS-B paper extends the limited-memory BFGS matrix to bound-constrained problems.
e.lalr>slr-parsing: SLR and LALR were proposed by the same author as different ways of computing lookahead on the LR(0) automaton.
e.lamport-clock>chandy-lamport-snapshot: Snapshot consistency is defined on the happened-before relation between events introduced by Lamport
e.lamport-clock>hybrid-logical-clock: The HLC paper presents HLC as a clock combining Lamport's logical clock with physical clocks
e.lamport-clock>ricart-agrawala: Ricart and Agrawala reduced the message count of Lamport-timestamp-based distributed mutual exclusion to 2(N−1) per entry
e.lamport-clock>vector-clock: Generalizes Lamport's logical clock to per-process vectors
e.lamport-signature>merkle-signature: Generalizes one-time signatures by binding them in a tree so that one public key signs many times
e.lanczos-algorithm>arnoldi-iteration: Arnoldi's paper extends Lanczos's principle of minimized iterations to the nonsymmetric matrix eigenvalue problem.
e.lanczos-algorithm>conjugate-gradient: For symmetric positive-definite matrices, the conjugate gradient method shares the Krylov subspace structure of the Lanczos process.
e.lanczos-algorithm>minres: The Paige–Saunders paper derives MINRES and SYMMLQ from the tridiagonal matrix produced by the Lanczos process.
e.laplacian-eigenmaps>umap: UMAP initializes its low-dimensional embedding with a spectral embedding.
e.laplacian-pyramid>sift: SIFT's difference-of-Gaussians scale space, like the Laplacian pyramid, stacks differences of Gaussian-smoothed images across scales
e.lasso>elastic-net: The paper extends the lasso by adding an L2 penalty to its L1 penalty so that groups of correlated variables are selected together.
e.lasso>lars: The paper shows that a simple modification of LARS computes the entire lasso solution path efficiently.
e.latent-semantic-analysis>glove: The GloVe paper states that it combines the advantages of global matrix factorization methods such as LSA and local context-window methods.
e.latent-semantic-analysis>plsa: Hofmann presents pLSA as a probabilistic reformulation of LSA.
e.lawson-flip>s-hull: S-hull converts the triangulation produced by its radial sweep into a Delaunay triangulation with a final step of diagonal flips between adjacent triangle pairs.
e.lawson-flip>sweep-line-cdt: The sweep-line constrained Delaunay triangulation restores the Delaunay condition with edge flips each time new triangles are attached to the front.
e.layer-norm>group-norm: The paper describes layer normalization as the special case of group normalization with a single group
e.layer-norm>rmsnorm: RMSNorm removes mean-centering from layer normalization, keeping only rescaling to reduce computation
e.layer-norm>transformer: Applies layer normalization after the residual connection, citing Ba et al.
e.lcg>mrg32k3a: Multiple recursive generators generalize the first-order recurrence of linear congruential generators to higher order, and MRG32k3a combines two such generators
e.lcg>pcg: States that it combines LCG state transitions with a permutation output function
e.lcg>wichmann-hill: The Wichmann–Hill generator is defined as a combination that adds the outputs of three multiplicative congruential generators and takes the fractional part
e.ldpc>tornado-code: Like LDPC codes, Tornado codes are defined by sparse bipartite graphs, designed here for erasure channels.
e.leaky-bucket>weighted-fair-queuing: The GPS analysis derives delay bounds assuming flows constrained by leaky buckets.
e.leftist-heap>skew-heap: Sleator and Tarjan presented the skew heap as a self-adjusting form of the leftist heap.
e.lenet>alexnet: Cites LeCun's line of convolutional neural networks and scales up depth and size
e.lenet>googlenet: The GoogLeNet paper describes starting from the standard CNN structure established since LeNet-5
e.lengauer-tarjan>cytron-ssa: The SSA construction of Cytron et al. takes the dominator tree as input, computed with the Lengauer–Tarjan method.
e.levenshtein-distance>damerau-levenshte: Belongs to the same edit-distance family and is named for adding adjacent transpositions to the Levenshtein operations.
e.levenshtein-distance>levenshtein-autom: Presented as performing spelling correction with automata that recognize words within Levenshtein distance n.
e.levenshtein-distance>qgram-distance: The q-gram distance is used to derive a lower bound on edit distance for filtering approximate-matching candidates.
e.levenshtein-distance>wagner-fischer: Computes Levenshtein distance by dynamic programming and generalizes edit costs (the same DP was discovered independently by several researchers)
e.lex-bfs>maximum-cardinality-search: Tarjan and Yannakakis introduced maximum cardinality search as a new search that simplifies the chordality test of Rose, Tarjan and Lueker.
e.liang-barsky>nicholl-lee-nicholl: The Nicholl–Lee–Nicholl algorithm targets the same 2D line clipping problem and is compared with earlier methods on the number of operations.
e.lin-kernighan>lkh: As its title states, it is an effective implementation and refinement of the Lin–Kernighan heuristic.
e.linear-blend-skinning>dual-quaternion-: The paper addresses the volume-loss problem of linear blend skinning with dual quaternion blending
e.linear-counting>hyperloglog-pp: The HyperLogLog++ paper states that it uses the LinearCounting of Whang et al. for small cardinalities.
e.linear-probing>cuckoo-hashing: Within the open-addressing family, fixes the candidate locations to two hashes and allows relocation
e.linear-probing>hopscotch-hashing: The paper's abstract says the hopscotch technique has the flavors of chaining, cuckoo hashing and linear probing; linear probing is one of them.
e.linear-probing>quadratic-probing: An open-addressing variant that probes at quadratic instead of fixed offsets to reduce the primary clustering of linear probing.
e.linear-probing>quotient-filter: The quotient filter builds on Cleary's compact hash table, which places remainders by linear probing.
e.linear-probing>robin-hood-hashing: Celis et al. presented it as an insertion rule that reduces the variance of probe lengths in open addressing
e.link-cut-tree>euler-tour-tree: The Euler tour tree tackles the same dynamic-tree problem as the link-cut tree with a different representation, without evidence of direct derivation.
e.link-cut-tree>top-tree: Top trees were devised to support the same operations as Sleator–Tarjan dynamic trees while also handling non-local queries.
e.ll-parsing>all-star: ALL(*) is LL parsing whose fixed k-token lookahead is widened to as much lookahead as needed, decided dynamically.
e.locally-linear-embedding>laplacian-eig: The Laplacian eigenmaps paper discusses how LLE is approximately connected to the graph-Laplacian eigenproblem.
e.logistic-regression>conditional-random: A linear-chain CRF can be viewed as a discriminative model extending logistic regression (maximum-entropy models) to sequence labeling.
e.loglog>hyperloglog: Described as combining LogLog registers with a harmonic mean to reduce error
e.lora>qlora: QLoRA trains LoRA adapters on top of a 4-bit quantized base model
e.louvain>leiden: The paper shows that Louvain can yield internally disconnected communities and presents Leiden to fix this.
e.lpa-star>d-star-lite: The paper states that it presents D* Lite by building on LPA*.
e.lpc>opus: The SILK layer of Opus is a speech coding layer based on linear prediction
e.lr-parsing>glr: GLR generalizes LR parsing by handling conflicts in the LR table in parallel with a graph-structured stack.
e.lr-parsing>lalr: Presents a way to reduce Knuth's LR(k) parsers to a practical size
e.lr-parsing>ll-parsing: LL(k) was defined as the top-down deterministic counterpart of LR(k).
e.lr-parsing>slr-parsing: DeRemer defined SLR(k) as a subclass of Knuth's LR(k) grammars with a simple construction.
e.lru-k>lirs: Like LRU-2, LIRS uses the interval between a block's last two references (inter-reference recency) as its replacement criterion
e.lru-k>two-queue-replacement: The 2Q paper presents 2Q as an algorithm that performs close to LRU-2 with low, constant-time overhead
e.lsh>p-stable-lsh: As its title says, the paper presents a locality-sensitive hashing scheme based on p-stable distributions.
e.lsh>simhash: Charikar presents the hash derived from random-hyperplane rounding as a locality-sensitive hashing scheme.
e.lstm>ctc: The CTC paper applies CTC to the outputs of a bidirectional LSTM network in its experiments
e.lstm>glu: The gating mechanism of GLU draws on the multiplicative gates of LSTMs, which the paper discusses
e.lstm>gru: Proposes a simpler gated unit motivated by the LSTM
e.lstm>highway-network: The paper states that the gating of highway networks is inspired by LSTM recurrent networks
e.lstm>seq2seq: Sutskever et al. use multilayer LSTMs for the encoder and decoder
e.lt-code>raptor-code: Raptor codes are defined as a precode concatenated with an LT code.
e.lucas-kanade>farneback-optical-flow: Both estimate optical flow between two frames; Farnebäck's method computes dense flow
e.lucas-kanade>shi-tomasi: Shi–Tomasi selects features at points where the linear system of a Lucas–Kanade-style feature tracker is well conditioned
e.lucifer>des: Standardized as a modification of IBM's Lucifer
e.lz77>brotli: RFC 7932 defines it as a combination of LZ77, Huffman coding, and second-order context modeling
e.lz77>deflate: RFC 1951 defines Deflate as a combination of LZ77 and Huffman coding
e.lz77>lz4: Byte-oriented LZ77-family format with no entropy stage
e.lz77>lzma: Range-codes the output of LZ77-style match finding
e.lz77>lzp: It keeps LZ77's match-copy structure but predicts the match position from a context hash, removing the transmitted offset
e.lz77>lzrw1: As its title states, it is a fast Ziv–Lempel (LZ77-family) compression algorithm
e.lz77>lzss: LZ77 improvement that emits short matches as literals
e.lz77>snappy: The Snappy format description states that Snappy is an LZ77-type compressor
e.lz77>zstd: RFC 8878 defines LZ77-style sequences and FSE/Huffman entropy stages
e.lz78>lzmw: As the title 'Variations on a theme by Ziv and Lempel' indicates, it is a variant of Ziv–Lempel dictionary compression
e.lz78>lzw: Initializes the dictionary with all single characters, eliminating LZ78's literal output
e.lzw>lzmw: It keeps an LZW-like dictionary structure and changes only the rule for creating new entries to the concatenation of two matches
e.manacher>eertree: Addresses the same problem of processing palindromic substrings, and the paper mentions Manacher's algorithm as prior work.
e.mapreduce>rdd: The RDD paper presents RDDs as a more general abstraction able to express existing dataflow models such as MapReduce
e.marching-cubes>dual-contouring: Turns grid-cell-based isosurface extraction into a dual scheme with one vertex per cell, preserving sharp features
e.marching-cubes>poisson-surface-reconst: Extracts the isosurface from the computed indicator function in the manner of marching cubes
e.mark-sweep>boehm-gc: The Boehm–Weiser collector is a mark-sweep collector that identifies pointers conservatively without type information
e.mark-sweep>copying-gc: Tracing GC that reclaims by copying instead of sweeping
e.mark-sweep>immix: The Immix paper presents Immix as a mark-region collector combining the space efficiency of mark-sweep with the fast allocation of copying collection
e.mark-sweep>tri-color-marking: Presents a way to run the marking phase concurrently with the mutator
e.marr-hildreth>canny-edge-detector: The Canny detector was designed from optimality criteria for the same edge-detection problem after Marr–Hildreth
e.matula-beck>batagelj-zaversnik-cores: It computes core numbers with the same structure of repeatedly removing minimum-degree vertices from buckets.
e.matula-beck>eppstein-loffler-strash: It uses the smallest-last (degeneracy) ordering as the vertex order of its outer loop.
e.mccreight-algorithm>ukkonen-algorithm: Giegerich and Kurtz (1997) showed the two constructions share the same suffix-link principle, but neither derives from the other
e.mcs-lock>clh-lock: The CLH lock is a queue-based FIFO spin lock like the MCS lock, varied so that each waiter watches its predecessor's flag instead of its own node
e.mcts>alphazero: AlphaZero selects moves with Monte Carlo tree search guided by the policy and value outputs of a neural network.
e.mcts>uct: Monte Carlo tree search methods published independently in the same year
e.md4>md5: RFC 1321 describes MD5 as an extension of MD4
e.md4>ripemd-160: RIPEMD was designed from MD4, and RIPEMD-160 is presented as its strengthened version
e.md4>sha-1: Follows the same design principles as MD4 (Handbook of Applied Cryptography §9.4)
e.mdct>celt: CELT is an MDCT-based codec that codes the per-band energy and the shape of MDCT coefficients separately
e.median-cut>octree-quantization: Both are palette color quantization methods; octree quantization was proposed after median cut
e.megiddo-lp>seidel-lp: Both solve fixed-dimensional linear programming in time linear in the number of constraints; Seidel's method uses a randomized incremental approach instead of deterministic prune and search.
e.meissel-lehmer>lmo-prime-counting: The paper by Lagarias, Miller and Odlyzko, as its title says, computes π(x) faster by the Meissel–Lehmer method
e.merge-sort>block-sort: Structurally it is a merge sort whose extra memory is reduced to O(1) by stable in-place merging.
e.merge-sort>merge-path: It splits the merge step of merge sort evenly so that several processors can perform it in parallel.
e.merge-sort>odd-even-merge-sort: Carries the recursive structure of merge sort over to a fixed comparator network
e.merge-sort>polyphase-merge-sort: It is a variant of tape-based external merge sort that changes how runs are distributed in order to save merge passes.
e.merge-sort>symmerge: It is a merging algorithm that performs the merge step of merge sort stably without a separate buffer.
e.merge-sort>timsort: listsort.txt describes run-based merging and galloping merges as its core
e.merkle-damgard>md4: Iterated hash structure that chains a compression function over each block (Handbook of Applied Cryptography §9.4)
e.merkle-damgard>sha-2: Uses a Davies–Meyer compression function within the Merkle–Damgård construction
e.merkle-damgard>tiger-hash: Applies its compression function in the Merkle–Damgård iterated structure
e.merkle-signature>sphincs: Stacks Merkle trees into a multi-layer hypertree to obtain a stateless signature
e.merkle-signature>xmss: As its name (eXtended Merkle Signature Scheme) says, it extends the Merkle signature scheme
e.merkle-tree>blake3: The BLAKE3 specification states that input is hashed as a binary Merkle tree of chunks
e.merkle-tree>merkle-signature: Authenticates many one-time public keys under a single root value with a hash tree
e.merkle-tree>nakamoto-consensus: The Bitcoin paper hashes a block's transactions in a Merkle tree so that old transactions can be discarded without breaking the block hash
e.mersenne-twister>sfmt: The SFMT paper presents a variant of the Mersenne Twister redesigned for SIMD instructions
e.mersenne-twister>well-rng: The WELL paper presents generators in the same GF(2)-linear family as the Mersenne Twister with improved equidistribution
e.metaphone>double-metaphone: Published by the same author as an extension of Metaphone that outputs a primary and an alternate code.
e.metropolis-hastings>adaptive-metropoli: Haario et al. present a variant of random-walk Metropolis whose proposal covariance keeps adapting to the sample path
e.metropolis-hastings>affine-invariant-e: The stretch move builds proposals relative to other walkers and accepts them with a Metropolis–Hastings-type acceptance probability
e.metropolis-hastings>gibbs-sampling: Can be interpreted as a special case of MH with acceptance probability 1, but was proposed independently
e.metropolis-hastings>reversible-jump-mc: Green's paper generalizes the Metropolis–Hastings method to model spaces of varying dimension
e.metropolis>hmc: Hybrid Monte Carlo combines proposals generated by molecular-dynamics trajectories with a Metropolis acceptance step
e.metropolis>metropolis-hastings: Generalizes the Metropolis method to asymmetric proposal distributions
e.metropolis>metropolis-light-transport: The paper applies the Metropolis sampling algorithm to the space of light paths
e.metropolis>parallel-tempering: Parallel tempering runs several Metropolis chains at different temperatures and also accepts state swaps between chains by a Metropolis criterion
e.metropolis>simulated-annealing: Presented as the Metropolis algorithm with an added temperature schedule
e.metropolis>swendsen-wang: The Swendsen–Wang algorithm reduces critical slowing down by flipping whole bonded clusters instead of single-spin Metropolis updates
e.metropolis>wang-landau: The Wang–Landau method walks in energy space with Metropolis-type updates whose acceptance probability is the ratio of density-of-states estimates
e.miller-rabin>baillie-psw: The BPSW test combines a base-2 strong probable-prime test (one Miller–Rabin round) with a strong Lucas test
e.miller-rabin>solovay-strassen: Both are probabilistic primality tests that look for witnesses of compositeness with random bases; no derivation is stated
e.minhash>simhash: Carries MinHash's idea of a hash whose collision probability equals similarity over to cosine similarity.
e.minimax>alpha-beta: Yields the same value as minimax while pruning unnecessary branches (analysis by Knuth and Moore, 1975)
e.minimax>expectiminimax: Expectiminimax is described as a generalization of minimax that adds chance nodes taking expected values
e.minimax>mcts: Approaches the same game tree search problem through sampling
e.minimizer>minimap2: Builds a minimizer index of the reference and uses minimizers as seeds.
e.misra-gries>lossy-counting: A different method for the same streaming frequent-items problem with an εN error guarantee.
e.misra-gries>space-saving: Both are counter-based algorithms that track frequent items with a fixed number of counters.
e.mixture-of-experts>sparsely-gated-moe: The paper extends the mixture of experts with sparse gating into a layer with thousands of experts
e.mlaa>fxaa: Both are post-process anti-aliasing methods that find and blend edges in the final image
e.mlaa>smaa: SMAA was presented as an enhancement and extension of morphological antialiasing (MLAA)
e.mobilenet>efficientnet: EfficientNet-B0 is built from MBConv blocks, depthwise-convolution blocks from the MobileNet family
e.momentum>adam: The first-moment moving average plays the same role as the momentum term
e.momentum>nesterov: Accelerated variant that evaluates the gradient at the point reached after the momentum step
e.monotone-polygon-triangulation>hertel-: The Hertel–Mehlhorn algorithm takes a triangulation as input and removes diagonals to form a convex partition, so a triangulation algorithm serves as its first stage.
e.monotone-polygon-triangulation>seidel-: Seidel's algorithm splits the polygon into monotone pieces via the trapezoidal decomposition and then completes the triangulation with a monotone-polygon triangulation step.
e.monte-carlo>gillespie-algorithm: The Gillespie algorithm is a Monte Carlo simulation procedure that samples reaction times and reaction types with random numbers
e.monte-carlo>importance-sampling: Kahn and Marshall treat importance sampling as a way to reduce the sample size needed in Monte Carlo computations
e.monte-carlo>latin-hypercube: McKay et al. propose Latin hypercube sampling for choosing computer-code inputs, comparing it with simple random sampling and stratified sampling
e.monte-carlo>mcts: Estimates node values as Monte Carlo averages over random playouts
e.monte-carlo>metropolis: Extends random sampling to Markov chains (Metropolis is a shared author)
e.monte-carlo>multiple-importance-sampli: Reduces the variance of Monte Carlo integration by combining several sampling techniques with weights
e.monte-carlo>path-tracing: Computes the rendering equation via Monte Carlo integration over random path samples
e.montgomery-multiplication>barrett-redu: Both perform modular reduction with multiplications and shifts instead of hardware division; no derivation is stated
e.moore-minimization>hopcroft-minimizati: Described as an improvement of the same state-partition refinement that uses only smaller blocks as splitters, reducing quadratic time to n log n.
e.mosse-tracker>kcf-tracker: KCF generalizes correlation-filter trackers such as MOSSE with kernel ridge regression and multi-channel features
e.move-to-front>bzip2: Applies the MTF transform to the BWT output
e.multi-query-attention>grouped-query-at: Defined as a generalization of multi-query attention
e.multiple-importance-sampling>restir: The paper presents balance-heuristic (MIS) weights over the candidate PDFs as a way to combine reservoirs without bias
e.murmurhash>cityhash: The CityHash documentation says it was designed relying heavily on previous work by Austin Appleby and others, and that CityHash32 has many similarities with Murmur3a.
e.murmurhash>xxhash: A fast non-cryptographic hash function of the same kind that mixes input with multiplications and rotations.
e.mvcc>snapshot-isolation: Berenson et al. defined snapshot isolation as an isolation level based on multiversion data
e.myers-diff>wavefront-alignment: Widens to gap-affine scores the O(ND) structure of extending only the furthest-reaching point on each diagonal.
e.needham-schroeder>kerberos: The Kerberos paper states that it is based on the Needham–Schroeder protocol
e.needleman-wunsch>gotoh: Structurally the global sequence alignment dynamic program computed in quadratic time with three matrices under affine gap scores.
e.needleman-wunsch>smith-waterman: Modifies global-alignment dynamic programming for local alignment
e.needleman-wunsch>wagner-fischer: The same form of dynamic programming was published independently in biology and in computer science
e.neocognitron>lenet: Papers in the convolutional neural network line cite the neocognitron as prior work
e.nerf>gaussian-splatting: Solves the same radiance-field novel view synthesis problem with explicit Gaussians instead of a neural network
e.nerf>instant-ngp: Greatly accelerated the training and rendering of NeRF with a multiresolution hash encoding
e.newton-method>broyden-method: Broyden's paper presents methods that replace the Jacobian in Newton's method with an approximation that is updated.
e.newton-method>dfp: The DFP formula is a quasi-Newton scheme that approximates the inverse Hessian of Newton's method from gradient information only.
e.newton-method>durand-kerner: The Durand–Kerner iteration is obtained by applying the multidimensional Newton method to the system of Vieta's formulas.
e.newton-method>halley-method: Halley's method is described as adding second-derivative information to Newton's method to obtain cubic convergence.
e.newton-method>ndt: NDT iteratively updates the transformation parameters that maximize the normal-distribution score function with Newton's method.
e.newton-method>steffensen-method: Steffensen's method replaces the derivative in Newton's method with a difference of function values while keeping quadratic convergence.
e.nice>realnvp: Real NVP extends the additive coupling layers of NICE to affine coupling layers that include scaling
e.non-local-means>bm3d: BM3D combines the non-local idea of gathering similar blocks within the image with collaborative filtering in a transform domain
e.normalized-cuts>laplacian-eigenmaps: Laplacian eigenmaps use the same graph-Laplacian eigenproblem as normalized cuts, but for embedding.
e.normalized-cuts>njw-spectral-clusterin: The NJW paper builds on the Shi–Malik normalized-cut family of spectral methods to give a multi-way clustering algorithm.
e.nsw>hnsw: The HNSW paper states that it improves on the authors' earlier NSW structure by adding a hierarchy of layers.
e.ntru>falcon-signature: As its name says, designed to work over NTRU lattices
e.oblivious-transfer>yao-garbled-circuit: The evaluator obtains the keys for its inputs via oblivious transfer
e.ocb>xex-mode: As its title says, the XEX construction was introduced while refining the OCB mode
e.odd-even-merge-sort>aks-sorting-networ: For the same sorting-network problem it lowers the depth from O(log^2 n) to O(log n).
e.odd-even-merge-sort>pairwise-sorting-n: It is a differently constructed sorting network with the same size and depth as Batcher's odd-even merge network.
e.operator-precedence-parsing>pratt-pars: Pratt parsing recasts operator-precedence parsing in a top-down recursive-descent framework.
e.optics>local-outlier-factor: LOF defines local density with the reachability-distance notion used by the same research group in OPTICS.
e.ordered-dithering>floyd-steinberg: Both address the dithering problem of rendering continuous-tone images with binary or few-color output
e.package-merge>boundary-package-merge: Presents a method that solves the same length-limited coding problem as package-merge while reducing its space usage
e.packrat-parsing>peg: Ford formalized the recognition-based grammars handled by packrat parsers as the PEG formalism.
e.paeth-predictor>loco-i: Both use a nonlinear predictor that estimates the current pixel from its left, upper and upper-left neighbors
e.pagerank>hits: Link analysis algorithms proposed independently around the same time
e.pagerank>infomap: For directed graphs it computes the flow with a random surfer that teleports as in PageRank.
e.pagerank>simrank: The SimRank paper gives a random-surfer-pairs interpretation that extends the random-surfer model to pairs of vertices.
e.pagerank>topic-sensitive-pagerank: It is a variant of PageRank whose teleportation vector is biased toward individual topics.
e.painters-algorithm>bsp-tree: The BSP tree yields the viewpoint-dependent back-to-front drawing order through tree traversal
e.pairing-heap>rank-pairing-heap: The paper describes the rank-pairing heap as combining the simplicity of pairing heaps with the efficiency of Fibonacci heaps.
e.partial-redundancy-elimination>lazy-co: Lazy code motion refines the partial redundancy elimination of Morel and Renvoise to be computationally optimal with minimal lifetimes.
e.path-tracing>bidirectional-path-tracin: Generalizes camera-side path tracing by combining it with subpaths traced from the light sources
e.path-tracing>photon-mapping: Combines Monte Carlo ray-traced rendering with a photon map traced in advance from the light sources
e.paxos>epaxos: EPaxos was presented as a variant of Paxos that orders commands by their dependencies without a fixed leader
e.paxos>flexible-paxos: Flexible Paxos is a generalization showing that Paxos's two phases only need quorums that intersect each other
e.paxos>raft: Designed as an understandable alternative equivalent to (Multi-)Paxos
e.paxos>zab: The Zab paper explains that Zab addresses the same problem as Paxos but was designed as a separate protocol tailored to primary-backup systems
e.pbft>hotstuff: HotStuff was presented as a protocol that reduces the communication on leader replacement in PBFT-style BFT consensus to linear in the number of nodes
e.pbkdf2>scrypt: Uses PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 in the input and output stages
e.pca>fastica: FastICA usually preprocesses the data by PCA whitening before searching for independent components.
e.pca>kernel-pca: Kernel PCA generalizes PCA to be carried out in a feature space defined by a kernel.
e.pca>obbtree: OBBTree sets the axes of each bounding box to the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix of the vertex distribution, i.e. its principal directions.
e.peano-curve>hilbert-curve: Hilbert's paper takes as its starting point Peano's continuous mapping of a line segment onto a square and presents a new geometric construction.
e.pedersen-commitment>bulletproofs: Hides the value of a range proof in a Pedersen commitment
e.percentage-closer-filtering>pcss: PCSS varies the PCF kernel size according to the penumbra width estimated from the blocker distance
e.perceptron>backpropagation: Solved the problem of training multilayer perceptrons, but is not derived from the perceptron learning rule
e.perceptron>svm: Addresses the same problem of learning a linearly separating hyperplane
e.perlin-noise>improved-perlin-noise: The same author improves the original noise's interpolation function and gradient selection
e.perlin-noise>simplex-noise: Presented by the same author as a successor noise that replaces the lattice with a simplex lattice
e.perlin-noise>worley-noise: A different kind of noise designed, like Perlin noise, to serve as a basis function for procedural textures
e.perona-malik>total-variation-denoising: Both are edge-preserving denoising methods based on partial differential equations and variational formulations
e.pfordelta>fastpfor: The paper presents FastPFor, which changes how PFor stores exceptions and decodes with SIMD
e.pgz-decoder>berlekamp-massey: The Berlekamp–Massey algorithm replaces the matrix-solving step of PGZ with iterative updates, obtaining the error-locator polynomial more efficiently.
e.philox>threefry: Both are counter-based generators proposed together in the same paper; neither is derived from the other
e.phong-shading>blinn-phong: Blinn presented a variant that recasts the Phong model's specular term in terms of the halfway vector
e.phong-shading>bump-mapping: Bump mapping feeds perturbed normals into shading computations that use interpolated normals
e.phong-shading>deferred-shading: The normal vector shader defers Phong-style per-pixel lighting until after visibility has been resolved
e.pinocchio>groth16: Reduces proof size within the QAP-based pairing SNARK line of Pinocchio
e.plsa>latent-dirichlet-allocation: The LDA paper presents a generative model that adds a Dirichlet prior over per-document topic proportions to pLSI.
e.pollard-p-minus-1>lenstra-ecm: The elliptic-curve method is described as a generalization of the p−1 method that replaces its fixed multiplicative group with randomly chosen elliptic-curve groups
e.pollard-p-minus-1>williams-p-plus-1: Williams presented the counterpart method that uses Lucas sequences in place of the multiplicative group of the p−1 method to handle smooth p+1
e.pollard-rho>pollard-brent: Brent's paper presents an improved version of Pollard's Monte Carlo factorization algorithm
e.pollard-rho>pollard-kangaroo: The kangaroo method also adapts Pollard's Monte Carlo idea of colliding pseudo-random walks, here to discrete logarithms in an interval
e.pollard-rho>pollard-rho-log: The same author applied the pseudo-random walk and collision detection of the rho factoring method to computing discrete logarithms (indices)
e.poly1305>chacha20-poly1305: RFC 7539 defines the AEAD combination of ChaCha20 and Poly1305
e.porter-stemmer>lancaster-stemmer: Addresses the same English stemming problem by rule-based suffix removal, but there is no evidence of derivation.
e.position-based-dynamics>position-based: PBF solves an incompressibility constraint within the constraint-projection framework of position-based dynamics
e.position-based-dynamics>xpbd: XPBD adds compliance and Lagrange multipliers to position-based dynamics so that stiffness becomes independent of the iteration count
e.power-iteration>lanczos-algorithm: The Lanczos method exploits the whole Krylov subspace spanned by the vector sequence that power iteration generates.
e.power-iteration>pagerank: The PageRank vector, the dominant eigenvector of the link matrix, is computed by power iteration.
e.power-iteration>randomized-svd: The Halko–Martinsson–Tropp paper combines power iterations with the randomized range finder to improve accuracy.
e.ppm>lzp: It applies PPM's context-modeling idea of predicting from the preceding context to the prediction of match positions
e.ppm>paq: Mahoney's technical report presents context mixing as an improvement on PPM
e.ppm>ppmd: As the title 'PPM: one step to practicality' indicates, it improves PPM to make it practical
e.prim>stoer-wagner: The maximum-adjacency order in each phase is built, like Prim's algorithm, by repeatedly adding the vertex most strongly connected to the current set.
e.priority-inheritance>priority-ceiling: The same paper extends basic priority inheritance into the priority ceiling protocol, which prevents deadlock and chained blocking
e.progressive-meshes>quadric-error-metri: Performs the same kind of edge-collapse-based simplification quickly using quadric error metrics
e.proof-number-search>mcts: Both are searches that selectively expand game trees in a best-first manner
e.push-relabel>cost-scaling: By the same authors, it applies push–relabel operations in the refinement of ε-optimal flows.
e.q-coder>cabac: Both belong to the family of table-based adaptive binary arithmetic coders that avoid multiplication
e.q-coder>jpeg: The JPEG standard can optionally use adaptive binary arithmetic coding of the Q-Coder family instead of Huffman coding
e.q-learning>double-q-learning: The paper shows that Q-learning overestimates action values and proposes a variant using two estimators.
e.q-learning>dqn: DQN trains a convolutional neural-network value function with Q-learning updates and experience replay.
e.q-learning>sarsa: Rummery and Niranjan presented the method as a modified form of Q-learning.
e.qr-algorithm>cuppen-divide-and-conquer: Both are alternative LAPACK routes for solving the symmetric tridiagonal eigenvalue problem.
e.qr-algorithm>golub-reinsch-svd: The Golub–Reinsch algorithm computes singular values by applying a variant of the QR algorithm to the bidiagonal matrix.
e.qr-algorithm>golub-welsch: The Golub–Welsch algorithm obtains nodes and weights by solving the Jacobi-matrix eigenproblem with QR-type methods.
e.qr-algorithm>implicitly-restarted-arno: The implicit restart is carried out by applying shifted QR iterations implicitly to the Arnoldi factorization.
e.quadratic-probing>swiss-table: Abseil's source describes the Swiss table as an open-addressing hash table with quadratic probing, using a triangular probe sequence over groups.
e.quadratic-sieve>mpqs: Silverman's paper presents the multiple polynomial quadratic sieve as an extension of the quadratic sieve to many polynomials
e.quadratic-sieve>special-number-field-s: The number field sieve extends the sieving, factor-base and linear-algebra structure of the quadratic sieve to an algebraic number field side
e.quadtree>octree: The octree is described as the three-dimensional extension of the quadtree's subdivision scheme.
e.quickselect>floyd-rivest: Like quickselect it narrows the range by partitioning, but it improves the partition with bounds taken from a sample.
e.quickselect>introselect: Musser presents introspective selection, which combines quickselect with a switch to an algorithm that guarantees worst-case time.
e.quickselect>median-of-medians: Replacing pivot selection with the median of medians improves the worst case from O(n²) to O(n) (CLRS §9.3)
e.quicksort>bentley-mcilroy-partitioning: The paper introduces this three-way partition while engineering a quicksort-based qsort.
e.quicksort>blockquicksort: The paper changes quicksort's partitioning step to block-wise processing to remove the effect of branch mispredictions.
e.quicksort>dual-pivot-quicksort: Quicksort with single-pivot partitioning replaced by three-way partitioning around two pivots
e.quicksort>introsort: Musser defined it as starting with quicksort and switching to heapsort once the recursion depth limit is exceeded
e.quicksort>multikey-quicksort: The paper states that its sorting algorithm blends quicksort and radix sort.
e.quicksort>quickhull: Named for a divide-and-conquer structure resembling quicksort, but no evidence of derivation
e.quicksort>quickselect: Published together by the same author in the same issue (CACM 4(7)) as Algorithms 63, 64, and 65, which share the partition procedure
e.quicksort>samplesort: Structurally it generalises quicksort by choosing several splitters from a sample and splitting many ways at once.
e.quicksort>spreadsort: The paper explains that small bins are handled by a comparison sort such as quicksort.
e.quotient-filter>counting-quotient-filt: The same research group extended the quotient filter with variable-length counters and bit-manipulation instructions.
e.r-cnn>fast-rcnn: Fast R-CNN speeds up R-CNN by sharing convolution over the whole image instead of recomputing it per proposal
e.r-tree>gist: The GiST paper treats the R-tree as a special case expressible through its extension methods.
e.r-tree>hilbert-r-tree: The Hilbert R-tree is an R-tree variant that orders entries by Hilbert-curve value.
e.r-tree>m-tree: Like the R-tree, the M-tree keeps covering regions in balanced paged nodes, but it uses only distances instead of coordinates.
e.r-tree>r-star-tree: The R*-tree paper improves the insertion and split algorithms of the R-tree.
e.rabin-karp>bentley-mcilroy: To find long repeated strings, it uses the Karp–Rabin technique of computing rolling-hash fingerprints for blocks
e.rabin-karp>winnowing: Computes k-gram hashes with a Karp–Rabin-style rolling hash and then selects the minimum in each window.
e.rader-fft>winograd-fft: Winograd's algorithm computes prime-length DFTs by converting them into cyclic convolutions in Rader's manner.
e.radiosity>path-tracing: Kajiya's rendering equation paper describes radiosity as a special-case approximation of the rendering equation
e.radix-sort>american-flag-sort: The paper says American flag sort was conceived as a replacement for the existing two-array radix sort library routine.
e.radix-sort>gaussian-splatting: Uses a GPU radix sort to sort Gaussians by keys built from tile and depth
e.radix-sort>multikey-quicksort: The paper states that its sorting algorithm blends radix sort and quicksort.
e.radix-sort>onesweep: The paper presents Onesweep as a faster least-significant-digit radix sort for GPUs.
e.radix-sort>spreadsort: The author describes spreadsort as a hybrid that combines radix-style binning by key value with comparison sorting.
e.ramalingam-reps>lpa-star: The paper states that LPA* combines the incremental approach of DynamicSWSF-FP with A*'s heuristic approach.
e.ramer-douglas-peucker>visvalingam-whya: Both address the same line simplification problem; Visvalingam–Whyatt removes points by effective area rather than by distance.
e.random-forest>extra-trees: Extra-Trees ensemble randomized trees like random forests but also draw the split thresholds at random.
e.random-forest>isolation-forest: Isolation Forest uses an ensemble of randomly split trees to measure the path length needed to isolate a point.
e.random-subspace>random-forest: Cites Ho's random subspace method as prior work
e.range-coding>lzma: Uses context-model-based range coding as the entropy stage
e.rank-select-bitvector>louds: Jacobson implemented tree navigation on the LOUDS bit string with rank and select.
e.rank-select-bitvector>wavelet-tree: Each node of a wavelet tree consists of a bit vector supporting rank and select.
e.rate-monotonic-scheduling>earliest-dea: The same paper analyzes both the fixed-priority rate-monotonic scheme and the dynamic-priority deadline-driven scheme
e.rate-monotonic-scheduling>priority-inh: The schedulability analysis of the priority inheritance protocols is carried out under rate-monotonic priority assignment
e.ray-casting>bvh: A hierarchical acceleration structure for reducing the number of ray–object intersection tests
e.ray-casting>moller-trumbore: Computes ray–triangle intersection, a core operation of ray casting, quickly and without extra storage
e.ray-casting>sphere-tracing: Performs ray casting against implicit surfaces by iterative stepping based on a distance function
e.ray-casting>volume-ray-casting: Applies ray casting to sampling and compositing volume data instead of surfaces
e.ray-casting>whitted-ray-tracing: Extends primary ray casting to recursive tracing of reflection, refraction, and shadow rays
e.rc5>rc6: The RC6 specification states that it was designed from RC5 to meet the AES requirements
e.rcu>epoch-based-reclamation: Like RCU's grace periods, EBR frees retired memory only after all threads have passed a certain point
e.readers-writer-lock>rcu: RCU is used in place of readers–writer locking for read-mostly data, letting readers proceed without locks
e.red-black-tree>aa-tree: Andersson presented it as a simplified variant of red-black trees requiring less case analysis
e.red-black-tree>dsst-persistence: The paper applies node copying to red–black trees to obtain persistent balanced search trees.
e.red-black-tree>tango-tree: The tango tree uses red–black trees as the auxiliary trees that store preferred paths.
e.red-black-tree>wavl-tree: The paper describes the WAVL tree as designed to combine the advantages of AVL trees and red–black trees.
e.red>codel: CoDel addresses the same active-queue-management problem as RED, using sojourn time instead of queue length.
e.red>ecn: The ECN paper considers RED gateways that mark packets instead of dropping them.
e.red>pie: Like RED, PIE drops packets probabilistically, but sets the probability from queueing delay instead of queue length.
e.reed-solomon>forney-algorithm: The Forney algorithm is the standard step for computing error values in non-binary Reed–Solomon decoding.
e.reference-counting>bacon-rajan-cycle-c: Bacon and Rajan added to reference-counted systems a cycle-collection algorithm that finds cyclic garbage reference counting alone cannot reclaim
e.reference-counting>deferred-reference-: Deutsch and Bobrow reduced the cost of reference counting by deferring updates so that references from the stack are not counted
e.regev-lwe>ml-dsa: Bases its security on Module-LWE, the module-lattice variant of LWE
e.regev-lwe>ml-kem: As its title says, builds a CCA-secure KEM on the LWE problem over module lattices
e.regev-lwe>ring-lwe: As its title says, a variant that moves LWE onto polynomial rings
e.relu>alexnet: AlexNet uses ReLUs as its nonlinearity, following Nair and Hinton
e.relu>gelu: The GELU paper presents GELU as weighting inputs by their value rather than gating them by their sign as ReLU does
e.relu>he-init: He initialization is derived from the variance-preserving condition for ReLU and PReLU networks
e.reservoir-sampling>reservoir-sampling-: The paper presents reservoir-sampling algorithms with lower time complexity.
e.reservoir-sampling>weighted-reservoir-: The paper generalizes one-pass reservoir sampling to weighted random sampling.
e.resnet>densenet: DenseNet extends the shortcut connections of ResNet to connections from all preceding layers
e.resnet>simclr: SimCLR uses a ResNet as its base encoder
e.resnet>transformer: Uses a residual connection around each sub-layer, citing He et al.
e.ricart-agrawala>maekawa-algorithm: Maekawa's algorithm reduces the Ricart–Agrawala requirement of permission from all nodes to permission from a quorum of size √N
e.richardson-extrapolation>romberg: Romberg integration is the repeated application of Richardson extrapolation to trapezoidal-rule values.
e.ridge-regression>elastic-net: The paper defines the elastic net as a regularization combining the ridge L2 penalty with the lasso L1 penalty.
e.ridge-regression>lasso: The lasso has the form of ridge regression with the L2 penalty replaced by an L1 penalty.
e.ring-lwe>bgv: Its Ring-LWE version reduces ciphertext size and computation
e.ring-lwe>ckks: Defines approximate arithmetic on the Ring-LWE ciphertext structure
e.ring-lwe>ml-kem: Uses Module-LWE, which generalizes Ring-LWE to a module structure
e.rip>bgp: BGP's path-vector approach is a variant of distance-vector exchange that attaches the AS path to prevent loops.
e.rlhf>dpo: DPO replaces the reward-model fitting and reinforcement-learning stages of RLHF with a single classification loss
e.rmsprop>adam: The Adam paper states that it combines the advantages of AdaGrad and RMSProp
e.rsa>blind-signature: Uses the multiplicative property of RSA signatures to blind and unblind the message
e.rsa>oaep: Designed as padding applied to the plaintext before a trapdoor permutation such as RSA
e.rsa>rsa-pss: As its title says, presents an improved way to sign with RSA
e.runge-kutta-fehlberg>dormand-prince: The Dormand–Prince pair follows Fehlberg's embedded error-estimation structure while advancing with the higher-order solution.
e.runge-kutta>bogacki-shampine: As its title states, the paper presents a 3(2) pair of Runge–Kutta formulas.
e.runge-kutta>dormand-prince: The Dormand–Prince paper derives a family of embedded Runge–Kutta formulae.
e.runge-kutta>rosenbrock-method: Rosenbrock methods insert the Jacobian into a Runge–Kutta-type stage structure to make it linearly implicit.
e.runge-kutta>runge-kutta-fehlberg: Fehlberg's report presents low-order Runge–Kutta formulas with step-size control.
e.rvo>orca: The ORCA paper reformulates the same authors' reciprocal velocity obstacle concept with half-plane constraints and linear programming
e.s4>mamba: Mamba adds an input-dependent selection mechanism to structured state space models such as S4
e.salsa20>chacha: The ChaCha document is titled "a variant of Salsa20"
e.salsa20>scrypt: Uses the Salsa20/8 core in BlockMix
e.samplesort>super-scalar-samplesort: The paper presents it as a refinement of samplesort tailored to the superscalar features of a single processor.
e.sbb-tree>red-black-tree: The dichromatic framework reformulates symmetric binary B-trees in terms of color rules
e.scanline-rendering>edge-function-raste: Solves the same polygon rasterization problem by parallel evaluation of edge functions instead of scanline traversal
e.scanline-rendering>z-buffer: Both address hidden-surface removal on raster displays, but the Z-buffer uses per-pixel depth comparison instead of span sorting
e.schieber-vishkin-lca>bender-farach-col: The paper points out the complexity of the Harel–Tarjan and Schieber–Vishkin methods and offers a simpler alternative.
e.schnorr-signature>dsa: Structural similarity led to a patent dispute, but no official statement of derivation
e.schnorr-signature>eddsa: Describes EdDSA as a variant of Schnorr signatures
e.schonhage-strassen>furer: States that it improves on the Schönhage–Strassen bound
e.segment-tree>fenwick-tree: Both structures serve range queries such as prefix or range sums over arrays, but there is no evidence that the Fenwick tree was derived from the segment tree.
e.seidel-lp>welzl: Welzl states that his smallest-enclosing-disk algorithm is based on Seidel's randomized linear programming algorithm.
e.sellers-algorithm>myers-bit-vector: As its title says, a method computing the dynamic programming matrix of approximate string matching with bit vectors.
e.sellers-algorithm>ukkonen-cutoff: Described as an improvement of the classical dynamic program for approximate string search that computes only the necessary cells.
e.semaphore>readers-writer-lock: Courtois, Heymans and Parnas built their readers–writers solutions from Dijkstra's semaphores (P and V operations)
e.seq2seq>additive-attention: Identifies the fixed-length vector bottleneck and extends the encoder–decoder to learn alignment
e.sequitur>re-pair: Both are grammar-based compression methods that build a grammar by replacing repeated symbol pairs with rules
e.serpent>present-cipher: Simplifies an SPN with 4-bit S-boxes, as in Serpent, for hardware
e.sgd>adagrad: Introduces per-coordinate adaptive learning rates into stochastic (sub)gradient updates
e.sgd>bpr: LearnBPR is stochastic gradient descent combined with bootstrap sampling.
e.sgd>funk-svd: Funk describes learning the user and item factors by incremental gradient descent on the known ratings.
e.sgd>mini-batch-k-means: Mini-batch k-means updates centers in the form of stochastic gradient descent with per-center learning rates.
e.sgd>sgdr: SGDR adds periodic warm restarts of the learning rate to stochastic gradient descent
e.sha-1>sha-2: Extends the word size and round functions within the same FIPS 180 family
e.sha-3>kangarootwelve: As its title says, presented as a hash using the Keccak-p permutation reduced to 12 rounds
e.shadow-mapping>percentage-closer-filte: The paper reduces aliasing in depth-map shadows by filtering the results of depth comparisons
e.shadow-mapping>variance-shadow-maps: Stores moments of depth instead of depth so that the shadow map can be prefiltered
e.shadow-volumes>shadow-mapping: Solves the same shadow determination problem with a depth map from the light's viewpoint instead of geometric volumes
e.shamir-secret-sharing>feldman-vss: Makes shares verifiable by attaching commitments to the coefficients of the Shamir polynomial
e.shamos-hoey>bentley-ottmann: Standard computational geometry textbooks describe the Bentley–Ottmann intersection-reporting algorithm as an extension of the Shamos–Hoey plane sweep for intersection detection.
e.shannon-fano>huffman: Optimal prefix code that originated as an assignment in Fano's course and resolved the suboptimality of Shannon–Fano coding
e.shellsort>comb-sort: Structurally it applies Shellsort's idea of comparing elements a shrinking gap apart to an exchange sort.
e.shift-or>bndm: Presented, as the title indicates, as combining bit parallelism with suffix-automaton-based search.
e.shift-or>wu-manber-agrep: Extends the Baeza-Yates–Gonnet Shift-Or bit vector with one vector per error count to perform approximate search.
e.shunting-yard>operator-precedence-pars: Both analyze expressions by operator precedence, and the shunting-yard algorithm was published first.
e.sieve-of-eratosthenes>linear-sieve: Presented as a linear-time sieve that crosses out each composite only once
e.sieve-of-eratosthenes>segmented-sieve: The paper by Bays and Hudson, as its title says, treats the sieve of Eratosthenes performed segment by segment
e.sieve-of-eratosthenes>sieve-of-atkin: Compared with the sieve of Eratosthenes, but uses a different principle based on quadratic forms
e.sift>hog: The HOG paper explains that its descriptor resembles orientation histograms such as SIFT descriptors but is computed on a dense grid
e.sift>surf: The SURF paper presents a faster way to compute SIFT-like scale-invariant detection and description by approximating them with integral images and box filters
e.sigma-key-exchange>tls-1-3-handshake: Follows a SIGMA-style authentication structure in which the server signs the Diffie–Hellman transcript and adds a Finished MAC
e.simple-9>simple-8b: The same authors extended the word-aligned scheme of Simple-9 to 64-bit words
e.simplex>branch-and-bound: The Land–Doig method obtains bounds by solving linear programming relaxations at each branch.
e.simplex>frank-wolfe: The Frank–Wolfe algorithm determines its direction by solving a linear programming subproblem at each iteration.
e.simplex>karmarkar: A separate method that solves the same linear programming problem by an interior-point approach
e.simulated-annealing>boltzmann-machine: The Boltzmann machine paper uses simulated annealing to reach thermal equilibrium
e.siv>gcm-siv: Follows the SIV paradigm for nonce-misuse resistance
e.skip-list>hnsw: The HNSW paper describes the structure as an extension of the probabilistic skip list with proximity graphs in place of linked lists.
e.skip-list>zip-tree: The paper describes the zip tree as a binary-search-tree representation of a skip list.
e.slink>hdbscan: The HDBSCAN hierarchy is built in the same way as single-linkage clustering over the mutual reachability distance.
e.smith-waterman>blast: Approximates local alignment with a word-seed extension heuristic to gain speed
e.smith-waterman>striped-smith-waterman: As its title says, accelerates Smith–Waterman alignment with a striped SIMD layout.
e.smo>one-class-svm: The one-class SVM paper trains the model with a modified version of SMO.
e.snapshot-isolation>percolator: The Percolator paper states that it provides cross-row, cross-table transactions with snapshot-isolation semantics
e.snapshot-isolation>serializable-snapsh: Cahill et al. modified snapshot isolation by adding detection of dangerous antidependency structures so that it guarantees serializability
e.soundex>metaphone: Described as a phonetic code improving on Soundex by reflecting English pronunciation rules in more detail.
e.sparsely-gated-moe>switch-transformer: Switch Transformer simplifies the top-k routing of the sparsely-gated MoE to top-1
e.special-number-field-sieve>general-num: The paper by Buhler, Lenstra and Pomerance extends the number field sieve from special-form integers to general integers
e.sph>position-based-fluids: PBF formulates its incompressibility constraint with SPH density estimation
e.splay-tree>pairing-heap: Same group of authors (Sleator, Tarjan) applies self-adjusting amortized analysis to heaps
e.splay-tree>tango-tree: The tango tree is a binary search tree aimed at the dynamic optimality conjecture posed for splay trees.
e.spline-interpolation>de-boor-algorithm: The papers by de Boor and Cox give recurrences for stably computing the B-splines introduced by Schoenberg.
e.sponge-construction>ascon: Builds authenticated encryption on the duplex mode of the sponge construction
e.sponge-construction>sha-3: Defines Keccak as a sponge function over the Keccak-f permutation
e.square-cipher>aes: The Rijndael proposal states that it is a successor design to Square
e.srp>opaque: Addresses the same asymmetric PAKE problem as SRP, adding resistance to pre-computation attacks
e.ssa-form>braun-ssa: Braun et al. presented a simpler construction that builds SSA form directly without dominance information.
e.ssa-form>cytron-ssa: Cytron et al., from the same group that proposed SSA form, presented an efficient way to compute it.
e.ssa-form>sccp: The sparse conditional constant propagation of the TOPLAS version operates on SSA form.
e.station-to-station>sigma-key-exchange: The SIGMA paper analyzes the shortcomings of STS and proposes an alternative combining signatures and MACs
e.strassen-mm>coppersmith-winograd: A later result in the line of work, following Strassen, that lowers the matrix multiplication exponent
e.subset-construction>thompson-construct: Searching while tracking a whole set of NFA states at once has the same structure as performing the subset construction on the fly.
e.subtract-with-borrow>ranlux: Lüscher's RANLUX is the Marsaglia–Zaman subtract-with-borrow generator with part of its output discarded to reduce correlations
e.suffix-array>dc3: As its title says, presents a simple method for constructing suffix arrays with linear work.
e.suffix-array>fm-index: The BWT column is defined by suffix array order, and locate queries use a sampled suffix array
e.suffix-array>kasai-lcp: As its title says, performs longest-common-prefix computation for suffix arrays in linear time.
e.suffix-array>sa-is: Presented as an algorithm for constructing suffix arrays in linear time.
e.suffix-automaton>bndm: Presented as a variant that simulates the pattern's suffix automaton with bit parallelism instead of determinizing it.
e.suffix-tree>mccreight-algorithm: Presented as a more space-efficient suffix tree construction than Weiner's
e.suffix-tree>suffix-array: Manber and Myers presented it as an alternative that uses less space than suffix trees
e.suffix-tree>suffix-automaton: Support the same substring queries and correspond to each other, but no evidence of derivation
e.suffix-tree>ukkonen-algorithm: Presented as an online, left-to-right construction of suffix trees
e.super-scalar-samplesort>ips4o: The IPS4o paper states in its title that it is an in-place parallel version of Super Scalar Samplesort.
e.sutherland-hodgman>weiler-atherton: Weiler–Atherton clipping extends reentrant polygon clipping, which handles only convex clip regions, to concave and holed clip polygons.
e.svd-plus-plus>factorization-machines: The FM paper shows that, by choosing the input features, FMs can mimic models such as matrix factorization and SVD++.
e.svm>factorization-machines: Rendle introduces FMs as a model that combines the generality of SVMs with the advantages of factorization models.
e.svm>kernel-pca: The kernel PCA paper applies the kernel trick used in support vector machines to principal component analysis.
e.svm>one-class-svm: The one-class SVM applies the SVM maximum-margin approach to estimating the support of unlabeled data.
e.svm>smo: SMO solves the SVM dual quadratic program analytically by splitting it into two-variable subproblems.
e.svm>soft-margin-svm: Extends the optimal margin classifier to the non-separable case
e.swendsen-wang>wolff-algorithm: Wolff's paper turns the Swendsen–Wang cluster update into a single-cluster update grown from one seed
e.t-sne>barnes-hut-t-sne: The same author reduced t-SNE's gradient computation to O(N log N) with a Barnes–Hut approximation.
e.t-sne>umap: UMAP shares t-SNE's structure of optimizing an embedding from a neighbor graph, and the paper compares it directly with t-SNE.
e.t5>switch-transformer: Switch Transformer builds on T5 models, replacing their feed-forward layers with expert layers
e.tarjan-bridges>chain-decomposition: Both methods find the bridges of an undirected graph in linear time.
e.tarjan-scc>gabow-scc: It solves the same problem as Tarjan's algorithm in the same linear time but uses a stack of path boundaries instead of lowlink values.
e.tcp-newreno>prr: PRR is a replacement for the fast-recovery step that improves how the congestion window is reduced during loss recovery.
e.tcp-slow-start>bic-tcp: BIC replaces the linear congestion-avoidance growth of standard TCP with binary-search growth.
e.tcp-slow-start>hystart: HyStart is proposed as a new slow start replacing the standard slow-start algorithm.
e.tcp-slow-start>tcp-newreno: NewReno keeps the slow-start/congestion-avoidance framework and only changes how fast recovery handles partial ACKs.
e.tcp-slow-start>tcp-vegas: Vegas reworks the slow start and congestion avoidance of the existing TCP around delay measurements.
e.tcp-vegas>bbr: Both judge congestion from RTT measurements rather than from loss.
e.td-lambda>gae: GAE estimates the advantage as a λ-weighted sum of temporal-difference residuals, analogous to TD(λ).
e.td-lambda>q-learning: Q-learning applies temporal-difference learning to off-policy updates of the action-value function.
e.telea-inpainting>criminisi-inpainting: Both are inpainting methods for restoring damaged or removed regions, published in 2004
e.tiernan-cycles>johnson-cycles: Johnson gave a better time bound than earlier circuit-enumeration algorithms such as Tiernan's.
e.timsort>powersort: CPython's listsort.txt records that Timsort's merge-ordering strategy was replaced by the powersort strategy of Munro and Wild.
e.tomita-pivot>eppstein-loffler-strash: The outer loop follows a degeneracy ordering and the inner recursion uses Tomita-style pivoting Bron–Kerbosch.
e.tonelli-shanks>cipolla: Both compute square roots modulo a prime; no derivation is stated
e.topological-sort>goldberg-radzik: In each pass it scans vertices in a topological order of the admissible-edge graph.
e.tornado-code>lt-code: Luby, a co-author of Tornado codes, presented LT codes as rateless codes that remove the fixed-rate restriction.
e.torrance-sparrow>cook-torrance: The Cook–Torrance model carries the Torrance–Sparrow microfacet reflection theory over into a reflectance model for rendering
e.torrance-sparrow>ggx: Uses a different form of microfacet normal distribution within the same microfacet reflection framework
e.torrance-sparrow>oren-nayar: Applies V-groove microfacet geometry to a diffuse reflectance model
e.transformer>alibi: ALiBi replaces the position embeddings of the Transformer with a distance bias added to attention scores
e.transformer>bert: States that it is a multi-layer bidirectional Transformer encoder
e.transformer>clip: The text encoder of CLIP is a Transformer
e.transformer>flash-attention: Presented as an IO-aware implementation that produces the same results as standard attention
e.transformer>gpt: States that it uses a multi-layer Transformer decoder
e.transformer>lora: Mainly applied to Transformer weights, but not a technique derived from the architecture
e.transformer>multi-query-attention: Proposes a variant of multi-head attention in which the key and value heads are shared as a single head
e.transformer>paged-attention: PagedAttention improves the memory management of the KV cache used in Transformer autoregressive generation
e.transformer>rope: Replaces the Transformer's positional encoding with rotation matrices
e.transformer>sparse-transformer: The Sparse Transformer reduces cost by replacing the full attention of the Transformer with sparse factorizations
e.transformer>speculative-decoding: Speculative decoding is proposed to accelerate inference of large autoregressive models such as Transformers
e.transformer>swiglu: SwiGLU is presented as a replacement for the Transformer feed-forward sublayer
e.transformer>t5: T5 uses the original Transformer encoder–decoder architecture with only minor changes
e.transformer>vit: ViT applies a standard Transformer encoder to sequences of image patches with minimal modification
e.treap>randomized-bst: Randomized binary search trees belong to the same family of randomized balanced trees as treaps but use subtree sizes instead of priorities.
e.treap>zip-tree: The paper states that a zip tree has the same shape as a treap whose priorities are geometrically distributed ranks.
e.tri-color-marking>yuasa-snapshot-barri: Yuasa's write barrier is a variant of preserving the tri-color invariant during incremental marking, based on the value before overwriting
e.trie>adaptive-radix-tree: ART adaptively changes the node size of a byte-wise radix tree (trie).
e.trie>aho-corasick: Automaton that adds a failure function to the pattern-set trie (goto function)
e.trie>burst-trie: The burst trie is a trie variant that replaces the lower parts of the trie with small containers.
e.trie>double-array-trie: The double array compactly represents a trie's transition table with two arrays.
e.trie>fp-growth: FP-growth compresses frequent items into the FP-tree, a prefix-tree structure.
e.trie>hamt: The HAMT is a trie that branches on bits of the hash value and compresses nodes with bitmaps.
e.trie>masstree: The paper describes Masstree as a trie whose layers are B+-trees.
e.trie>patricia-trie: Trie with single-child paths compressed (Knuth TAOCP Vol.3 §6.3)
e.trie>suffix-tree: Defined as a compressed trie of all suffixes
e.trie>x-fast-trie: The x-fast trie is a binary trie over the bits of integer keys augmented with per-level hash tables.
e.trpo>gae: The GAE paper trains both the policy and the value function with trust-region optimization.
e.trpo>ppo: The PPO paper proposes a clipped objective that obtains the benefits of TRPO's trust region using only first-order optimization.
e.two-opt>lin-kernighan: It generalizes local search with a fixed number of exchanged edges, such as 2-opt, into a variable-depth search that decides the exchange depth each time.
e.two-phase-commit>percolator: Percolator commits via a two-phase commit anchored on a primary lock
e.two-phase-commit>three-phase-commit: Skeen presented three-phase commit as a nonblocking commit protocol that removes the blocking problem of two-phase commit
e.two-phase-locking>optimistic-concurren: Kung and Robinson proposed the validation-based optimistic approach as an alternative to locking
e.two-phase-locking>wait-die: Wait–die is a rule that uses timestamps to prevent deadlocks in advance in lock-based concurrency control
e.two-phase-locking>wound-wait: Wound–wait is a rule that uses timestamps to prevent deadlocks in advance in lock-based concurrency control
e.two-queue-replacement>arc: The ARC paper takes recency/frequency hybrid policies such as 2Q and LRU-2 as baselines and improves on them with a self-tuning scheme without fixed parameters
e.u-net>ddpm: The noise-prediction network of DDPM uses a U-Net backbone
e.ukkonen-cutoff>myers-bit-vector: Skipping lower blocks whose values exceed k in the blocked computation has the same structure as the cut-off technique.
e.ullmann>vf2: Both solve the same subgraph isomorphism problem with backtracking search and pruning.
e.unification>hindley-milner: Milner's Algorithm W solves type constraints with Robinson's unification algorithm.
e.unification>steensgaard-analysis: Steensgaard's analysis computes points-to relations by unifying types at each assignment.
e.union-find>connected-component-labelin: Merging label equivalences in two-pass connected-component labeling is implemented with a disjoint-set structure
e.union-find>felzenszwalb-segmentation: The paper implements region merging with a disjoint-set forest using path compression and union by rank
e.union-find>lengauer-tarjan: The LINK and EVAL operations of Lengauer–Tarjan use the same path-compression technique as union–find.
e.union-find>steensgaard-analysis: Steensgaard's analysis merges equivalence classes with a union–find structure to obtain almost linear time.
e.union-find>tarjan-offline-lca: Tarjan handled offline LCA queries with a union–find structure using path compression.
e.universal-hashing>fks-perfect-hashing: FKS builds its two levels from a randomly chosen hash family of the form (kx mod p) mod s.
e.vae>latent-diffusion: The first-stage autoencoder of latent diffusion includes a variant with VAE-style KL regularization of the latent space
e.van-emde-boas-tree>x-fast-trie: The x-fast trie was proposed to keep the O(log log u) query time of van Emde Boas trees while reducing their space usage.
e.vatti-clipping>greiner-hormann: The Greiner–Hormann paper compares its method with Vatti's algorithm for the same general polygon clipping problem and reports that it is faster.
e.vector-clock>crdt: Operation-based CRDTs assume causal delivery, for which vector clocks (version vectors) are used
e.velocity-obstacle>rvo: The RVO paper states that it extends the velocity obstacle concept by assuming the other agent also takes part in avoidance
e.verlet-integration>velocity-verlet: Swope et al. presented the velocity form of the Verlet algorithm, which handles positions and velocities together.
e.vgg>fcn: FCN converts classification networks such as VGG into fully convolutional form and fine-tunes them for segmentation
e.vgg>resnet: States that the plain baseline network is inspired by the philosophy of VGG
e.viewstamped-replication>paxos: Replicated consensus schemes devised independently around the same time
e.viewstamped-replication>pbft: PBFT's primary-replica and view-change structure has the same shape as Viewstamped Replication by Liskov and colleagues
e.viewstamped-replication>raft: The Raft paper states that, of existing algorithms, it is most similar to Viewstamped Replication
e.vincenty-formulae>karney-geodesic: Karney's paper points out that Vincenty's method fails to converge for nearly antipodal points and presents a solution that converges in all cases.
e.vit>clip: CLIP uses the Vision Transformer, alongside ResNets, as its image encoder
e.viterbi>baum-welch: Both use dynamic programming over the same HMM trellis, but for different purposes
e.viterbi>bcjr: Both run on a trellis, but BCJR maximizes per-symbol posterior probabilities instead of the most likely sequence.
e.viterbi>conditional-random-field: The best label sequence of a linear-chain CRF is found by Viterbi-style dynamic programming.
e.volcano-iterator-model>data-centric-co: Neumann's paper points out the limits of the tuple-at-a-time iterator model and proposes data-centric compilation to replace it
e.volcano-iterator-model>morsel-driven-p: Morsel-driven parallelism was presented as an alternative to Volcano-style plan-driven parallelism through exchange operators
e.volcano-iterator-model>vectorized-quer: X100 replaced the tuple-at-a-time Volcano iterator model with vector-at-a-time processing to reduce interpretation overhead
e.volume-ray-casting>nerf: NeRF computes pixel colors with classical volume rendering that integrates density and color along rays
e.vp-tree>cover-tree: The cover tree addresses the same metric nearest-neighbor problem as the VP-tree, without evidence of direct derivation.
e.wagner-fischer>hirschberg: Structurally computes the same quadratic-time dynamic program in linear space by divide and conquer.
e.wagner-fischer>myers-diff: Finds the shortest edit script on the edit graph in time proportional to the number of differences D
e.wagner-fischer>sellers-algorithm: Structurally the edit-distance dynamic program with only the first-row initialization changed so that it finds approximate occurrences inside a text.
e.wavelet-tree>wavelet-matrix: The paper presents the wavelet matrix as a different arrangement of the wavelet tree suited to large alphabets.
e.wegman-carter-mac>gcm: Authentication in the Wegman–Carter style, masking the GHASH universal-hash value with an encrypted value
e.wegman-carter-mac>poly1305: A Wegman–Carter-style MAC that masks a polynomial universal-hash value with a one-time value
e.wegman-carter-mac>umac: The UMAC paper states that it follows the Wegman–Carter paradigm of universal hashing followed by masking
e.weight-balanced-tree>scapegoat-tree: The scapegoat tree uses a weight-balance condition on subtree size ratios α as its rebuilding criterion.
e.weiler-atherton>greiner-hormann: Both insert intersection points into the boundary lists of the two polygons and build the result by alternately following the boundaries from entering intersections.
e.welsh-powell>dsatur: It is a greedy-colouring variant that picks the next vertex dynamically by saturation instead of a fixed degree order.
e.welsh-powell>matula-beck: It uses the reverse of the minimum-degree removal order, instead of decreasing degree, as the greedy-colouring order.
e.whitted-ray-tracing>distributed-ray-tr: The paper extends conventional ray tracing to fuzzy phenomena by distributing the directions of rays
e.whitted-ray-tracing>path-tracing: Kajiya recast existing ray tracing methods as special approximations of the rendering equation and generalized them
e.winnowing>minimizer: The same idea of choosing the minimum hash per window as a representative was proposed separately for document fingerprinting and for sequence comparison.
e.word2vec>fasttext: fastText extends the skip-gram model with character n-gram subword vectors.
e.word2vec>glove: The GloVe paper states that it combines local context-window methods such as skip-gram with global co-occurrence statistics.
e.wordpiece>bert: BERT uses WordPiece embeddings with a 30,000-token vocabulary
e.wordpiece>bpe-tokenization: Both methods address the same problem of growing a subword vocabulary by frequency or likelihood criteria
e.work-stealing>abp-deque: The ABP paper implements Blumofe and Leiserson's work stealing with a non-blocking deque and extends it to multiprogrammed environments
e.x-fast-trie>y-fast-trie: The same paper reduces space to O(n) with the y-fast trie, which stores only group representatives in an x-fast trie and the rest in balanced trees.
e.x25519>eddsa: Ed25519 uses a twisted Edwards curve birationally equivalent to Curve25519
e.x25519>wireguard: The paper states that Curve25519 is used for key exchange
e.xavier-init>he-init: He initialization extends the variance derivation of Xavier initialization, which assumes linear activations, to rectifiers
e.xex-mode>xts: IEEE 1619 defines XTS as an XEX-based tweaked-codebook mode with ciphertext stealing
e.xor-filter>binary-fuse-filter: The same authors present it as a filter that improves on the space and construction speed of xor filters.
e.xor-filter>ribbon-filter: Addresses the same static approximate membership problem; the paper's title claims it is smaller than Bloom and xor filters.
e.xorshift>xoshiro: Adds a scrambler to the xorshift-family linear engine
e.yarrow>fortuna: A successor design by Yarrow's designers that removes the need for entropy estimation
e.yen-k-shortest-paths>eppstein-k-shorte: Both address the k shortest paths problem, but Eppstein's method handles the case without the simple-path constraint.
e.yuasa-snapshot-barrier>g1-gc: G1 uses a snapshot-at-the-beginning (SATB) write barrier during its concurrent marking phase
e.z-buffer>a-buffer: The paper presents the A-buffer as an anti-aliased hidden-surface method that raises the effective resolution over the Z-buffer
e.z-buffer>shadow-mapping: Uses a depth buffer rendered from the light's viewpoint for shadow tests
e.z-buffer>ssao: SSAO estimates occlusion by surrounding geometry from depth-buffer values alone
e.z-order-curve>geohash: Geohash writes as a base-32 string the Z-order (Morton) encoding obtained by interleaving latitude and longitude bits.
